4XC operates under the 4xCube Ltd entity, which is authorized by the FSC in the Cook Islands. I confirmed that the broker keeps client funds in segregated accounts, but negative balance protection is only partial. I also discovered that 4XC operates on a âbest executionâ basis, where the broker is required to provide optimal price quotes. Overall, I concluded that 4XC is sufficiently transparent and safe.

4XC Regulators

When reviewing a broker, we examine how each of its entities is regulated and assess how effectively they protect clients. We use a three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier-1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about 4XC:

  • 4xCube Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) of the Cook Islands under license number MC03/2018. We rate the FSC as a Tier-3 regulator.

How Does 4XC Protect You?

I reviewed the brokerâs client agreement and other relevant legal documents to examine how 4XC protects its clients. I found that the legal section can be accessed from the âAbout Usâ tab on the 4XC website, under âLegalâ. I also confirmed 4XCâs licensing info from the FSC website.

Here is what I found about 4xCube Ltd:

â Segregated Accounts â Client funds are kept separate from the companyâs own capital.

â ï¸ Negative Balance Protection â Your losses cannot exceed your invested capital only when trading FX pairs and metals. 4XC does not guarantee negative balance protection when trading instruments from other asset classes.

â Compensation Scheme â In the unlikely event of insolvency, you will not be entitled to insurance.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, check our dedicated guide on client protections.

Stability and Transparency

We also assess a brokerâs stability and transparency. This includes how long the company has been in business, its size, and how openly it shares information about its business and services.

I researched 4XCâs background on its website and LinkedIn page. From there, I learned that the company was established in 2018, employs around 30 professionals, and is privately audited by a third-party accounting firm.

I also went over 4XCâs key legal documents, including its client agreement, terms and conditions, execution policy, and risk disclosure.

While there were no glaring issues, I was surprised by 4XCâs unusual negative balance protection policy. As of 14 January 2026, clause 3.12 of the brokerâs client agreement states that the policy applies âONLY to trades of FX (Forex) currency pairs and Metalsâ. This is very unusual for a broker and problematic for traders who use instruments other than FX pairs and metals, as their losses may exceed their account balance.

I appreciated 4XCâs live spreads feed on the website, which helps casual visitors assess the brokerâs fee transparency and competitiveness. However, the displayed spreads are taken from the Pro account, which has lower spreads plus commissions. Consider this if you open a Standard account.

Is 4XC Safe?

Despite some issues with the negative balance protection, I concluded that 4XC is reasonably safe to trade with due to the following factors:

  • Authorized by the FSC of the Cook Islands.
  • Keeps client funds segregated.
  • Provides partial negative balance protection.
  • Required to provide optimal price quotes.
  • Privately audited.

Fees

4XCâs fees depend on the account type and the asset you trade. I found that its Standard account offers very competitive pricing on most instruments, except for Bitcoin and crude oil. Spreads on GBP/JPY and DAX 40 were exceptionally low on both the Standard and Pro accounts. That said, if you mainly trade EUR/USD or gold, the Standard account is generally cheaper.

4XC Swaps

A swap fee is the cost of keeping a trade open overnight, and itâs tied to the difference in interest rates between the two currencies in a pair. If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

4XC Non-Trading Fees

Inactivity Fee: 4XC charges a $30 inactivity fee to dormant accounts after 30 days without placing any orders or performing any other account operations. The fee is charged monthly until account activity resumes or the balance drops to zero. Such a fee is quite high compared to many other brokers, considering that itâs charged after only a month of inactivity.

Platforms and Tools

4XC offers MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5, known for their high functionality. Both platforms are available for web, desktop, and mobile trading. They also support algorithmic trading via Expert Advisors and copy trading. But, in my opinion, MetaTraderâs rugged charts are inferior to newer, sleeker platforms. 4XC also provides free VPS hosting for low-latency trading.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

On January 14, at around 13:00 CET, I placed a standard market order on the DAX 40 index. Given that this is one of the most low-cost assets to trade with 4XC, I wanted to see how the platform handles placing orders for immediate entries. Everything was in order, and I did not experience any slippage or requotes.

While taking down my measurements, I also noticed that 4XC provides two servers. The one I was automatically connected to resulted in a ping of around 60 milliseconds, which is pretty standard for the industry. If you are looking for precise entries, 4XC may be a good option. However, keep in mind that the execution speed may differ depending on your location, internet speed, and other external factors.

A classic setup. I have done my fair share of trading on MetaTrader and have always liked it for its universal design, which was replicated by many newer platforms. You can easily spot your watchlist screen on the left-hand side and your charts screen on the right.

Easily Adaptable. What I like most about MT5 is how well it adapts to different trading styles and experience levels. Itâs suitable for basic technical analysis, placing trading orders, and copy trading. MT5 is also loaded with multiple integrated tutorials, helping users learn how to use the platform.

DoM and EAs. Those interested in algorithmic trading will find the Depth of Market (DOM) tool very useful. The platform also features Expert Advisors (EAs) for automated trading and a strategy tester tool for performance assessment.

Acuity Signal Centre. 4XC also integrates Acuity Signal Centre on MT5, providing a steady stream of AI-generated, actionable trading signals. You can lock into a trade with preconfigured entry parameters with just a few clicks.

Outdated Charting Capabilities. On the downside, I consider MT5âs charts outdated and somewhat rugged compared to those on more modern platforms like cTrader and TradingView.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by 4XC is available for Windows and Mac users and supports 39 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is packed with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format.

Notice, for example, how applying the Ichimoku Kinko â my favourite indicator for spotting large price trends â makes it difficult to discern the price action itself. It is also quite difficult to make out convergences and divergences on the MACD histogram below. Both of these problems are owing to MTâs poor visuals.

Overall, MT5âs charts are not ideal for traders accustomed to streamlined and easily scalable setups.

Order Types

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android devices and offers most of the desktop versionâs functionality. This makes the MT5 app a convenient tool for staying connected to the market and adjusting your positions on the go.

You can place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as manage position size and risk directly from the app. That said, the charting experience still feels a bit cramped, and price action can be hard to scale and analyze comfortably on a small screen.

VPS Hosting

4XC provides Virtual Private Server (VPS) hosting for low-latency trading and a stable internet connection. I recommend this service to algorithmic and high-volume traders seeking fast, precise execution.

The service is free for traders with funded accounts of at least $5,000 who achieve a monthly traded volume of at least 4 lots.

4XC Execution Model

4XC operates as a Straight-Through Processing (STP) broker without a dealing desk. Client orders are routed to the brokerâs pool of liquidity providers, where they are filled at the best possible price.

Tradable Instruments

4XC offers 81 tradable instruments across currency pairs, commodities, indices, and cryptocurrencies. There are over 60 forex pairs, far more than most brokers offer. However, 4XC cannot keep pace with other brokers in terms of asset diversity. Plus, it does not offer any stock CFDs, which can limit some traders.

Customer Support Test

When we test a brokerâs customer support, we evaluate the agentâs knowledge of their own website, the time it takes them to respond to questions, and the level of detail in their answers.

I performed my test on January 15 at approximately 12:00 CET via live chat. I provided my name, email address, and phone number, and was promptly connected to 4XCâs chatbot. First, I asked about the copy trading service and whether the broker charged a servicing fee for it. I also asked about 4XCâs execution model and negative balance protection.

The botâs responses were instant and fairly insightful. However, I noticed some gaps in its knowledge. For example, the chatbot wasnât aware that 4XCâs negative balance protection only applies to trading FX pairs and metals.

Overall, I would recommend using 4XCâs chatbot only for general topics. And if you need more detailed information, itâs better to reach out to 4XCâs agents.

Deposits are free of charge, but withdrawals incur a handling fee, depending on the chosen method. Withdrawal processing times also take a bit longer than usual.

I did not test 4XCâs withdrawal process with real funds.

Account Types and Terms

4XC offers three account types: one spread-based account with no commissions, and two commission-based accounts with raw spreads. You can get started with $50, and there are four base currencies available. I found the onboarding process fast and easy. It took me less than 10 minutes to set up my account and place my first trade.

How to Open an Account With 4XC

To open an account with 4XC, I followed these simple steps:

  1. I clicked âGet Startedâ at the top-right corner of the main page.
  2. I stated my name, date of birth, and country of residence.
  3. I provided my phone number and email address.
  4. I agreed to 4XCâs T&Cs and proceeded with the registration.
  5. I confirmed my email address and received the login credentials.
  6. I confirmed I have read and understood 4XCâs Terms and Conditions.
  7. I provided the rest of my personal details.
  8. I uploaded proof of ID and proof of address to verify my account.
  9. I configured the parameters of my trading account.

The three 4XC accounts differ in pricing, deposit requirements, and target clients. With $50 minimum deposit, the Standard account is the most affordable option. However, I found that it features higher trading costs.

If youâre seeking the lowest pricing, I recommend the VIP account. It features raw spreads and a $4 commission per lot, beating the industry average of $6. The catch is that the VIP account has a steep $10,000 barrier to entry.

I consider the Pro account the most balanced option. While its minimum deposit is only $100, my hands-on testing revealed that youâll get pretty competitive pricing on most of the more popular instruments.

I also tested the execution performance of both the Standard and Pro accounts and recorded a ping of 60 ms, which aligns with industry standards. I also learned that all accounts use a 100% margin call and a 50% stop-out, which trigger a warning when your free margin falls dangerously low.

Demo Accounts

4XC offers a demo account on the MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 platforms. With a demo account, you can explore the functionality of trading platforms and test your strategies without depositing any funds. Since markets are constantly changing, itâs crucial to keep your skills sharp without risking real money. You can open a demo account before or alongside your live CFD account.

Swap-Free (Islamic) Accounts

4XC offers an Islamic account for swap-free trading. It is only available with the Standard accountâs pricing. For further information, please contact 4XCâs customer support.

What Leverage Does 4XC Offer?

4XC offers a maximum leverage of 1:500, which is considered pretty high. For example, if you deposit $100, you could open positions that are 500 times larger. In other words, you would be able to place orders of $50,000. In that way, the leverage allows you to amplify your market exposure.

While the leverage can boost your profits, it can also significantly increase your losses. So make sure you are fully aware of the risks associated with margin trading before you start trading on leverage.

Research

4XCâs research content is almost entirely AI-powered. It incorporates the Acuity Signal Centre package, which includes an intuitive economic calendar, a news sentiment gauge, and actionable trading signals. You can use it to keep tabs on the latest trade opportunities and gain instantaneous entries. On the downside, I noticed that 4XC has significantly scaled back the scope of its proprietary research content since my previous review. It no longer publishes video market breakdowns or written articles.

Economic Calendar

The economic calendar is a fundamental research tool that informs traders of upcoming economic releases and financial news that could move the market and create viable trading opportunities.

What I like about Acuityâs economic calendar is that it also tracks the historical performance of various economic indicators. You can read about past releases and how the market behaved then to assess how it is likely to behave during the next release. This gives you valuable insights into market seasonality. However, keep in mind that historical data is not a 100% guarantee of future market behavior.

Acuity Signal Centre

The Acuity plugin lets you track emerging trading opportunities across multiple assets. You can read about developing price patterns and what they entail, the underlying market sentiment, viable entry levels, take-profit levels, stop-loss orders, and more. I found these signals most convenient for day trading and news trading.

To access the full Acuity Signal Centre package, you must have deposited at least $500 into your account.
Education

4XC shines in the educational category with its outstanding courses, videos, and third-party content, including the Alpha, FX, T4F, and UK Trading academies. I was most impressed by 4XCâs proprietary courses, especially in technical and fundamental analysis. I also appreciated the hundreds of educational videos on the brokerâs YouTube channel, published in Spanish.

4XC caters to the needs of first-time traders with its three educational courses: âIntroduction to Forexâ, âTechnical Analysisâ, and âFundamental Analysisâ. You can learn about price action behavior and how to spot various price patterns, how to implement different trading strategies, how to understand market-moving headlines, and much more.

The other thing I really liked about 4XCâs offering is that it includes three third-party academies: âAlpha FX Academyâ, âT4F Academyâ, and âUK Trading Academyâ. They help you gain a deeper, more comprehensive understanding of trading basics. By subscribing to these academies, you also obtain morning briefings, live streaming sessions, practical insights into various trading strategies, and much more.

The Bottom Line

Founded in 2018 and headquartered in the Cook Islands, 4XC is making a name for itself with its robust market research content and rich collection of educational materials.

I was most impressed by 4XCâs rock-bottom costs for trading the GBPJPY pair and the German DAX40 index. From live testing, I also learned that the broker averages execution speeds of around 60 milliseconds, which is in line with the industry average. And if you seek even faster execution, you can take use of 4XCâs free VPS hosting.

The broker offers the standard MT4 and MT5 suites. You can use both platforms for basic technical analysis and easy order execution. Moreover, you can install the Acuity plugin and receive actionable trading signals directly on the platform.

No broker is perfect, and 4XC certainly has its disadvantages, such as its high crude oil spread and high Bitcoin commission. It also does not offer any stocks, and its instrument offering is pretty limited.

If you are a beginner trader looking for solid education, an algo trader looking for swift and precise execution, or simply looking for cost-free copy trading, then 4XC may be the broker youâve been looking for.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All ActivTrades entities guarantee the segregation of client funds from the companyâs corporate capital.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. All ActivTrades entities guarantee negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Clients of ActivTrades PLC are protected by up to GBP 85,000 under the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS). Clients of ActivMarkets â Empresa de Investimento S.A. are protected by up to EUR 20,000 under the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF). Clients of ActivTrades Corp and ActivTrades Markets Ltd are protected by up to $1,000,000 under a private insurance issued by the broker.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. ActivTrades Markets Ltd offers the highest leverage of up to 1:400 for global clients. In comparison, European clients have access to 1:30 leverage.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

Since its establishment in 2001, ActivTrades has successfully navigated the trading industry. According to its LinkedIn page, the company employs more than 270 professionals.

I reviewed ActivTradesâ client agreement and other legal documents and found everything is in order. I also discovered that ActivTrades displays live spreads data, helping visitors to the website assess the competitiveness of the brokerâs trading fees across different markets.

Is ActivTrades Safe to Trade With?

I determined that ActivTrades can be considered a safe partner due to the following factors:

  • Tightly regulated
  • Keeps client funds segregated
  • Ensures negative balance protection
  • Has issued a private indemnity insurance

Fees

ActivTrades doesnât charge commissions, but its spreads vary across instruments. While EUR/USD and share CFD spreads are highly competitive, the broker charges relatively high spreads on popular commodities. During my testing, swap fees were also on the higher side. ActivTrades imposes a Â£10 inactivity fee, but deposits and withdrawals are free of charge.

The broker imposes a GBP 10 inactivity fee applied to dormant accounts following 52 weeks of dormancy. The fee is charged monthly until account activity resumes or the balance drops to zero.

Are ActivTradesâ Fees Competitive?

I assessed that ActivTradesâ fees generally sit in the medium range. While some of its spreads are very competitive, its commodity spreads were quite elevated during my test. The same discrepancy applies to the non-trading fees: the broker does not impose a handling fee on deposits and withdrawals, but charges dormant accounts with an inactivity fee.

Platforms and Tools

ActivTrades offers its flagship web platform alongside the seamless TradingView and the popular MT4 and MT5. The broker has also developed a versatile mobile app for trading on the go. The platforms accommodate the execution of sophisticated technical analysis, scalping, automated trading, and more.

ActivTrader Features

I tested ActivTradesâ flagship platform, which has a familiar and user-oriented interface. The charts, orders, and instruments search bar are easy to locate, and even first-time traders can quickly learn their way around.

ActivTrader is available on Windows and Mac and supports 13 languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Arabic, Chinese, and more. I appreciated the integration of market research directly on the platform, as shown below. On the downside, the platform does not have a desktop version or full-screen charts.

ActivTrader features include:

  • Alerts-Setting Option: Traders can set alerts for when the price of a given instrument falls/rises to a predetermined level, which could potentially signal a viable entry opportunity.
  • Watchlist Customization: Traders can populate watchlists with their favorite instruments and track market changes more easily.
  • One-click Trading: This feature enables instant market entries at the spot price and is invaluable for high-precision traders, such as scalpers.
  • Trading from the Chart: Traders can place conventional trading orders directly from the chart, specifying the entry price, volume level, stop and take-profit levels, and more.

The platform has high-definition charts powered by TradingView, which allow chart artists to examine price action behaviour in great detail. I also appreciated the progressive trailing stop, which allows traders to place up to two price levels upon which, once reached, the distance of the trailing stop will be adjusted. Traders can use this feature to exercise tighter risk management even in highly volatile markets.

Charts

Analytical tools and chart configurations include:

  • 106 technical indicators: Including trend-based and volume-based indicators, as well as oscillators. These are used to analyze price action and assess market sentiment, helping predict market movements.
  • 75 drawing tools: Tools like Fibonacci retracement levels and Elliott waves help identify price patterns, support/resistance levels, and breakout points.
  • 9 timeframes: For multi-timeframe analysis, enabling detailed price action analysis.
  • 16 chart types: Price action can be displayed in multiple ways, offering diverse perspectives on current trading opportunities.

The platformâs charts are fluid and easily scalable. Price action is represented clearly and in great detail. These contributing factors make ActivTrader great for comprehensive technical analysis.

My only two gripes with the platform are that the charts screen does not have a full-screen option, and that the lowest timeframe is 1 minute.

Orders

ActivTrader features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which supports immediate entries at the spot price.

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.
  • Progressive Trailing Stop: Unique to the ActivTrades platform, the progressive trailing stop affords traders a two-tiered backstop for tighter and more dynamic risk management during moments of heightened market volatility.

ActivTrader: My Key Takeaways

The ActivTrades platform is a powerful and user-friendly solution for beginner, intermediate, and advanced traders alike. Its layout is easy to discern, and its high-definition charts are powered by TradingView.

ActivTrader supports one-click trading and features a progressive trailing stop for advanced risk management. On the downside, the platform does not have a desktop version and does not feature full-screen charts.

ActivTrader App

The ActivTrades mobile app is available on iOS and Android. It retains the flexibility of its web counterpart and enables fast and easy order execution and management. Featuring a pleasant outlook with clear and streamlined charts, ActivTrader App is equipped with a news screener and supports one-tap trading.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives that speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical ownership.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

ActivTradesâ hour-long webinars are available in 7 languages, including English, German, French, and Chinese. Highly informative and practical, they often cover the current trading landscape, but also focus on trading-specific topics, such as trading plan and risk management. More than 100 past webinars are available from the brokerâs YouTube channel along with several platform tutorials.

The Bottom Line

London-based ActivTrades was established in 2001 and is regulated across multiple jurisdictions. The broker offers over 1,100 CFD instruments and also supports spread betting.

I was particularly impressed by ActivTradesâ lightning-fast execution and its intuitive, feature-rich trading platform. It also supports MT4, MT5, and TradingView, while delivering high-quality market research, responsive customer support, and comprehensive educational resources.

On the downside, spreads on some popular instruments are high, and there is no raw spread account and copy trading solutions.

I consider ActivTrades is an excellent choice for day traders of all experience levels, and a solid option for those looking to engage in spread betting.

ACY Securities Regulators

When reviewing brokers, we examine the licenses held by each of their entities to assess how effectively they protect clients. We use a simple three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier-1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about the three entities operating under the ACY Securities trade name:

  • ACY Securities Pty Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) under license number 403863. We rate ASIC as a Tier-1 regulator.
  • ACY Securities SA Pty Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Conduct Authority (FSCA) in South Africa under license number 51008. We rate the FSCA as a Tier-2 regulator.
  • ACY Capital LLC is incorporated in St Vincent and the Grenadines as a Limited Liability Company with company number 2610 LLC 2022. The entity is not regulated.

chunked.content:
How Does ACY Securities Protect You?

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is how ACY Securities Pty Ltd protects you:

â Segregated Accounts â Client funds are kept separate from the companyâs own capital.

â Negative Balance Protection â Your losses cannot exceed your invested capital.

âCompensation Scheme â In the unlikely event of insolvency, you will be compensated by up to AUD 2.5 million under ACY Securitiesâ Professional Indemnity Insurance.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, check our dedicated guide on client protections.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

ACY Securities isnât a newcomer. I checked the brokerâs track record and found it has been operating for over 15 years, supported by a global team of more than 150 professionals. The company also maintains a dedicated R&D technology team based in Taiwan, responsible for developing and maintaining proprietary products like the ACY Trading Platform, in-house copy trading solution, and the client portal.

I appreciated that ACY Securities publishes live raw spreads from its ProZero account directly on the homepage, allowing visitors to see real-time pricing before signing up. By clicking on any of the instruments listed, I was taken to a dedicated instrument page with access to live charting and sentiment analysis.

I also read through ACY Securitiesâ legal documents, including its customer agreement and risk notices, and everything was in order and presented in clear, easy-to-understand language.

Is ACY Securities Safe?

I concluded that ACY Securities is reliably safe to trade with due to the following factors:

  • Licensed by two global regulators.
  • Keeps client funds separate from its own capital.
  • Guarantees negative balance protection.
  • Provides insurance coverage up to AUD 2.5 million.

Fees

My tests placed ACY Securities right in the industry middle ground, though they offered notably tight spreads on EUR/USD and share CFDs. While overnight swaps were standard, the broker charges zero fees for deposits or withdrawals, and, unlike many competitors, you are not penalized with an inactivity fee if you take a break from trading.

If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

chunked.content:
It is designed for speed and simplicity. I found the ACY Trading platform easy to navigate, so even first-time traders can quickly get their bearings. While it doesnât offer the overwhelming feature density of some competitor platforms, it compensates with a streamlined interface that feels fast and efficient. The platform runs smoothly on all major browsers and supports English, Arabic, Chinese, and Vietnamese.

More than just a good look. Beyond its clean design, the ACY Trading Platform includes several practical trading features. Depending on jurisdiction, eligible traders can access dynamic leverage of up to 1:5000, while guaranteed stop losses are available to help manage downside risk. The platform also integrates a built-in economic calendar and a sentiment widget, allowing traders to monitor upcoming events and market positioning without relying on external tools.

The charting capabilities are surprisingly deep. Despite its simple look, the platform is packed with analytical power. I counted 21 built-in technical indicators and 26 drawing tools, including Fibonacci retracements and Elliott Waves.

I particularly liked the 10 available timeframes, one of the larger offerings Iâve seen, which makes multi-timeframe analysis a breeze. The charts feel fluid and illustrate price action in great detail, making it easy for technical traders to scale in and out of positions.

It handles the essentials well. The ACY platform supports one-click trading and allows you to manage orders directly from the chart, a must-have for fast-paced day trading. It also includes an integrated economic calendar, so you donât have to tab out to check news. It covers all the core order types â Market, Limit, and Stop â providing the necessary tools for most manual strategies to protect positions and manage risk.

chunked.content:
The trade-offs

It lacks advanced automation. If you rely on expert advisors (EAs) or copy trading, you are out of luck here. Youâll need to stick to ACYâs MetaTrader 4 or 5 offerings for those features.

Scalpers might feel limited. The lowest timeframe available is 1 minute. This means that scalpers looking for tick-by-tick precision or Depth-of-Market (DoM) data will find the platform lacking.

Multitasking is restricted. I noticed that you canât detach charts to separate windows, which is a minor annoyance for traders who prefer running multi-monitor setups.

My Verdict

I found the ACY Trading Platform clean, fast, and easy to master, with excellent charting tools for technical analysis. However, it lacks the automation and advanced depth-of-market features found in MetaTrader.

MT5 App

Since ACY doesnât offer its own trading app, I tested the MetaTrader 5 app, which is available on iOS and Android. Itâs a reliable, no-frills tool that is perfect for managing positions on the go, though it lacks the slick interface of modern competitors.

I also noticed that ACY publishes several educational blog posts dedicated to the MT5 mobile platform. Traders can learn about underused features like partially closing positions directly from the mobile app.

It gets the job done. While the MT5 app lacks the polish of proprietary apps from other brokers, it provides quick and easy access to the market on the go. You can use it for opening, closing, and tweaking positions while away from the desk.

Control is at your fingertips. The app allows you to place market, limit, and stop orders with ease. I found it essential for adjusting exposure during bursts of market volatility. If you need to hit the brakes or take profit while youâre out for coffee, the MT5 app handles the task without complaint.

The trades-offs

It feels clunky. The MetaTrader app is powerful, but it isnât pretty. Analyzing price action on a small screen can be challenging compared to smoother, more modern alternatives, and in my view, it functions primarily as an execution tool rather than a platform for in-depth technical analysis.

That said, Iâve observed that some traders overcome the small-screen limitation by connecting their mobile device to a smart TV or external display, executing trades on the phone while viewing charts on a larger screen.

VPS Hosting

ACY Securities offers free VPS hosting for low-latency forex trading, which is particularly useful for traders running Expert Advisors (EAs) on MT4 or MT5.

In practice, most EA traders tend to use the Standard or ProZero account types when deploying automated strategies, including martingale EAs and other algorithmic systems that rely on stable execution.

I also noted that ACY staff regularly carry out internal EA testing, enabling account managers to discuss the pros and cons of different EA styles, the operational nuances of running automated strategies, and even the fundamentals of creating and coding custom EAs. Live account holders also receive access to 15 proprietary MetaTrader scripts developed in-house.

ACY Securities processes client orders either internally or via external liquidity providers. In some cases, the broker may take the opposite side of a clientâs trade, consistent with its execution model and risk management practices.

What Are CFDs?

CFDs (Contracts for Difference) let you trade on the price movements of assets, like gold, without actually owning them.

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you lose, without ever buying real gold.

The biggest perk is that you can jump in or out of the market quickly to take advantage of even the smallest price changes.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money, allowing them to open larger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Sessions regularly cover Smart Money Concepts, fundamental analysis, and live market reviews across actively traded instruments, including gold, the Nasdaq, Silver, major indices, and key forex pairs. Traders can ask questions in real time and request on-the-spot analysis of specific markets or breaking news events directly from the analyst. These sessions are genuinely interactive, with participants encouraged to engage and explore real-time price action as it unfolds.

The webinars are offered in multiple languages, including English, Arabic, Chinese, and Spanish, and can be accessed for free via the ACY website or the client portal. In addition to regular live sessions, the broker also runs periodic masterclasses and strategy-focused webinars that break down complete entry and exit rules, allowing traders to backtest and study different trading approaches in more depth.

Trade Ideas

I also liked the Trade Ideas videos in the client portal. These arenât just random signals; experts break down specific price patterns and support levels, explaining the why behind the move: the emergence of a particular price pattern, what motivates it (e.g., a specific economic development), key support and resistance levels, and more.

Market Sentiment

If you like to know how the crowd is positioning, the Market Sentiment gauge is a handy feature. It displays the real-time split between buyers and sellers among ACYâs own clients, giving you a clear view of the underlying market dynamics.

Market Analysis

For a broader market context, ACY Securities publishes daily market analysis that goes beyond surface-level commentary. These articles are available in multiple languages, including English, Arabic, Chinese, and Spanish, and are designed for traders looking for actionable trade ideas rather than general market opinion.

I found that the analysis consistently outlines both intraday and swing trading scenarios, clearly marking key technical levels while explaining the underlying fundamental narrative driving price action.

Each piece focuses on how major economic data, central bank developments, and macro events are influencing the market, with technical execution framed around tools such as Smart Money Concepts, Fibonacci retracements, and trend identification.

This combination makes the content particularly useful for active traders who want to align fundamental catalysts with precise technical timing, whether trading short-term opportunities or more structured swing setups.

Room for Improvement

The ACYâs research requires some navigation. While the content is high-quality, much of it, like the Trade Ideas and webinars, is housed in the client portal rather than being fully integrated into the trading platform window. You will likely need to keep a separate browser tab open to make the most of it.

Education

ACY Securities offers a solid library of videos, articles, and e-books tailored for beginners as well as traders looking to level up their skills. Beyond general education, I found a wide range of in-depth educational blogs focused specifically on how to trade Gold using Smart Money Concepts, along with full trading strategy breakdowns such as the Quick Start Trading Strategy. Overall, the material goes beyond pattern recognition, offering practical guidance designed to support consistent decision-making and risk management.

I was most impressed by ACY Securitiesâ extensive collection of video content. I counted over 800 educational videos and past webinars on the brokerâs YouTube channel. If you are struggling with the software, I found 54 dedicated tutorials covering everything from MetaTrader to the ACY platform. Itâs rare to see a catalog this exhaustive.

The broker has also published numerous educational articles on its website, with free access to both registered clients and casual visitors. I found the articles particularly valuable because they go beyond charts to cover the mindset, tackling topics like âMental Energy Managementâ and âSelf-Discipline.â Most brokers skip this aspect of trading entirely, but ACY dives right in.

The educational section also includes dedicated sections on technical and fundamental analysis, trading mindset, position sizing, and stop-loss strategies, helping traders build a more structured and disciplined approach.

To round out the education offering, ACY provides three eBooks. One that stood out to me focuses specifically on news trading and goes beyond general concepts, outlining four distinct methods used by ACY analysts to trade major economic releases. It also details the key data sources analysts monitor before and after news events, along with practical dos and donâts for trading high-impact Forex economic news.

The Bottom Line

Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Australia, ACY Securities is making waves in the financial derivatives trading industry with its fast execution speeds, broad tradable instruments offering, and variety of trading platforms.

I learned that ACY Securities is achieving average order execution speeds of around 30 milliseconds, which is significantly faster than the industry average of 60 milliseconds. Its clients can also engage with over 2,380 tradable instruments across multiple markets from one of ACYâs three platforms: MT4, MT5, and its proprietary ACY Trading Platform.

The brokerâs fees are reasonable, although its cross-FX and crypto spreads could be lower. Another minor drawback is the lack of a proprietary mobile app. On the plus side, ACY provides comprehensive supporting content in the form of penetrating market research and illuminating educational content.

I concluded that ACY Securities is a great fit for casual traders and day traders.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity they choose to open an account with.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of client funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Client funds are kept in segregated accounts with ADSS and away from the companyâs corporate capital.
  • Negative balance protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance for retail clients. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. The broker does not guarantee negative balance protection.
  • Compensation scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. ADSS does not participate in a compensation scheme.
  • Maximum leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with ADSS is 1:500.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

ADSS has been operational for nearly 15 years and has over 500 associated employees on its LinkedIn page, both indicating its high stability. I also went over its legal documents and found that everything was in order â information is readily available and easy to discern.

I appreciated ADSSâs tight client categorization policy and âbest execution policyâ, which is a legal mandate to provide its clients with optimal price quotes under the prevailing market conditions.

A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

  2. The size of the clientâs financial instrument portfolio, including cash deposits AND financial instruments, exceeds EUR 500,000.
  3. The client has worked or is currently working in the financial sector for at least one year in a professional position that requires knowledge of the transactions or services being considered.

ADSS offers accounts for swap-free trading under Shariah law. All types of available accounts can be converted to Islamic accounts. For further assistance, please contact the broker.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Research

ADSS provides decent market research, blending in-house content with content from third-party providers. The broker offers a variety of highly insightful market breakdowns, a Dow Jones-powered news screener, an advanced market sentiment gauge, and featured trading ideas. However, it lacks video market research.

Research Tools

I have broken ADSSâ research content by type below:

  • Economic Calendar: A staple of market research, the calendar informs traders of upcoming economic and financial releases that could create viable trading opportunities.
  • ADSS Analysis: ADSS delivers detailed in-house market analyses, offering insights into the latest market movements and breaking down the reasons behind price action through fundamental analysis.
  • Dow Jones News: The news screener, powered by Dow Jones, helps ADSSâ clients stay on top of the latest market developments and changes in market dynamics.
  • Market Insights: ADSS incorporates the Trading Central package, which is available to fully verified live accounts. The package includes featured trading ideas, technical breakdowns, and the Market Buzz sentiment gauge.

ADSS Research: My Key Takeaways

ADSS provides comprehensive market research, keeping traders informed about emerging trading setups and the factors driving market movements. The analysis incorporates both fundamental and technical perspectives, making it insightful yet easy to digest. However, one notable gap is the lack of video breakdowns, which could enhance the learning experience for visual learners.

Education

ADSS provides a diverse range of educational resources, including articles, videos, and a comprehensive glossary of trading terms. The content covers key topics like technical and fundamental analysis, trading psychology, and risk management, catering to traders of all experience levels.

ADSS offers a wide selection of educational videos and articles, allowing traders to choose the format that best suits their learning style. Most importantly, the content covers all key aspects of tradingâtechnical and fundamental analysis, risk management, and trading psychologyâproviding a well-rounded foundation for traders at any level.

One standout feature of ADSSâs educational library is its clear and structured layout, making it easy for traders to quickly find and access the topics that interest them most.

The Bottom Line

ADSS is a financial institution based in the UAE, operating since 2011 under the regulation of the Capital Market Authority (CMA). The broker complies with strict safety standards and offers 1,050+ tradable instruments and 11,500 investing products across multiple markets, giving traders a broad range of opportunities.

When it comes to trading costs, ADSS offers a mix of low to high fees, but one standout feature is its crude oil spreadâone of the lowest in the industry.

On the trading platform side, ADSS delivers a versatile experience with its flagship WebTrader, which is packed with integrated market research for a seamless trading process. It also supports the widely used MetaTrader 4, catering to traders who prefer a more familiar setup.

A few drawbacks include the lack of copy trading and VPS hosting, and the fact that USD is the only available base currency.

I rated ADSS as a great choice for both casual and experienced traders, especially those focused on commodity trading.

Is Alchemy Markets Regulated?

When reviewing a broker, we examine how each of its entities is regulated and assess how effectively they protect clients. We use a three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier-1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about the three entities operating under the Alchemy Markets brand:

  • Alchemy International Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Seychelles Financial Services Authority (FSA), license number SD136. We rate Seychelles FSA as a Tier-3 regulator.
  • Alchemy Markets Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA), registration code C 56519. We rate MFSA as a Tier-1 regulator.
  • Alchemy Prime Limited is licensed and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), reference number 612233. We rate the UK FCA as a Tier-1 regulator.

chunked.content:
How Does Alchemy Markets Protect You

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts separate from those used for the brokerâs corporate capital protects clients in the event of broker insolvency. All of Alchemy Marketsâ entities ensure this.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. All Alchemy Markets entities provide negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects retail traders against the brokerâs liabilities in the unlikely event that the company becomes insolvent. Clients of Alchemy Prime Limited are insured under the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) for up to Â£85,000, and clients of Alchemy Markets Ltd benefit from insurance of up to â¬20,000 from the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF). Clients of the offshore entity (Alchemy International Ltd) do not have account insurance.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category tests, we also cover factors related to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Founded in 2016, Alchemy Markets has a solid 10-year operating history. The company is headquartered in Malta and reports having 201 to 500 employees worldwide.

I found the company to be transparent overall, and during my review, I was able to easily find key information. The About Us page covers the companyâs background; commissions are covered in the Accounts section; regulatory info is listed in the website footer, and the finer details can be found in the Legal Documents section.

Is Alchemy Markets Safe to Trade With?

To conclude, I rate Alchemy Markets as having a better than average level of trustworthiness and stability due to the following factors:

Keep in mind that Alchemy Markets has two other account types â Premier and VIP â that offer more competitive trading costs but require much higher deposits.

Alchemy Markets MetaTrader 4 Desktop Platform

Alchemy Markets offers the MetaTrader 4 platform, which includes advanced functions such as automated trading.

MetaTrader 4 is available in 39 languages, from Arabic to Vietnamese. The platform provides popular features, including the following:

  • Alerts: This feature updates traders when an instrument reaches a specific price level.
  • Watchlists: Traders can create a list of their favorite instruments and follow live quotes in a market watch panel.
  • One-Click Trading: This feature allows traders to execute orders with a single click and no secondary confirmation. This feature enables traders to operate faster and is especially useful for short-term traders.
  • Trading from the Chart: MT4 also allows users to trade directly from the chart.

  • 9 Time Frames: Traders can choose from nine time frames, from one minute to one month.
  • 3 Chart Types: Traders can use Bar Charts, Japanese Candlestick Charts, and Line Charts.

I ran my tests, using my preferred chart type (Candlesticks), which you can customize by color and background, and with popular indicators like Bollinger Bands and MACD.

Orders

MetaTrader also delivers when it comes to the range of available order types. The platform offers these order types:

  • Market Order: Traders use market orders to buy or sell an instrument at the best current price.
  • Limit Order: Traders use limit orders to buy or sell an instrument at a specified price or better.
  • Stop Loss Order: Traders use stop-loss orders to buy or sell an instrument when its price reaches a specified level.
  • Trailing Stop Order: Traders use trailing stop-loss orders as a stop-loss order at a defined percentage or dollar amount away from an instrumentâs current market price. This order type allows traders to secure profits when they are in a winning trade without having to exit the position.

MetaTrader 4 Desktop Platform: My Key Takeaways

As one of the most popular trading platforms in the world and the only one offered by many forex brokers, I have spent a lot of time testing MT4. The platformâs look and feel are a bit dated, and I feel there is room for improvement in design and usability.

Still, MT4 is a highly versatile platform that outperforms many competitors. It offers advanced charting, a comprehensive range of order types, and popular features such as one-click trading, trading directly from charts, and customizable alerts.

Its desktop platform stands out with advanced features, including the ability to run and backtest automated strategies, making it a powerful tool for skilled traders. However, its steep learning curve makes it better suited to experienced traders than to beginners.

MT4 Mobile App

Alchemy Markets offers the MetaTrader 4 mobile app for Android and iOS. The app offers popular features such as alerts, 1-click trading, and trading from the chart.

Charting within the app offers:

  • 30 Indicators: including trend indicators, oscillators, and volume.
  • 24 drawing tools/objects: including trendlines, Fibonacci retracement, and channels.
  • 9 timeframes: from 1 minute to 1 month.
  • 3 chart types: line chart, bar chart, candlestick chart.

The MT4 app also provides standard order types, including pending and stop orders. However, trailing stop-loss orders are only available from the desktop.

To change the language in the MT4 app, you must set your phoneâs language.

MT4 Mobile App: My Key Takeaways

As with the desktop platforms, the MT4 appâs interface is not highly intuitive, but it offers a solid range of features. I rate it as a reliable option for placing trades and managing your account on the go.

Alchemy Markets Order Execution Model

Like all CFD brokers, Alchemy Markets is the contractual counterparty to client trades. It describes itself as a Straight Through Processing (STP) broker operating an A-book risk model, meaning it typically hedges client positions externally with liquidity providers such as banks or prime brokers. In practice, this reduces potential conflicts of interest compared to a B-book model, where the broker keeps client trades in-house and may profit when they lose.

Alchemy Markets offers three retail account types: Classic, Premier, and VIP. The Classic account starts at $1,000, while the Premier account has a $5,000 minimum and features tighter spreads and lower commissions. The VIP account requires a $50,000 minimum deposit and provides raw spreads and the lowest commissions. Demo and swap-free accounts are also available. Minimum initial deposits are higher than the industry average across all account types, which reduced the brokerâs score in this category.

How to Open an Account with Alchemy Markets

Opening a live account with Alchemy International Ltd is a quick online process that can be completed within a few minutes. You need to provide the following information:

  • Personal details: Name, email, country of residence, phone number, date of birth
  • Documents: Proof of ID (Passport, driverâs license), proof of residence (utility bill, tax bill)

In my experience, this short account registration process is typical when you are signing up with an offshore entity. I opened a demo account that required only basic personal details.

The account minimums are among the highest I have encountered in my reviews, which might be a serious dealbreaker for casual and beginner traders.

Alchemy Markets offers demo accounts via MetaTrader. Demo accounts are especially important for beginners as they allow them to practice their strategies and get comfortable with the trading platform without risking real money.

The demo account features live quotes and simulates real market conditions for assets such as forex and CFDs on commodities, indices, and stocks. Once users are up to speed on a demo, they can easily switch to a live account.

Swap-Free (Islamic) Accounts

Alchemy Markets offers a swap-free account for traders who follow Sharia law. The account removes overnight interest charges while still providing access to the brokerâs platforms and core trading features.

What Leverage Does Alchemy Markets Offer?

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex and CFD markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is the use of borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

For the Alchemy International Ltd entity, the maximum leverage is 1:500 (verified April 2026). This means that with an account of $1,000, you can control up to $50,000 worth of positions in the market. For an offshore broker entity, this level of leverage is fairly standard. While it can increase potential returns, it also significantly raises risk.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders should keep in mind that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

Alchemy Markets does not offer services to residents or any other country where such distribution or use would be contrary to local law or regulation, such as Russia, Ukraine, Iran, the USA, and Malaysia.

Research

Alchemy Markets shines in the research category, with a steady flow of well-crafted reports from its in-house team, coupled with analysis by third-party Trading Central and tools from FXBlue. Research resources provide high-quality insights for active, short-term traders. I found the Featured Ideas section of Trading Central the most useful, as it calls out specific chart patterns and directional bias. I rate the offering as better than the industry average.

The Market Insights section at Alchemy Markets is a research hub focused on short-term analysis, technical setups, and macro-driven commentary. With actionable ideas, the analysis is best suited to active traders, like day traders, scalpers, and news traders.

Themed reports like âChart of the Dayâ, âWeekly Outlookâ, and âOpening Bellâ include a mix of technical analysis and fundamental drivers like central bank policy and economic releases. Reports cover a broad range of assets, including forex, commodities, indices, and crypto. I liked that the analysis goes beyond the theoretical to provide actionable trading ideas.

Alchemy Markets clients can access Trading Central research within the client portal. The Technical Views section offers bullish or bearish setups with key levels, Market Buzz tracks real-time news and social sentiment to highlight trending assets, and Featured Ideas provides trade ideas based on chart patterns.

Alchemy Markets clients can also access MetaTrader tools from FXBlue that enhance trading with sentiment analysis, correlation data, and faster execution. MetaTrader add-ons like Market Manager help to better manage trades in real time, while the Correlation Matrix allows you to analyze asset correlations instantly.

Alchemy Markets Research: My Key Takeaways

Alchemy Markets provides a well-rounded research offering, combining in-house analysis with Trading Central research and FXBlue tools. The focus is on actionable trading ideas, key price levels, and macro-driven catalysts, geared towards active, short-term traders. I especially liked focused reports like the Chart of the Day and practical tools like the Correlation Matrix MetaTrader add-on.

Education

Alchemy Markets also provides strong educational materials, including sections on classic chart patterns, Japanese Candlestick patterns, and in-depth guides to basic and intermediate concepts. These are supplemented with live education via webinars. Educational materials are more slanted towards beginners, but I also found some content that could be useful to experienced traders.

I went over the Candlesticks section at Alchemy Markets and found that it does an excellent job of explaining how to read price action using candlestick patterns like the Harami and Shooting Star. It shows how to identify potential price reversals and continuations, and how to use other technical indicators to improve accuracy.

Materials include in-depth, practical guides to improve your trading. For example, the Volume Footprint Chart Complete Guide shows how traders can analyze buying and selling activity at each price level to better understand market behavior and identify potential reversals and breakouts.

Alchemy Markets also offers regular live webinars on topics like trading gold, covering the macro backdrop, key market drivers, and major price levels to watch.

The Bottom Line

Malta-based Alchemy Markets is an established CFD broker that launched in 2016. It offers the popular MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, and TradingView platforms but lacks a proprietary option.

Perks include free VPS hosting, FIX API, research from Trading Central, and MetaTrader add-ons from FXBlue. The broker offers a wide range of CFD assets, notably strong in forex and crypto, but leaving room for improvement in shares.

Client protections such as segregated funds and negative balance protection are in place across all three of its entities, although compensation schemes are limited to UK and EU clients. Overall, I found the broker to be reasonably transparent in key areas like regulation and trading costs.

Fees are mixed and depend on the account type. While index pricing is competitive and raw spreads are available on the VIP account, the Classic account trading costs are mostly more expensive than average. Commissions on shares, crypto, and futures are substantial. Swap fees are broadly in line with the industry, but the inactivity fee is high.

Overall, I rate Alchemy Markets as best suited to experienced traders, including day traders, scalpers, and algo traders who can take full advantage of its advanced platforms and tools. While itâs not a good fit for long-term investors looking for access to traditional assets like real stocks and ETFs, it offers a solid trading environment for active, short-term CFD traders.

What I Did not Test

Please note that for this review of Alchemy Markets, I did not use live accounts to test spreads or deposit/withdraw real capital. My tests were also limited to the MetaTrader 4 platform.

chunked.content:
Quick Verdict

I began reviewing forex brokers in 2021, after over a decade in the trading industry in Chicago, where I was a professional trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and a Series 3-licensed futures and forex broker. I took an active role in developing our rating system based on my experience of what traders value. For this Alchemy Markets review, I used a demo trading account. Here is a summary of my findings:

Best Fit For: Experienced day traders, scalpers, and algo traders who can benefit from MT4, MT5, VPS hosting, FIX API, and custom tools from FXBlue. Forex traders can access a wide variety of pairs, while those trading indices will appreciate tight spreads on DAX and Dow.

Less Ideal For: Long-term investors due to the lack of non-CFD instruments. Traders focused on CFDs on shares may be disappointed by high commissions and limited selection. Beginners and casual traders may be put off by high initial deposit requirements.

Swing Trading Average swap fees, diverse range of CFD assets Lacks real stocks â Acceptable Choice
Investing â Lacks traditional investment assets like real stocks, ETFs, mutual funds â Not Recommended

Alchemy Markets Overview

Alchemy Markets is a forex and CFD broker founded in 2016 and based in Malta. It holds licenses from three regulators, including the top-tier FCA and MFSA, as well as from the offshore FSA of Seychelles. Alchemy Markets is a Straight Through Processing (STP) broker and provides access to over 300 instruments.

My Key Takeaways of Alchemy Markets

  • MT4, MT5, and TradingView form a solid platform lineup, but the broker lacks a proprietary platform.
  • I experienced high trading costs via the Classic account on all instruments tested, except for indices. Much of the cost in shares, crypto, and futures is reflected in commissions rather than the spread.
  • Superb range of forex and crypto pairs, but shares lack global coverage.
  • The broker offers many tools for active traders, including Trading Central signals, MetaTrader add-ons from FXBlue, free VPS hosting, and the FIX API.
  • I found Alchemy Marketsâ research and educational materials better than average, with timely and actionable ideas.

Alchemy Markets Pros and Cons

Pros Cons
  • 80 forex pairs
  • Trading Central
  • MetaTrader add-ons from FXBlue
  • Tight spreads in indices
  • Free VPS hosting
  • Live webinars
  • Practical trading guides
  • No proprietary platform
  • High minimum deposit
  • High commissions

What Sets Alchemy Markets Apart?

Alchemy Markets stands out for its setup for experienced, short-term traders. My research showed that the broker supports this by offering the MetaTrader 4 and 5 platforms, free VPS hosting, FIX API, Trading Central signals, MetaTrader add-ons, and raw spreads via the VIP account.

For this review, I performed my tests on MetaTrader 4 using the desktop platform and MT4 mobile app. The account was opened with Alchemy International Ltd. Some features and services may vary depending on where you reside.

AMarkets Regulators

When reviewing brokers, we examine the licenses held by each of their entities to assess how effectively they protect clients. We use a simple three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier 1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about the two entities operating under the AMarkets trade name:

  • AMarkets Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Mwali International Services Authority (MISA) under license number T2023284. We rate MISA as a Tier-3 regulator. The entity is also incorporated in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines with the Financial Services Authority (FSA) there.
  • AMarkets LLC is registered in the Cook Islands with registration number LLC14486/2023 and is registered in a relevant registry operated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC). The entity is not regulated.
  • AMarkets LTD is incorporated in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines as a Limited Liability Company with registration number 22567 BC 2015. The entity is not regulated.

How Does AMarkets Protect You?

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is how AMarkets LLC protects you:

â Compensation scheme â In case of insolvency, the Financial Commission will reimburse your funds up to EUR 20,000.

â Negative balance protection â Your losses cannot exceed your invested capital.

â Segregated accounts â Your funds may be kept in the same accounts used for the companyâs own capital.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, click here.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share essential information.

My research showed that AMarkets has been around for nearly two decades and employs over 130 professionals worldwide, which really speaks to its stability and experience in the industry.

I also liked that the website is highly transparent, displaying live spreads and detailed contract specs so traders can easily check its fees and trading conditions.
Another plus is that AMarkets isnât just a member of The Financial Commission â itâs also regularly audited by VerifyMyTrade, which helps ensure fair and efficient order execution.

My only concern is that while AMarkets claims to keep client funds in segregated bank accounts, I couldnât find any confirmation of this in its legal documents.

Is AMarkets Safe?

I concluded that, despite the absence of segregated accounts and one unregulated entity, AMarkets is sufficiently safe to trade with due to the following factors:

  • Maintains high fee transparency.
  • Participates in the Financial Commission resolution scheme.
  • Maintains high execution standards.
  • Regularly audited by VerifyMyTrade.

Fees

AMarketsâ spreads are generally higher than the industry average, except for Apple stock CFDs. I was also surprised to see commissions on its Standard account â something rare for this account type. Fee competitiveness also suffers from high swaps. On the plus side, there is no inactivity fee, and deposits are free of charge.

AMarkets Spreads

I tested AMarketsâ spreads on 9 October 2025 during the London and New York opens. The results are shown in the table below:

AMarkets Swaps

A swap fee is the cost of keeping a trade open overnight, and itâs tied to the difference in interest rates between the two currencies in a pair. If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

AMarkets doesnât charge any fees on deposits, but withdrawals come with a handling fee, the amount of which depends on the payment method used. On the plus side, thereâs no inactivity fee, so dormant accounts wonât incur extra charges.

Are AMarketsâ Fees Competitive?

I concluded that AMarketsâ fees are less competitive than those of many of its peers. The brokerâs spreads on popular instruments are above the industry average, and it even charges commissions on some assets within the Standard account â something uncommon for this type of account. My testing also showed that commissions and overnight swap fees are relatively high.

On the positive side, deposits are free, and thereâs no inactivity fee, but withdrawals via bank transfer or credit/debit cards incur a handling fee.

Platforms and Tools

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I tested the MetaTrader 5 (MT5) desktop platform and found it relatively easy to navigate. The main dashboard is intuitive, with charts, order types, and trading instruments located in familiar places. Even first-time users can grasp the basics with minimal effort.

However, the platform design feels a bit outdated. Compared to more modern trading platforms, MT5âs chart visuals are rugged and lack the sleek, polished look that many traders today prefer.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by AMarkets is available for both Windows and Mac users and supports 39 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese â making it accessible to traders worldwide.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

In my opinion, MT5 excels particularly in automated trading. It supports Expert Advisors (EAs) and comes with an easy-to-use strategy tester, enabling algorithmic traders to fine-tune their systems for various market conditions.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is loaded with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format.

That said, the charts can get visually cluttered quite fast â even when only two indicators are active. This can make it harder to interpret price action clearly and may not be ideal for traders who rely heavily on clean, minimalistic chart setups.

Order Types

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a solid platform for fast and straightforward trading, particularly if youâre into algorithmic strategies or use EAs. Itâs reliable, packed with tools, and supports detailed trade execution.

However, its interface feels dated compared to more modern alternatives like TradingView or cTrader. If youâre a trader who values sleek design and customizable charting, MT5 may feel too rigid and visually overwhelming.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

What Are CFDs?

CFDs (Contracts for Difference) let you trade on the price movements of assetsâlike goldâwithout actually owning them.

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you loseâwithout ever buying real gold.

The biggest perk? You can jump in or out of the market quickly to take advantage of even the smallest price changes.
