In contrast, the ECN account offers tighter spreads and a $5 round-turn commission per traded lot (100,000 units), which is lower than the industry average of $6.

The Zero account provides raw spreads starting from 0.0 pips, but its $11 round-turn commission is nearly double the industry average.

Demo Accounts

AMarkets offers a demo account that lets traders explore the brokerâs available platforms and test their strategies in a risk-free environment. Since markets are constantly changing, itâs crucial to keep your skills sharp without risking real money. You can open a demo account before or alongside your live CFD account.

Swap-Free (Islamic) Accounts

AMarkets offers Islamic accounts for swap-free trading in accordance with Shariah law. For further information, please contact AMarketsâ customer support.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money, allowing them to open larger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Research

AMarkets offers excellent market research designed for day and swing traders of all levels. The broker combines in-house market analysis and trading signals with third-party insights from Autochartist, creating a well-rounded research experience. The real highlights are its Trade Plan and Trade Analyzer tools, which help traders maintain consistency and discipline in their approach.

Research Tools

  • Economic Calendar: The economic calendar is a fundamental research tool that informs traders of upcoming economic releases and financial news that have the potential to move the market and create viable trading opportunities.

• Sentiment Indicator: AMarkets has developed a unique sentiment indicator tool that tracks the correlation between an instrumentâs price action and the underlying buying and selling pressures.
    The RSI indicator is also overlaid as an additional gauge of overbought and oversold levels. Traders can utilize the tool to identify potential shifts in market direction.

• Trading Plan: One of AMarketsâ standout features is its personalized trading plan tool, designed to help less experienced traders build structured and effective trading strategies. It factors in each traderâs goals, capital, and risk tolerance, promoting a more systematic and disciplined approach to trading â a key step toward developing long-term consistency and success.

• Premium Analytics: AMarkets has created a proprietary information hub that gives clients access to a wide range of research materials, including trading ideas, market news breakdowns, and key event analyses. This premium analytics hub provides traders with a comprehensive, 360-degree view of current market trends and emerging trading opportunities.

• Trading Signals: AMarkets incorporates the Autochartist package, which includes actionable trading signals for various assets. Traders can read about viable trading opportunities across multiple timeframes. Each signal highlights an emerging trading pattern (e.g., the descending wedge from below) and explains how it can be effectively traded.

• Trade Analyzer: A supplementary tool to the Trade Plan, the Trade Analyzer assists traders by assessing the performance of their past trades â where they have been successful, where they have made mistakes, and what could have been done better. It, essentially, helps traders learn from their past performance.
  • YouTube Content: AMarkets publishes video breakdowns and trading ideas on its YouTube channel. These materials provide traders with a hands-off approach to learning about recent market developments and trading setups.

AMarkets Research: My Key Takeaways

I was impressed by the breadth and sophistication of AMarketsâ research content. The broker offers comprehensive coverage of key market developments and trading opportunities, seamlessly integrating proprietary research with third-party materials from Autochartist.

I especially enjoyed the high functionality of the Trading Plan and Trade Analyzer tools. The two are indispensable to traders who want to achieve consistent success.

Education

AMarkets provides a collection of educational videos and articles that equip beginner traders with essential trading insights and know-how on technical analysis, fundamental analysis, trading psychology, and risk management. However, the broker does not delve into the subject matter in great detail and does not conduct regular webinars, unlike many other brokers.

AMarketsâ blog features a rich collection of trading articles on various topics, including a comprehensive beginnerâs course. I counted over 240 articles across several categories: âTrading Strategiesâ, âFor Novicesâ, âEconomyâ, âCryptocurrenciesâ, and âTrading Course: Beginnerâs Guideâ.

First-time and intermediate traders can learn about the ABCs of technical analysis, fundamental analysis, trading psychology, and risk management. The content is written in an easy-to-understand manner and provides a strong basis for further learning.

AMarkets has also published a variety of educational videos on its website and YouTube channel. Some are more general, explaining topics such as âHow to Verify Your Account,â while others provide more specific insights â âTrend, Support, and Resistance Explainedâ.

The Bottom Line

After testing AMarkets firsthand, Iâd say itâs a solid choice for beginners and research-driven traders who value structure, insights, and practical trading tools over razor-thin spreads. Its Trading Plan and Trade Analyzer really stand out â features you donât often see elsewhere â helping traders build consistency instead of relying on luck or emotion.

That said, trading costs are higher than average, with spreads and commissions that may deter more cost-conscious traders. Still, AMarkets makes up for it with top-tier transparency, deep market research, and membership in The Financial Commission, which adds a layer of credibility many offshore brokers lack.

Overall, AMarkets might not be the cheapest broker around, but itâs a good fit if youâre looking to learn, grow, and trade with structure rather than just chase quick wins.

Anzo Capital operates under two entities: one authorized by the CMA (Kenya) and one unregulated. While the broker claims to segregate client funds, it does not offer negative balance protection or participate in any compensation scheme. Although Anzo Capital appears relatively transparent, its overall level of security remains weak.

Anzo Capital Regulations

In our reviews, we examine the licenses and regulations of each entity operated by a broker, allowing us to compare their different levels of protection. We rank licenses by various regulatory bodies on a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing indicates the highest level of regulation.

This is what I discovered about the two entities operating under the Anzo Capital trade name:

  • Anzo Capital Limited (SVG) LLC is incorporated in St. Vincent and the Grenadines with registration number 308 LLC 2020. The entity is not regulated.
  • Anzo Capital Limited is licensed and regulated by the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) of Kenya under license number 219. We rate the CMA as a Tier-2 regulator.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of client funds. Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Anzo Capital keeps client funds in segregated accounts.
  • Negative balance protection. This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. Anzo Capital does not guarantee negative balance protection. I also learned that under point 19.2 of the client agreement, if you incur a negative balance, you are responsible for depositing additional funds to compensate for the outstanding debt. Otherwise, the broker may take legal action against you.
  • Compensation scheme. A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Anzo Capital does not participate in a compensation scheme.
  • Maximum leverage. Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with Anzo Capital is 1:1000.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

According to Anzo Capitalâs LinkedIn page, the broker has been operating for 5 years and has around 30 employees. Additionally, I found out that Anzo has issued a âbest execution policyâ, which is a legal mandate to provide optimal price quotes under the prevailing market conditions.

I also reviewed the brokerâs website and legal documents and assessed that everything was in order overall. My one minor gripe is that Anzo does not display a live spread feed on the main page so that visitors can assess the fairness of its fees.

Is Anzo Capital Safe to Trade With?

I found that Anzo Capital keeps client funds in segregated accounts and has issued a Best Execution Policy. However, I concluded that the broker offers a low level of safety due to several key factors:

  • It operates without any regulatory oversight
  • It does not provide negative balance protection
  • It does not participate in a compensation scheme
  • It offers access to high leverage

Fees

My testing revealed that Anzo Capitalâs spreads vary, with low costs on share CFDs and oil, but higher spreads on major forex pairs. The broker does not charge commissions and has average overnight fees on its Standard account. Anzo Capital does not impose a handling fee for deposits or withdrawals, but dormant accounts are charged an inactivity fee.

Are Anzo Capitalâs Fees Competitive?

The same discrepancy applies to Anzoâs non-trading fees, as the broker allows cost-free payments but charges an inactivity fee.

Anzo Capital MT5 Desktop

I tested the desktop version of the MetaTrader 5 platform, which offers several essential tools, including one-click trading, an alarm setting option, and a market depth tool. These features enable traders to analyze market developments from multiple perspectives and take advantage of trading opportunities in various ways.

In my opinion, MT5 is best suited for automated trading via Expert Advisors (EAs). The platform also has an intuitive strategy tester, allowing experienced algo traders to tweak the parameters of their strategies so that they can be used under different market conditions.

General Ease of Use

Anzo Capitalâs MT5 platform is available on Windows and Mac and supports 52 languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Arabic, Chinese, and more.

MT5 also features:

  • Alerts-Setting Option: Traders can set alerts for when the price of a given instrument falls/rises to a predetermined level, which could potentially signal a viable entry opportunity.
  • Watchlist Customization: Traders can populate watchlists with their favorite instruments and track market changes more easily.
  • One-click Trading: This feature enables instant market entries at the spot price and is invaluable for high-precision traders, such as scalpers.
  • Trading from the Chart: Traders can place conventional trading orders directly from the chart, specifying the entry price, volume level, stop and take-profit levels, and more.

Charts

From my experience of using MetaTrader, its charts can quickly become cluttered, even with just two indicators. This can obscure price action examination and make it harder to perform detailed technical analysis.

I have broken down the available analytical tools and chart configurations below:

  • 38 technical indicators: This includes trend-based and volume-based indicators and oscillators to analyze price action and assess market sentiment, helping predict market movements.
  • 24 drawing tools: Tools like Fibonacci retracement levels and Elliott waves help identify price patterns, support/resistance levels, and breakout points. However, MT5âs design can make price action harder to interpret.
  • 21 timeframes: For multi-timeframe analysis, enabling detailed price action analysis.
  • 3 chart types: Price action can be displayed as line, bars, or candlesticks, offering diverse perspectives on trading opportunities.

In my opinion, the chart screen is one of the most crucial features of a trading platform. It equips traders with essential tools and configurations to analyze price action and spot trading opportunities. Just as important is the ability to easily scale price action, allowing for a clearer and more detailed view of market movements.

Orders

MetaTrader 5 features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which allows for immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the MetaTrader 5 platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a good option for fast and simple order execution, even though its dated and rugged design is inferior to newer and sleeker platforms. Still, MetaTrader remains the most popular and widely used trading platform in the industry.

Anzo Capital MT5 Mobile

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives that speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical ownership.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

How ATFX Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

â Segregation of client funds. ATFX keeps client funds in fully segregated bank accounts, separate from the brokerâs own operating capital. This structure helps reduce the risk of accounting errors and ensures that client money remains protected across all ATFX entities.

â Negative balance protection. ATFX provides negative balance protection across all its entities, ensuring that traders cannot lose more than the funds deposited in their accounts. This safeguard is particularly important during periods of high market volatility, as it prevents losses from exceeding your account balance.

â Compensation scheme. Client protection varies by ATFX entity. Clients of AT Global Markets (UK) Ltd are covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) up to GBP 85,000, while clients of AT Global Markets (Cy) Ltd are protected by the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF) up to EUR 20,000. Clients of AT Global Markets LLC receive additional coverage of up to USD 1,000,000 under the brokerâs Excess of Loss insurance policy.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Founded in 2017, ATFX has grown into a globally established CFD broker, holding licenses in multiple major jurisdictions. In our database, ATFX is among the more tightly supervised brokers in the retail forex and CFD industry.

My research revealed that ATFX employs 501â1,000 employees, operating at a scale that supports long-term stability and consistent service delivery. My research also showed that the broker maintains a strong presence across Europe, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, APAC, and South Africa, reflecting a mature international operating model.

ATFX also demonstrates a high level of transparency. I found all the necessary information on its website, including corporate structure, regulatory licenses, and client protection measures. Trading conditions and legal terms are set out in its Terms of Business document.

Is ATFX Safe to Trade With?

To summarize, my findings indicate that ATFX can be regarded as having a relatively high level of trust and stability due to the following factors:

  • Founded in 2017, with a proven and steadily expanding operating history
  • Regulated by multiple top-tier authorities, including the FCA, ASIC, and CySEC
  • Large operational scale, with 501â1,000 employees and a global presence
  • Transparent operating model with clear disclosure of risks, protections, and trading conditions

The broker balances this by charging no fees for deposits or withdrawals, helping to keep non-trading costs low. However, an inactivity fee applies to dormant accounts.

This structure allows ATFX to deliver consistent pricing, fast execution, and a clear zero-commission cost model, while using internal liquidity management and external hedging where necessary to maintain stable and reliable trade execution.

What Are CFDs?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

They also offer a wide range of trading courses and webinars, tailored for beginners, intermediate, and advanced traders alike, so thereâs something useful no matter where youâre at in your journey.

AvaTrade has published over 400 educational webinars on its YouTube channel, and traders can easily subscribe to future events from the website. The webinars are highly informative and pertain to different trading aspects: technical analysis, fundamental analysis, and trading psychology.

The broker also has developed a very well-organized and comprehensive system of educational courses, which span 27 individual lectures and have a total runtime of more than 205 minutes. This content allows traders to delve into the subject matter and go at their own pace. I appreciated that the lectures are packed with useful and highly practical information.

As a whole, I deem AvaTradeâs educational content wide enough and penetrating enough to help novice traders become consistently successful.

The Bottom Line

AvaTrade is a global broker offering over 1,450 CFDs and options. It stands out with a top-tier lineup of trading platforms and tools, strong market research, and a solid range of educational resources.

In my tests, AvaTradeâs fees proved to be competitive. Spreads on EUR/USD and crude oil were particularly attractive, and its low swap fees make the broker a good choice for swing traders. I also liked AvaTradeâs innovative AvaProtect tool, which adds an extra layer of risk management.

On the downside, Bitcoin trading fees could be more competitive, and the broker should consider adding more payment options for European users.

All in all, AvaTrade is a well-rounded broker that works great for day traders, swing traders, casual traders, and beginners alike.

I then use these as reference points for possible rebounds/reversals or breakouts/breakdowns, depending on the underlying trendâs direction.
  • 26 timeframes: cTrader offers the largest selection, which is great for multi-timeframe analysis. Typically, I use higher timeframes (above 4H) to determine the marketâs general direction and smaller timeframes (below 1H) to spot viable entries within the broader trend.
  • 6 chart types: Line, bar, candlestick, and more options that let traders view price action in their preferred format. Personally, I prefer candlesticks because they provide a more comprehensive picture. For example, a bullish Marubozu candlestick may signify strong buying sentiment, whereas the formation of a shooting star candlestick may indicate a possible bearish reversal.

My verdict on cTraderâs charting capabilities is overwhelmingly positive. Though not as fluid as TradingView, the platform is still detail-oriented and allows you to conduct probing technical analyses. I like that cTrader features detachable charts, which let you examine price action behaviour in full-screen mode. This helps scalability and allows you to spot even minor price action developments.

Order Types

cTrader offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries.
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.
  • Stop-Limit Order: Unlike most other platforms, cTrader also supports stop-limit orders. Once the stop price is reached, the order becomes a limit order that will be filled at the specified price, or better.

Algorithmic Trading

I consider cTrader the best option for algorithmic traders due to its comprehensive algo trading environment. You can access a wide selection of built-in cBots or purchase custom-built systems from the platformâs extensive marketplace. Moreover, experienced algo traders can use cTraderâs cutting-edge software to build their own systems, test them, and even sell them.

Copy Trading

cTrader also boasts a comprehensive copy-trading environment where signal providers and followers can interact and benefit from each otherâs needs. If you want to copy other tradersâ positions, you can sift through the available strategies and assess them based on their performance.

You can look at various metrics, such as average profits, return on investment, longevity, and more. And if you wish to earn a commission on your own strategies, you can upload them quite easily, set your subscription fee, and start attracting subscribers.

cTrader App

The cTrader mobile app is available on iOS and Android devices and offers most of the desktop versionâs functionality. This makes the cTrader app a convenient tool for staying connected to the market and adjusting your positions on the go.

You can place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as manage position size and risk directly from the app. Moreover, you can access a variety of market analytics, including a news screener and an economic calendar, as well as cTraderâs copy trading environment. That said, the charting experience still feels a bit cramped, and price action can be hard to scale and analyze comfortably on a small screen.

BlackBull Markets Order Execution

BlackBull Markets operates as an ECN broker. Client orders are matched using Electronic Communication Networks (ECN) technology, resulting in faster execution speeds (averaging 20-50 milliseconds) and tighter spreads. Essentially, buying orders are matched with selling orders, and selling orders are matched with buying orders.

I clocked BlackBull Marketsâ execution speed on 15 February (Sunday) at around 09:00 CET. I was impressed by the 30 milliseconds reading, given that it was recorded during off-trading hours when market liquidity tends to be greatly reduced.

In our reviews, we examine the licenses and regulations of each entity operated by a broker, allowing us to compare their different levels of protection. We rank licenses by various regulatory bodies on a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing indicates the highest level of regulation.

This is what I discovered about the two entities operating under the Bullwaves trade name:

chunked.content:
Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of Client Fund:. Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Both Bullwaves entities guarantee the segregation of client funds.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. The only Bullwaves entity that guarantees negative balance protection is Moonance LLC.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Bullwaves does not participate in a compensation scheme.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with Bullwaves is 1:500.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

Bullwaves has only been active for a year, so its long-term presence in the market remains unproven. According to the âassociated membersâ section on the brokerâs LinkedIn page, the company appears to have fewer than a dozen employees, which suggests itâs still in an early growth phase.

During my review of Bullwavesâ legal documents and website content, I uncovered several transparency issues:

  • The broker has not published a âbest execution policyâ, which is essential for ensuring fair and competitive pricing.
  • The site is missing a âcontract specificationsâ page, where traders would typically find details like target spreads, margin requirements, and live pricing.
  • Trading commissions are not disclosed anywhere on the website, which raises concerns about fee transparency.

I also noted some user experience (UX) issues on the website, such as small design inconsistencies that suggest the platform is still a work in progress. While these arenât major dealbreakers, they do reinforce the impression that Bullwaves is still finding its footing as a broker.

Is Bullwaves Safe to Trade With?

I determined that Bullwaves has a moderate level of safety due to the following factors:

  • Is authorized by two regulators
  • Keeps client funds in segregated accounts
  • Ensures readily available legal info

Fees

Bullwaves charges both spreads and commissions on its Classic account, and based on my testing, the overall fees fall in the upper range of the industry. The broker doesnât impose handling fees on deposits or withdrawals, except for withdrawals under EUR 100, which may incur a charge. Additionally, dormant accounts are subject to a $10 monthly inactivity fee.

Bullwaves Execution Model

Bullwaves operates on a hybrid model, serving both as principal to client orders and intermediary between its clients and the broader market. In the first instance, Bullwaves operates as a market maker (counterparty to client orders). In such cases, Bullwaves creates liquidity by trading against the trader â it buys against sellers and sells against buyers.

In the second instance, the broker routes client orders to its pool of liquidity providers, where they are filled at the best possible prices. In such cases, Bullwaves does not act as a counterparty to client orders but merely as an intermediary.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives that speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical ownership.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives that speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical ownership.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the derivativeâs price. However, this speed and flexibility come with high risk, as CFDs are leveraged products that can amplify both gains and losses.

What Are Knock-Outs?

Knock-out options are all about control. They come with built-in limits that let you cap your maximum exposure. In other words, you cannot lose more than the amount you have predetermined when purchasing the option.

Because of these boundaries, they are generally cheaper to trade than standard options, though they still come with a set expiration date.

Knock-out options work best in calmer markets. If the market gets too volatile and the price hits your pre-set boundary, the trade âknocks outâ immediately and closes at a loss.

  • CMC Markets Germany GmbH is authorised and regulated by the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin), ID number 10154814. We rate BaFin as a Tier 2 regulator.
  • CMC Markets Singapore Pte. Ltd. is authorised and regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). We rate MAS as a Tier 2 regulator.
  • CMC Markets Middle East Ltd. is authorised and regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), reference number F002740. We rate DFSA as a Tier 2 regulator.
  • CMC Markets NZ Ltd. is authorised and regulated by the New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA), reference number FSP41187. We rate FMA as a Tier 2 regulator.

Why is it important to know where your broker subsidiary (entity) is regulated?

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients worldwide. However, licenses obtained from regulators in different jurisdictions do not always entail the same degree of protection. 

Some regulators mandate compliance with the strictest financial frameworks, while others are less rigid. That is why traders must familiarize themselves with the safety mechanisms ensured by the entity they want to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of client funds. Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All CMC Markets entities guarantee the segregation of client funds.    
  • Negative balance protection. This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. All CMC Markets entities ensure negative balance protection.
  • Compensation scheme. A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Clients of CMC Markets UK PLC are protected by up to GBP 85,000 under the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS). Two more broker entities also have such a compensation scheme in place.  
  • Maximum leverage. Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum leverage with CMC Markets UK PLC is 1:30.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

Founded in 1989, CMC Markets has a substantial operating history and is one of the oldest forex and CFD brokers in the world. It is also one of the largest, with between 501 and 1,000 employees, according to the companyâs LinkedIn page. Headquartered in the City of London, CMC Markets also has offices in Sydney, Singapore, Toronto, and across Europe.

CMC Markets is publicly traded and listed on the London Stock Exchange (UK:CMCX). In 2020, it became part of the FTSE 250 Index, a capitalisation-weighted index listing the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange. As a publicly traded company, CMC Markets must disclose financial reports, allowing for greater insight into the stability of the company.

In our research, CMC Markets demonstrated a high level of transparency regarding its regulatory status, fees, and general background information. The materials are readily available on the website. 

The regulatory status of different subsidiaries is covered at the footer of each page. The Trading Costs page clearly outlines all the costs, such as spreads and overnight holding fees. A User Agreement (Terms of Business) document is available on the CFD Legal Documents page.

Is CMC Markets Safe to Trade With?

I concluded that CMC Markets is very safe to trade with due to the following factors: 

  • Authorized by multiple Tier-1 regulators
  • Has a âbest execution policyâ
  • Has transparent legal documents

Fees

CMC Markets offers industry-leading spreads on assets like forex and CFDs on commodities and indices. Overnight financing costs are standard for the industry, and we found no hidden expenses that might surprise traders. The broker offers commission-free trading, except for share CFDs.

CMC Markets Trading Fees

CMC Markets Spreads

I tested CMC Marketsâ spreads on 3 July 2024 during the London and the New York open. The results are shown in the table below:

Broken down by asset class and compared to the industry average, CMC Markets offers low spreads on share CFDs, low-to-average spreads on currency pairs and indices, and average spreads on commodities. 

CMC Markets Swaps

A swap fee is a traderâs cost for holding an open position overnight because of changing interest rates. Swap long refers to the charge deductible or credit receivable for holding a buy position open overnight. In turn, swap short relates to the charges/credits deductible or receivable for holding a selling position open overnight.

CMC Markets Non-Trading Fees

CMC Markets does not charge a handling fee for deposits and withdrawals. There is, however, a GBP 10 inactivity fee charged on dormant accounts. 

Accounts Comparison

I have compiled the table below to help you better understand the difference between the trading fees of CFC Marketsâ two retail trading accounts and the industry average. It illustrates the spreads and commissions I have recorded for the EUR/USD pair and compares them against the typical costs for ECN and STP accounts in the industry at large. 

The table demonstrates how much you would have to pay to trade 1 full lot (100,000 units) in EUR/USD with a pip value of $10 for each account.

Based on my research, the CMC Marketsâ two retail account types beat the industry average by quite a bit. This combination of commission-free trading (except for share CFDs) and raw spreads from 0.5 pips is suitable for all kinds of trading strategies.

Are CMC Marketsâ Fees Competitive?

Overall, I was impressed by the fees at CMC Markets and especially by the tight spreads, which are highly important to traders. The spread reflects the costs of entering and exiting trades. For an active trader, this cost can often make the difference between being profitable or suffering losses at the end of the day.  

Platforms and Tools

CMC Markets offers its proprietary Next Generation platform via web and mobile. Clients can also trade via MetaTrader 4 on desktop, web, and mobile.

Platform/Tool Suitable For
Next Generation Advanced technical analysis, order placing, automated trading
MetaTrader 4 Basic technical analysis, order execution, technical analysis 

The Next Generation Platform

CMC Marketsâ Next Generation platform certainly lived up to its name. Testing its many features was a breeze, and I assessed that the platform could be used to carry out comprehensive technical analysis. This is made possible due to the fluidity of its charts, supplemented with a wide array of analytical tools.

The Next Generation platform offers built-in chart pattern recognition tools. The idea is that you can scan multiple instruments and timeframes for classic chart patterns that may have predictive value. The patterns recognized are mostly basic ones, such as triangles, wedges, and double tops/bottoms. The more sophisticated Head and Shoulders pattern can also be identified.

A client sentiment tool lets you know what other clients within the platform are trading and whether they are long (buyers) or short (sellers). Sentiment can be viewed across the whole client base or just among the top-performing traders. Sentiment is usually used as a contrarian indicator.

General Ease of Use

At the core of CMC Marketsâ offering is its proprietary web-based Next Generation platform. The platform has a clean, easy-to-use interface along with advanced functionality, making it suitable for beginners as well as experienced traders.

Charts

Charting within the Next Generation Platform is robust and easy to use. Charts include the following features:

  • 115 technical indicators: These are categorized into Overlays and Studies. Overlays include indicators like moving averages, Bollinger Bands, and Keltner Channels, which sit on top of charts. Studies encompass indicators such as MACD, RSI, and various oscillators, typically shown beneath charts. These overlays and studies can be easily added from the bottom of the chart, making the process smooth and intuitive for beginners.
  • 13 chart types: These include classic formats like Japanese Candlesticks and Bar charts, as well as more exotic Kagi and Renko charts.
  • 40 drawing tools: Ranging from basic trend lines and channels to various Fibonacci and Gartley tools. These tools are visually represented beneath the chart for easy understanding and use.
  • 17 time frames: Ranging from 1 second to 1 week, allowing traders to analyze specific periods. One-minute charts show price movements for each minute, hourly charts for each hour, and so forth. You can also select the total time period for the chart, from 1 day to a maximum that varies by instrument. For example, gold data goes back 26 years to 1996.

The layout of charts within the platform is easily customizable, and there are a variety of preset layouts you can select if you want to watch the charts of multiple markets at once.

Orders

The platform offers an above-average range of order types for placing trades. Traders can choose between the following orders:

  • Market orders: This order type is used to open or close trades at the current market price.
  • Limit orders: Limit orders are used to enter or exit the market at a specific price.
  • Stop-loss orders: Here you can specify the price at which a position will be closed if the market moves adversely.
  • Trailing stop-loss orders: This type of stop-loss order follows the market price as it moves in your favor. It remains at a set distance from the current price, allowing you to lock in profits.
  • Guaranteed stop-loss orders: GSLOs provide certainty that your stop-loss will be executed at your desired price. However, an additional charge can be applied.
  • Boundary orders: For use in fast markets, this order type allows you to set a price range that you are willing to accept to ensure that your trade is executed.

Time-in-force conditions can be applied to orders. For example, if you are entering a limit order to buy gold at a price below where the market is trading, you can either mark the order GTC (good âtil canceled) or set a specific expiry date for your order.

My Key Takeaways After Testing the Next Generation Web Trader Platform

It was a breeze to test CMC Marketsâ proprietary platform. I especially enjoyed using its advanced charting capabilities. The high level of detail displayed makes price action examinations especially easy. 

CMC Marketsâ Mobile App

The CMC Markets mobile app has a great user interface and is packed with functionality similar to that of the web platform. Over 12,000 instruments are available to trade. Charts are optimized for mobile and offer 25 technical indicators and 15 drawing tools. You can place, edit, and close trades directly from charts.

The appâs order tickets allow users to place the full range of order types, including guaranteed stop-loss orders and trailing stops. Biometric (fingerprint) and two-step login are available.

My Key Takeaways After Testing CMC Marketsâ Mobile App

The CMC Markets mobile app is intuitive and feature-rich, delivering a great experience for traders on the move. I appreciated its light design and intuitive layout. The start screen is customizable to suit your preferences. You can also set up push notifications, SMS, or email alerts on your orders or price levels.

However, you canât be logged into mobile or web platforms at the same time. Another drawback is that charts do not automatically sync with the way you have them set up in the web platform.

MetaTrader 4

MetaTrader is a powerful platform with impressive features but the interface appears dated in comparison with the Next Generation Platform. What distinguishes MetaTrader is its ability to perform strategy backtesting and automated trading.

Key Features

The platform provides popular features such as:

  • Alerts. This feature allows traders to be updated when an instrument reaches a specific price level. Alerts can be delivered via audio, an email, or a push notification to a mobile device.
  • Watchlists. Traders can set up a list of their favorite instruments and follow live quotes in a panel called Market Watch.
  • One-click trading. This feature allows traders to execute orders with a single click and no secondary confirmation. Being able to place a trade with a single click saves time and is especially useful for short term traders.
  • Trading from the chart. MT4 also allows users the convenience of trading directly from the chart.

Order Types

MetaTrader also delivers when it comes to the range of available order types and its charting functionality. The following order types are available:

  • Market Order. This is an order to buy or sell an instrument at the current best available price.
  • Limit Order. This is an order to buy or sell an instrument at a specified price or better.
  • Stop Loss Order. This is an order to buy or sell an instrument that is triggered when price reaches a specified level.
  • Trailing Stop Order. This is a stop loss order that can be set at a defined percentage or dollar amount away from an instrumentâs current market price. It is used to secure profits when you are in a winning trade, while not having to exit the position.

Charting

Charting features are robust. MetaTrader 4 offers:

  • 30 technical indicators. These include classic trend indicators, volume indicators and oscillators.
  • 23 analytical objects. These include lines, channels, Gann and Fibonacci tools.
  • 9 time frames Each instrument can be displayed in nine time frames, from one minute to one month.
  • 3 chart types. Traders can choose between Bar Charts, Japanese Candlestick Charts and Line Charts.

Advanced Features

MetaTrader is also popular due to its copy trading and automated trading features.

  • Trading Signals. Signals in MetaTrader 4 allow users to automatically copy the activity of other traders in real time.
  • Automated trading. MetaTrader 4 allows users to develop, test and apply Expert Advisors (EAs). EAs are programs that monitor and trade markets using algorithms. They find opportunities according to set parameters and then either create a notification or automatically open a trade.

To conclude, the MetaTrader 4 desktop platform is one of the most feature-rich and popular trading platforms in the world. It does not have the best design and it does require some time and effort to learn, but that is typical of advanced platforms.

Order Execution

CMC Markets is a dealing desk/market maker broker, meaning that they set the bid (buy) and offer (sell) prices internally and automatically take the other side of a clientâs trade. This contrasts with STP/ECN brokers who provide clients direct access to other market participants. (STP stands for straight-through processing, and ECN stands for electronic communications network.)

Tradable Instruments

CMC Markets impresses with its wide and diverse array of more than 12,000 tradable and investing assets. Traders can choose from currency pairs, commodities, share CFDs, indices, cryptocurrencies, and treasuries.

Markets Amount Industry Average

CMC Marketsâ instruments offering beats the industry average for every asset class.

In the UK, cryptocurrencies are only available to clients with professional accounts. This restriction stems from the FCAâs January 2021 ban on the sale of crypto-derivatives to retail consumers.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives used to speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical delivery.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

What Can You Trade With CMC Markets?

My Key Takeaways After Exploring CMC Marketsâ Instruments Offering

CMC Markets offers an impressive number of commonly traded assets and exotic instruments. Forex and commodity traders, in particular, stand to benefit from the brokerâs rare instruments on offer. My only gripe is that there are few alternatives to CFDs, such as futures contracts and vanilla options.

Customer Support

CMC Markets offers support via email, chat, and phone. Its quality is high, although there is still room for improvement, especially with the waiting times for responses via chat. Chat and local phone support are available 24 hours a day from Monday to Friday.

Customer Support Channels

Live Chat Email Phone
24/5 from the website

Online form:

clientmanagement@cmcmarkets.co.uk 

 +44 (0)20 7170 8200  

Customer Support Test

When we test a brokerâs customer support, we evaluate the agentâs knowledge of their own website, how long it takes them to respond to questions, and how detailed their answers are.

When testing support via chat, I experienced a short delay and was placed in a queue. Although the wait time was brief, it was noticeably longer compared to market leaders, where responses are typically immediate. However, phone support had virtually no wait time, and email inquiries were answered within 1 business day.

We tested support with a variety of questions. These ranged from basic, such as âAre funds segregated?â to more unusual inquiries, such as âDoes CMC Markets offer VWAP?â Overall, we received a good quality response in a timely fashion. 

Available Languages 
English, French, German, Italian, Polish, Spanish, Swedish, Other

Deposits & Withdrawals

Deposits and withdrawals are free and can be made via credit card, PayPal, or bank wire. Payments can be made using Visa, Mastercard, and Maestro credit/debit cards, PayPal, or bank wire. Deposits via credit card or PayPal are immediate, but withdrawals can take as much as 5 business days.

*With credit card and PayPal, you can only withdraw as much as you deposited. Excess profits must be withdrawn via bank transfer.

We judged the speed of deposits and withdrawals at CMC Markets to be average for the industry.

Account Types and Terms

CMC Markets offers three account types: CFD, Corporate, and Spread Betting. Opening an account is straightforward and can be done online within 20 minutes. For clients in the UK, an important difference between spread betting and CFD trading is how they are taxed. Profits from spread betting are free from capital gains tax. Spread betting is also only available to clients in the UK or Ireland, while CFDs are available worldwide.

CMC Markets Account Opening Process

To set up an account with CMC Markets, follow these easy steps:

  • Step 1: Enter your email and set up a password. 
  • Step 2: Verify your email by using the code you are sent. 
  • Step 3: Enter your personal details. 
  • Step 4: Choose an account type. 
  • Step 5: State your financial background and employment status. 
  • Step 6: Explain your trading experience and reason for opening an account. 
  • Step 7: Verify your account by uploading proof of address and ID. 

CMC Markets Account Types

Spread From 0.0 pips 0.0 pips 0.0 pips

Demo Account Yes Yes Yes

The CFD Trading account is perfectly calibrated for experienced and novice traders. There is no minimum deposit requirement, making it quite accessible. Additionally, the combination of commission-free trading and raw spreads from 0.5 pips is extremely favorable.

Demo Accounts

CMC Markets offers a demo account that introduces traders to the brokerâs services and allows them to tweak their strategies in a risk-free environment. The market is continually evolving and never static, so it is important to hone your skills in a safe environment. You can set up a demo account along with a live CFD account.

Islamic Account

CMC Markets does not offer Islamic accounts for swap-free trading.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that the latter can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Maximum Leverage By Asset Class

In the table below, I have listed the maximum retail leverage available with CMC Markets for instruments from different asset classes:

Asset Class Maximum Leverage
Currency Pairs 1:30

Supported Countries

CMC Markets accepts clients from Australia, Austria, Bahamas, Bahrein, British Virgin Islands, Bulgaria, Canada, Cayman Islands, Chile, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Guernsey, Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Isle of Man, Israel, Italy, Jersey, Jordan, Kuwait, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxemburg, Malta, Monaco, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Oman, Peru, Philippines, Portugal, Qatar, Republic of Korea, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Seychelles, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, United Arabic, Emirates, United Kingdom, Vietnam.

Research

CMC excels in the research content that includes quality in-house analysis, third-party materials, and extensive video programming. The broker affords comprehensive coverage of current market developments and trading opportunities. I found the content easily digestible.

Research Tools

Market Insights

Market insights are provided throughout the day on the Next Generation Platform, with a variety of different reports, including:

  • Morning call. This brief report examines the news stories and economic data that could move the market in the day ahead.
  • Intraday insights. This recaps the results of important economic releases and other news.
  • Evening call. A more in-depth report covering the major stories of the day. Analysis is broken down by region (US and Europe) and by market (forex and commodities).
  • Breaking news. Covers market-moving news such as earnings releases and the reaction to it.
  • Price mover. This report focuses on trading instruments that are making big moves that day. Particularly useful to day traders, who often look for opportunities in markets experiencing unusual short-term volatility.

Blog

The blog on the CMC Markets website is frequently updated, with roughly five economic and market news stories posted per day. These stories range from in-depth analyses of specific stocks, indices, and sectors to forecasts of how upcoming economic data could impact the market.

Video Content

CMC TV, hosted on YouTube, features live coverage of headline economic events such as Non-farm Payrolls, central bank meetings, and major earnings releases. These video sessions range from roughly 30 to 45 minutes in length and also include technical analysis of the relevant charts.

My Key Takeaways After Exploring CMC Marketsâ Research Content

Research content with CMC Markets is rich and nuanced. The broker goes above and beyond to offer its clients powerful insights and actionable trading breakdowns, which can help them achieve consistent results. 

Education

CMC Markets is a leader in trading education, offering a wide range of materials, including articles, videos, podcasts, and webinars. Beginners can gain extensive insights into trading, and I especially appreciated the attention paid to technical analysis, fundamental analysis, and the psychology of trading.

Educational articles on the website, such as âHow to Trade Bitcoinâ and âWhat is a trailing stop order?â, help guide traders. More advanced guides that go deep into specific trading strategies, like momentum trading and price action trading, are especially useful.

Webinars cater to both beginners and experienced traders and cover topics ranging from the outlook for the global markets to making the most of the Next Generation trading platform. They take place weekly and are archived on the CMC Markets YouTube channel.

The Opto Sessions Podcast features interviews with industry experts, covering topics like value investing or investing in a specific sector such as software. These weekly podcasts are a great way to broaden your knowledge in a passive way, for example, while driving your car.

The Bottom Line

CMC Markets is a pioneer and market leader in the forex and CFD industry. As a large, extensively regulated, publicly traded company, it offers stability and diverse services. The proprietary Next Generation platform boasts advanced functionality and an attractive, user-friendly interface.

The depth of the product catalog places this broker in an elite group, and active traders will especially appreciate its tight spreads. Education and research offerings are strong, and customer service, while not always the fastest, is reliable.

These factors make CMC Markets an all-around winner and an appealing choice for both beginners and advanced traders.

chunked.content:
Our Take on CMC Markets

CMC Markets is a CFD and Spread Betting broker founded in 1989 and based in the UK. The company is listed on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) under the ticker symbol CMCX. CMC Markets is overseen by multiple regulators worldwide, including FCA, ASIC, IIROC, and others.

The broker stands out for its flagship Next Generation trading platform, very competitive spreads, and the collection of over 12,000 tradable instruments. Additionally, CMC Markets offers top-notch research and educational resources.

I concluded that CMC Markets is suitable for traders with different experience levels and a variety of trading styles.

CMC Markets Pros and Cons

Pros Cons
  • Multiple regulated globally
  • Competitive spreads and fees
  • Outstanding range of tradable instruments
  • Strong research resources
  • Cutting-edge platform
  • Spread betting
  • Inactivity fee of Â£10 a month (no deductions are made if there are no funds in the account)
  • No cryptocurrencies
  • No Islamic account

Is CMC Markets Right For You?

When reviewing a broker, we assess its suitability for implementing various trading strategies. To achieve this, we evaluate the availability of features and tools necessary for executing specific strategies. Below, I have evaluated CMC Marketsâ performance for each category:

Casual Trading: Perfect Match

CMC Markets does not require a minimum deposit, making its accounts quite affordable. It also offers raw spreads from 0.5 pips and supports commission-free trading (except for share CFDs). Finally, it provides robust support content and reliable customer support, making it a perfect choice for casual trading.

Social and Copy Trading: Not Recommended

CMC Markets does not support copy and social trading.

Swing Trading: Acceptable Choice

The broker has an intuitive trading platform, a variety of trading instruments from different markets, and very competitive fees. However, its overnight charges are quite elevated.

Day Trading: Perfect Match

Day traders can benefit from CMC Marketsâ competitive trading fees, penetrating research materials, and feature-rich proprietary platform to carry out comprehensive technical analysis.

Scalping: Acceptable Choice

The broker achieves fast average execution speeds, successfully fills most client orders, and offers an excellent proprietary platform with advanced charting capabilities. The only thing preventing it from scoring higher in this category was the absence of VPS hosting.

News Trading: Acceptable Choice

The risk of negative slippage with CMC Markets is small. Additionally, it offers penetrating market research and very competitive trading fees â the essential conditions for successful news trading. However, including third-party research content would make its market research more nuanced.

Automated Trading: Acceptable Choice

CMC Markets achieves fast order execution speeds and offers a variety of trading instruments. The only thing lacking is VPS, which facilitates low-latency trading and average execution speeds below 3 milliseconds.

Investing: Perfect Match

The broker offers a variety of instruments on which traders can invest and earn revenue. It also provides a well-rounded market overview, helping its clients spot viable investing opportunities.

What Sets CMC Markets Apart?

Being a heavyweight in the forex and CFD industry listed on the London exchange, CMC Markets combines a superior proprietary trading platform that boasts a range of advanced tools with affordable accounts offering no minimum deposit requirement, very competitive spreads, and no commissions. Additionally, the broker offers excellent research tools and educational content to hone your trading skills.

I opened a CFD Account with the CMC Markets UK PLC entity and performed my tests using the Next Generation Platform and mobile app. Some of the features and services will vary depending on which jurisdiction you open an account in.

DB Investing Regulators

When reviewing brokers, we examine the licenses held by each of their entities to determine how effectively they protect clients. We use a simple three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier 1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about the three entities operating under the DB Investing trade name:

  • DB Invest Limited is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Authority (FSA) of the Seychelles under license number SD053. We rate the FSA as a Tier-3 regulator.
  • DB Pay Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under license number M22286159. We rate FINTRAC as a Tier-1 regulator.
  • DBInvest Financial Services LLC is licensed and regulated by the Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA) of the UAE under license number 20200000197. We rate the SCA as a Tier-2 regulator.
  • DB Invest (MY) Limited is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) of Mauritius under license number GB25204845. We rate the FSC as a Tier-3 regulator.

How Does DB Investing Protect You?

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is how DB Investing protects you:

  • Holds client funds in segregated accounts.
  • Guarantees negative balance protection.
  • Operates on a best execution policy.
  • Provides insurance coverage.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, click here.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

According to DB Investingâs LinkedIn page, the broker has been around for 7 years and now employs over 100 people worldwideâa good sign of stability and a solid business model.

One thing that really stood out to me was the brokerâs detailed risk notice for EU clients. Most brokers just put up a short disclaimer saying they donât accept clients from specific regions, but DB Investing actually breaks down the differences between EU rules and those under FSA regulation. That level of transparency is rare and definitely a plus.

I also liked the way DB Investing categorizes new clients during account setup. It ensures traders get the services that best match their needs. On top of that, the broker has a âbest execution policy,â which means itâs legally bound to give you the best possible price quotes under current market conditions.

The only major downside I found is that DB Investing doesnât display daily swap rates on MT5. For swing traders, thatâs a big gap since it makes it harder to know the exact cost of holding positions overnight.

Fees

My testing revealed that DB Investingâs STP account spreads were higher than the industry average across most instruments, except for BTCUSD, which was in line with the benchmark. On the plus side, the broker doesnât charge commissions or fees on deposits and withdrawals. However, it does apply a $25 inactivity fee after 60 days of no trading, which is relatively high compared to industry standards.

DB Investing Swaps

A swap fee is a traderâs cost for holding an open position overnight because of changing interest rates. Swap long refers to the charge deductible or credit receivable for holding a buy position open overnight. In turn, swap short relates to the charges/credits deductible or receivable for holding a selling position open overnight.

DB Investing does not display data on daily swaps, so I was unable to measure its overnight charges. However, the websiteâs âContract Specsâ page states that the broker charges a â3% per yearâ swap long and swap short. This means that swing traders with DB Investing cannot receive credit for holding positions overnight due to changing interest rates.

DB Investing Non-Trading Fees

DB Investing doesnât charge any fees for deposits or withdrawals, though your bank or payment provider might add their own charges.

On the other hand, the broker does charge an inactivity fee: $25 if your account remains idle for 60 days. Thatâs on the high side for such a short period, and itâs charged monthly until you start trading again or your balance drops to zero.

Are DB Investingâs Fees Competitive?

On the positive side, the broker doesnât charge for deposits or withdrawals, though the inactivity fee is relatively steep and kicks in after 60 days without trading.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I tested the MetaTrader 5 (MT5) desktop platform and found it relatively easy to navigate. The main dashboard is intuitive, with charts, order types, and trading instruments located in familiar places. Even first-time users can grasp the basics with minimal effort.

However, the platform design feels a bit outdated. Compared to more modern trading platforms, MT5âs chart visuals are rugged and lack the sleek, polished look that many traders today prefer.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by DB Investing is available for Windows and Mac users and supports 52 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese â making it accessible to traders around the globe.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

In my opinion, MT5 excels particularly in automated trading. It supports Expert Advisors (EAs) and comes with an easy-to-use strategy tester, enabling algorithmic traders to fine-tune their systems for various market conditions.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is loaded with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format.

That said, the charts can get visually cluttered quite fast â even when only two indicators are active. This can make it harder to interpret price action clearly and may not be ideal for traders who rely heavily on clean, minimalistic chart setups.

Order Types

Placing an order on MetaTrader 5

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a solid platform for fast and straightforward trading, particularly if youâre into algorithmic strategies or use EAs. Itâs reliable, packed with tools, and supports detailed trade execution.

However, its interface feels dated compared to more modern alternatives like TradingView or cTrader. If youâre a trader who values sleek design and customizable charting, MT5 might feel a bit too rigid and visually overwhelming.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

DB Investing Execution Model

DB Investing operates on a hybrid STP/ECN model without a dealing desk. Client orders are either routed to the brokerâs pool of liquidity providers, where they are filled at the best possible price, or they are matched electronically using communications networks. This means that buying orders are matched with selling orders, and vice versa.

The lineup covers currency pairs, commodities, share CFDs, indices, cryptocurrencies, ETFs, and bonds. The ETF and bond selection is especially impressive, coming in larger than what many competitors provide.

What Are CFDs?

CFDs (Contracts for Difference) let you trade on the price movements of assetsâlike goldâwithout actually owning them.

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you loseâwithout ever buying real gold.

The biggest perk? You can jump in or out of the market quickly to take advantage of even the smallest price changes.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Research

DB Investing delivers solid market research with tools like an easy-to-use economic calendar, a regularly updated news screener, in-depth market breakdowns, and featured trading ideas. Some of the content is developed in-house, while other insights come from AI-driven providers such as Acuity and Perplexity Finance.

Research Tools

  • Economic Calendar: The economic calendar informs traders of upcoming market events and economic releases that have the potential to stir a market reaction and therefore create viable trading opportunities.

• Market News: The websiteâs market news segment represents an intuitive news screener. It filters the latest market news from major media outlets and delivers quick and highly informative breakdowns of current market developments to DB Investingâs clients.

• Signal Centre: The package is integrated from the data-driven Acuity service, which generates AI-powered trading signals. Traders are given entry, stop, and target levels, as well as a confidence barometer.

• Perplexity Finance: Perplexity Finance provides traders with a broad overview of market sentiment and highlights the top gainers and losers. It also lets you customize watchlists and dig deeper with thorough fundamental analysis, making it a handy tool for spotting key market drivers.

DB Investing Research: My Key Takeaways

I found DB Investingâs research both practical and fairly sophisticated. It works well for day traders who want to spot unfolding setups, as well as for those who prefer a broader market perspective. I especially liked the mix of in-house insights and third-party tools. The only drawback is the lack of video-based research content.

Education

DB Investing conducts periodic educational webinars and has published several e-books and video platform tutorials in multiple languages. However, the content only scratches the surface of the ABCs of trading and lacks depth.

DB Investing offers 14 platform tutorials in English, Arabic, Hindi, and Bengali that walk traders through the different features of MetaTrader 5. I also found nine written guides covering topics like how to set up FIX API or the basics of forex trading.

That said, the broker falls short of offering real educational depth. There are no detailed articles or videos on the essentials of technical or fundamental analysis, trading psychology, or risk managementâtopics that many traders would expect from a solid education package.

The Bottom Line

After testing DB Investing hands-on, Iâd say itâs a reliable and versatile broker that really shines when it comes to its huge product lineup (especially MENA stocks and ETFs) and advanced trading tools like FIX API and social trading. Its research offering is also a big plus, with a smart mix of in-house analysis and AI-driven insights.

That said, traders need to weigh the higher-than-average spreads and the steep inactivity fee against the benefits. Education is also on the lighter side compared to what many top brokers provide.

All in all, DB Investing is a strong pick for active traders, scalpers, and those looking for regional stock exposure, while casual beginners might find better fee structures and deeper learning resources elsewhere.

Our Take on DB Investing

DB Investing is a Dubai-based broker that has been operating globally since 2018. It stands out with its extensive lineup of over 2,600 CFDs, 170+ real stocks, and a rare selection of MENA shares, which few brokers offer.

On the tools side, DB Investing runs on MetaTrader 5, offers a FIX API for low-latency trading, and has even built its own social and copy trading app, which connects a large community of over 370,000 traders. Its research package is also strong, blending in-house insights with AI-driven signals from Acuity and analysis from Perplexity Finance.

The trade-off comes with costs. Spreads are higher than the industry average, and while there are no commissions, the brokerâs $25 inactivity fee after 60 days feels steep. Education is another weak pointâDB Investing mostly sticks to platform guides and beginner-level material, lacking the depth that rivals offer.

Overall, Iâd say DB Investing is an excellent fit for scalpers, hedgers, and high-frequency traders. Compared to the industry, it excels in its asset variety and trading technology, but lags behind in pricing and in-depth learning resources.

How Deriv Protects You

Brokers operate through various entities to serve clients worldwide; however, the level of regulatory protection varies by jurisdiction. Each broker is required to comply with the legal requirements of the jurisdiction in which they operate.

Some regulators enforce strict financial and operational standards, while others have more relaxed requirements. As a result, protections for traders can vary. Traders need to understand the regulatory framework and level of protection provided by the specific entity where they open their account.

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All Deriv entities follow this practice.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. All Deriv entities provide negative balance protection (for applicable clients).
  • Compensation Scheme: Deriv is a member of the Financial Commission. The Financial Commission protects clients by providing independent dispute resolution and compensation of up to â¬20,000 if a Deriv fails to honor its obligations.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. Deriv (SVG) LLC offers leverage of up to 1:1000.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Deriv was founded in 1999, marking it as one of the oldest and most experienced CFD brokers. According to its LinkedIn page, the company is headquartered in Malta and has over 1,000 employees.

In my research, Deriv showed high transparency in its regulatory status, listing its regulators in the footer of each page of the deriv.com website. The website clearly breaks down trading costs on the CFDs page. Traders can easily find the General Terms of Use agreement on the Terms and Conditions page, listed in the footer.

Is Deriv Safe to Trade With?

Although one of the Derivâs entities is unregulated, my findings indicate that the broker can be regarded as having a moderate to high level of trustworthiness and stability due to the following factors:

  • Regulation by multiple authorities
  • Segregation of client funds
  • Negative balance protection
  • Financial Commission coverage
  • Over 25 years of operational history

Fees

Deriv doesnât charge commissions across all its accounts. However, my hands-on tests showed that its spreads on the Standard MT5 account range from average to high. Swap fees were also average for the industry. Although Deriv does not charge fees for deposits or withdrawals, it does apply an inactivity fee.
