DLSM Regulations

In our reviews, we examine the licenses and regulations of each entity operated by a broker, allowing us to compare their different levels of protection. We rank licenses by various regulatory bodies on a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing indicates the highest level of regulation.

This is what I discovered about the DLSM trade name:

  • DLS Markets Limited is licensed and regulated by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) under license number 700455. We rate the VFSC as a Tier-3 regulator.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity they choose to open an account with.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Client funds are kept in segregated accounts from the companyâs corporate capital with DLSM.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance for retail clients. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. The broker does not guarantee negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. DLSM is a member of the Financial Commission resolution scheme, and its clients are protected by up to EUR 20,000.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with DLSM is 1:1000.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

DLSM is a relatively new broker, founded in 2020, and has yet to establish itself as a trustworthy partner. Its company size appears small, with only 6 associated members on its LinkedIn page. Beyond that, I appreciated that DLSM publishes a live spread feed on the website so that visitors can quickly asses its fee transparency and competitiveness.

I also checked its legal documents, including the client agreement, and assessed that everything was in order. All important information is readily available and easy to discern.

Is DLSM Safe to Trade With?

  • Participates in The Financial Commission
  • Keeps client funds in segregated accounts

I tested the desktop version of the MetaTrader 5 platform, which offers several essential tools, including one-click trading, an alarm setting option, and a market depth tool. These features enable traders to analyze market developments from multiple perspectives and take advantage of trading opportunities in various ways.

In my opinion, MT5 is best suited for automated trading via Expert Advisors (EAs). The platform also has an intuitive strategy tester, allowing experienced algo traders to tweak the parameters of their strategies so that they can be used under different market conditions.

MT5 Features

DLSMâs MT5 platform is available on Windows and Mac and supports 52 languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Arabic, Chinese, and more.

MT5 features include:

  • Alerts-Setting Option: Traders can set alerts for when the price of a given instrument falls/rises to a predetermined level, which could potentially signal a viable entry opportunity.
  • Watchlist Customization: Traders can populate watchlists with their favorite instruments and track market changes more easily.
  • One-click Trading: This feature enables instant market entries at the spot price and is invaluable for high-precision traders, such as scalpers.
  • Trading from the Chart: Traders can place conventional trading orders directly from the chart, specifying the entry price, volume level, stop and take-profit levels, and more.

Charts

A common issue with MetaTrader is that charts can quickly become cluttered, even with just two indicators. This can obscure price action examination and make it harder to perform detailed technical analysis.

I have broken down the available analytical tools and chart configurations below:

  • 38 technical indicators: This includes trend-based and volume-based indicators and oscillators to analyze price action and assess market sentiment, helping predict market movements.
  • 24 drawing tools: Tools like Fibonacci retracement levels and Elliott waves help identify price patterns, support/resistance levels, and breakout points. However, MT5âs design can make price action harder to interpret.
  • 21 timeframes: For multi-timeframe analysis, enabling detailed price action analysis.
  • 3 chart types: Price action can be displayed as line, bars, or candlesticks, offering diverse perspectives on trading opportunities.

The chart screen is undeniably one of the most crucial features of a trading platform. It equips traders with essential tools and configurations to analyze price action and spot trading opportunities. Just as important is the ability to easily scale price action, allowing for a clearer and more detailed view of market movements.

Orders

MetaTrader 5 features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which allows for immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the MetaTrader 5 platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a good option for fast and simple order execution. However, its dated and rugged design is inferior to newer and sleeker platforms. As a trader who prioritizes flexible charts that are easily scalable, I find MT5âs charting capability too rigid and less effective.

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for Difference (CFDs) are financial derivative instruments that allow traders to speculate on the price movements of an asset without owning the asset itself.

For instance, taking a long position in gold would result in a profit for the trader if the price goes up or, respectively, a loss if the price goes down. The opposite would be true for a short position in gold.

A key advantage of trading CFDs is the ability to enter and exit the market almost instantly, enabling traders to capitalize on even minor price fluctuations in the derivative.

DLSMâs blog features 63 articles covering a range of trading topics, including platform tutorials and strategy guides. While the content is somewhat insightful, it remains the only educational resource available. Without additional learning materials, I think beginners may struggle to build a well-rounded understanding of trading and will likely need to seek external resources to fill the gaps.

The Bottom Line

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Vanuatu, DLSM is a rising player in the financial derivatives space that operates globally and offers 120+ tradable instruments.

DLSM runs on MT4 and MT5, fully supports copy and algorithmic trading, and integrates market research from Trading Central. When it comes to costs, its fees are fair, even beating the industry average in some cases. I found its ECN account particularly competitive, making it a solid choice for traders looking for low-cost execution.

However, DLSMâs range of tradable assets is quite narrow, and its educational content lacks depth.

While DLSM is still establishing its reputation, I rate it as a decent option for casual traders and those interested in copy trading. Thereâs potential here, but it has yet to prove itself as a top-tier broker.

Doto operates four entities licensed and regulated by the FSCA, CySEC, FSC (Mauritius), and the FSA (Seychelles). The broker keeps client funds in segregated accounts and guarantees negative balance protection. I also found that Doto is a member of The Financial Commission and maintains transparent legal documents.

Doto Regulators

When reviewing brokers, we examine the licenses held by each of their entities to assess how effectively they protect clients. We use a simple three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier-1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about the four entities operating under the Doto trade name:

  • Doto South Africa (Pty) Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Conduct Authority (FSCA) of South Africa under license number 50451. We rate the FSCA as a Tier-2 regulator.
  • Doto Europe Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) under license number 399/21. We rate CySEC as a Tier-1 regulator.
  • Doto Global Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) of Mauritius under license number C119023978. We rate the FSC as a Tier-3 regulator.
  • Doto International Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Authority (FSA) of the Seychelles under license number SD0063. We rate the FSA as a Tier-3 regulator. This entity does not onboard retail clients.

How Does Doto Protect You?

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the entityâs safety measures before opening an account.

Here is how Doto South Africa (Pty) Ltd protects you:

â Segregated accounts â Client funds are kept separate from the companyâs own capital.

â Compensation scheme â In case of insolvency, your funds will be reimbursed up to EUR 20,000 under The Financial Commission.

â Negative balance protection â Your losses cannot exceed your invested capital.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, check out our dedicated guide on client protections.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

I looked into Dotoâs background and found that the broker has been around since 2019, employing over 51-200 professionals worldwide, according to its LinkedIn page.

I also discovered that Doto is a member of The Financial Commission, a respected dispute resolution body for forex brokers and their clients. This membership provides an additional layer of protection, offering compensation of up to EUR 20,000 in the event of broker insolvency.

My only concern about transparency is the absence of a live spreads feed on the website, which helps casual visitors to the website assess the brokerâs fee transparency and competitiveness.

Is Doto Safe?

I concluded that Doto is sufficiently safe to trade with due to the following factors:

  • Licensed by four global regulators.
  • Protects client funds from the brokerâs credit risk.
  • Ensures negative balance protection.
  • Participates in the Financial Commission resolution scheme.

Fees

I found that Dotoâs fees are a bit of a mixed bag. The good news is that it doesnât charge commissions and keeps spreads on forex and share CFDs quite competitive. However, during my testing, spreads on gold and indices were noticeably higher, and overnight fees also exceeded the industry average. On the plus side, deposits and withdrawals are free, though inactive accounts get hit with a $15 dormancy fee.

Doto Spreads

Doto Swaps

A swap fee is the cost of keeping a trade open overnight, and itâs tied to the difference in interest rates between the two currencies in a pair. If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

Live testing revealed that Dotoâs overnight fees exceeded the industry benchmark for all instruments I tested. While its EURUSD swap long was only marginally higher than the industry average, its XAUUSD swap was one of the highest I have ever recorded.

However, swaps tend to fluctuate over time.

Doto Non-Trading Fees

Doto charges a $15 inactivity fee to dormant accounts after six months of no trading activity. The fee is applied monthly until you resume trading or your account balance reaches zero.

The broker does not impose a handling fee for deposits or withdrawals; however, third-party processing fees may still apply.

Are Dotoâs Fees Competitive?

Dotoâs fees are mixed and vary in competitiveness. On the one hand, its forex and share CFD spreads are competitive, but the spreads on indices and gold were quite high. Doto also charges elevated swaps, but its non-trading charges are kept at a minimum.

Platforms and Tools

Doto has developed a versatile and feature-rich trading platform that combines advanced TradingView charting with AI-driven market insights. The platform offers integrated market analytics and a trading calendar that keeps users informed about important global events and data releases. The platform is also available on mobile devices. For traders seeking a more familiar interface, Doto offers both MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5.

MetaTrader 4 (Web, desktop, mobile) Easy order execution, basic technical analysis, automated trading, and trading on the go
MetaTrader 5 (Web, desktop, mobile) Easy order execution, basic technical analysis, automated trading, and trading on the go

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I tested the MetaTrader 5 (MT5) desktop platform and found it relatively easy to navigate. The main dashboard is intuitive, with charts, order types, and trading instruments located in familiar places. Even first-time users can grasp the basics with minimal effort.

However, the platformâs design feels somewhat outdated. Compared to more modern trading platforms, MT5âs chart visuals are rugged and lack the sleek, polished look that many traders today prefer.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by Doto is available for Windows and Mac users and supports 39 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese â making it accessible to traders around the globe.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

In my view, MT5 really shines when it comes to automated trading. It supports Expert Advisors (EAs) and comes with an easy-to-use strategy tester, allowing algo traders to fine-tune their systems for different market conditions.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is loaded with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format.

That said, the charts can get visually cluttered quite fast â even when only two indicators are active. This can make it harder to interpret price action clearly and may not be ideal for traders who rely heavily on clean, minimalistic chart setups.

Order Types

Placing an order on MetaTrader 5

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a solid platform for fast and straightforward trading, particularly if youâre into algorithmic strategies or use EAs. Itâs reliable, packed with tools, and supports detailed trade execution.

However, its interface feels dated compared to more modern alternatives like TradingView or cTrader. If youâre a trader who values sleek design and customizable charting, MT4 might feel a bit too rigid and visually overwhelming.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

Doto Web Platform

Dotoâs flagship web platform is a major step up from MetaTrader, thanks to its TradingView-powered charting suite. Price action is displayed in greater detail and can be scaled smoothly, while traders have access to over 100 analytical tools and chart configurations for deeper technical analysis.

The platform also integrates Trading Central signals, giving day traders actionable entry and exit points, plus access to useful tools like a market sentiment gauge and the Market Buzz feature â all directly within the web trader. I also appreciated the full-screen chart mode, which is perfect for traders who want to study price movements in high definition.

My only gripe is that the platform doesnât yet support copy trading, which would make an otherwise excellent tool even more complete.

Doto Mobile App

Dotoâs mobile app retains the flexibility and usability of its web counterpart. The app can be used for account management and trading on the go. It also features Dotoâs proprietary AI-powered trading signals, which analyze market sentiment and technical setups to help traders spot potential opportunities in real time.

Additionally, Doto App offers access to market analytics and a built-in trading calendar, enabling users to stay informed about key economic events. I found the appâs design light, modern, and easy to navigate.

Doto Execution Model

Doto operates as a Straight-Through-Processing (STP) broker without a dealing desk. Client orders are routed to the brokerâs pool of liquidity providers, where they are filled at the best available price.

Tradable Instruments

Doto offers over 220 CFD instruments across currency pairs, commodities, shares, indices, cryptocurrencies, and ETFs. The offering is reasonably diverse and features some rare assets, such as XAUSGD.

Compared to the industry average, Doto offers a high number of currency pairs, commodities, and cryptocurrencies, an average number of indices, and a low number of stocks.

What Are CFDs?

CFDs (Contracts for Difference) let you trade on the price movements of assetsâlike goldâwithout actually owning them.

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you loseâwithout ever buying real gold.

The biggest perk? You can jump in or out of the market quickly to take advantage of even the smallest price changes.

Doto Instruments: My Key Takeaways

In my estimation, Dotoâs tradable instruments offering is reasonably diverse. I appreciated the large forex and commodity selections, especially the addition of rare instruments like XAUSGD. However, the broker could enhance its general offering by expanding its selection of share CFDs and adding more low-risk securities, such as bonds and ETFs.

Customer Support

Doto offers 24/7 multilingual support via live chat, email, and phone. The live chat features a sophisticated chatbot for addressing more general questions, as well as the option to speak with live agents. I found Dotoâs agents to be pretty knowledgeable and very responsive. Overall, I rate Dotoâs support as very high quality.

I tested Dotoâs customer support by asking a series of questions of varying complexity on 7 October at around 12:47 CET via live chat. The chatbot handled most of my queries well, but couldnât answer a question about Dotoâs execution model.

When I requested a live agent, the connection was almost instant. The agent immediately understood my question and provided a clear, satisfactory answer.

Overall, I was pleased with Dotoâs customer support. The chatbot is efficient enough to handle around 90% of common queries, and for anything more complex, knowledgeable live agents are readily available to help.

Deposit and Withdrawal

Doto accepts payments via bank wire, credit and debit cards, as well as several e-wallets. It does not charge a handling fee for deposits or withdrawals, although third-party banking fees may still apply. Dotoâs transaction times are quite fast.

Account Types and Terms

Doto provides two retail account types: Standard and Raw. The Standard account features floating spreads from 1.0 pips and no commissions, while the Raw account features spreads from 0.0 pips and a $7 round-turn commission. The broker currently does not offer Islamic accounts for swap-free trading.

How to Open an Account With Doto

To open an account with Doto, follow these simple steps:

  1. Click âCreate Accountâ at the top-right corner of the main page.
  2. Provide and then confirm your email address.
  3. Fill in your name and date of birth.
  4. Provide your phone number and country of residence.
  5. Elaborate on your trading experience.
  6. Agree to Dotoâs terms and conditions.
  7. Configure the parameters of your trading account.
  8. Upload proof of ID and proof of address to verify your account.

The Standard account requires a minimum deposit of $15, making it accessible to most traders. It features zero commissions and floating spreads, offering a simple and affordable setup ideal for casual and beginner traders.

In contrast, the Raw account features more competitive spreads and is a better fit for high-volume traders. However, its $7 round-turn commission per traded lot (100,000 units) exceeds the industry average of $6. The Raw accountâs minimum deposit requirement of $200 is aligned with other ECN accounts.

Demo Accounts

Doto offers a demo account that lets traders explore the brokerâs available platforms and test their strategies in a risk-free environment. Since markets are constantly changing, itâs crucial to keep your skills sharp without risking real money. You can open a demo account before or alongside your live CFD account.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money, allowing them to open larger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Doto Restricted Countries

Doto does not accept as clients residents of American Samoa, Australia, Belgium, Canada, the Central African Republic, China, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, CÃ´te dâIvoire, Eritrea, the European Union, Guam, Heard Island and McDonald Islands, Iran, Israel, Japan, Liberia, Libya, Mali, Mauritius, Myanmar, New Zealand, North Korea, Northern Mariana Islands, Norway, Puerto Rico, Russia, Somalia, Sudan, the Syrian Arab Republic, Switzerland, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the United States Minor Outlying Islands, the United States of America, the Virgin Islands, Yemen, or any other restricted country or jurisdiction where trading is prohibited by law.

Research

Doto provides an economic calendar, a news screener, and Trading Central insights â all conveniently integrated into its trading platform. I found the AI-generated trading signals particularly useful for identifying actionable opportunities. However, while Dotoâs research tools are practical, the overall offering feels limited compared to what many competitors provide.

Research Tools

  • Economic Calendar: The economic calendar is a fundamental research tool that informs traders of upcoming economic releases and financial news that have the potential to move the market and create viable trading opportunities.

• News Screener: Traders can stay in sync with current market movers and other news via Dotoâs news screener, which is integrated directly on the platform. The market breakdowns are concise and easy to understand, although they lack supporting price charts.

• Trading Central Package: Doto incorporates content from Trading Central, which is arguably the best aspect of its research offering. The package comprises advanced market analytics and actionable trading signals. Traders are presented with viable entry levels, take-profit levels, and stop-loss levels on multiple assets. The signals are AI-generated, and traders should consider whether to utilise them at their own peril.

Doto Research: My Key Takeaways

Dotoâs market research caters well to day traders, offering actionable Trading Central signals that make it easy to spot and act on emerging opportunities with just a few clicks.

That said, while the tools are practical and effective, the research itself lacks depth. Doto could elevate its offering by including more detailed market analyses and broader insights to complement its short-term trading focus.

Education

Doto offers several articles on its trading platform, as well as an extensive Help Center filled with practical articles and step-by-step guides. However, there are no other types of content, such as videos or e-books, that delve deep into the subject matter.

I found 10 educational articles available directly on Dotoâs trading platform and mobile app. These cover basic topics like reading price action and understanding risk management, but thereâs little focus on technical analysis, fundamental analysis, or trading psychology.

Beyond the platform, Doto also maintains a Help Center on its website with over 70 articles explaining key trading concepts, risk management principles, and step-by-step platform tutorials.

The broker also shared that it plans to launch live webinars soon to further support clients and expand their trading knowledge.

Overall, I appreciate Dotoâs efforts to provide a mix of practical and accessible learning materials. That said, the educational library still feels limited compared to whatâs offered by larger, content-focused brokers.

The Bottom Line

Doto stands out as a modern, well-regulated broker with a strong focus on usability and technology. Its proprietary web platform â powered by TradingView and enhanced with Trading Central analytics â is one of the best in its class, offering traders advanced charting tools and real-time signals within a clean, intuitive interface. I found Doto particularly appealing for day traders and technically oriented traders who value actionable insights and quick execution.

That said, Doto still has room for improvement. While it offers pretty favorable costs on forex and share CFDs, its spreads on gold and indices are higher than the industry average. I also found that Dotoâs research and educational materials lag behind those of other brokers. The absence of copy trading and Islamic accounts also limits its appeal for certain audiences.

Overall, Doto is a solid and transparent broker that strikes a balance between innovation and accessibility. Itâs an excellent pick for active traders looking for a sleek, analytics-driven platform, though beginners may find its learning resources too limited compared to industry leaders.

Our Take on Doto

Founded in 2019 and based in Cyprus, Doto is a modern forex and CFD broker offering over 220 tradable instruments. What really makes it stand out is its sleek, intuitive trading platform powered by TradingView charts and Trading Central signals â a great combo for traders who like clean visuals and data-driven insights.

If you prefer something familiar, Doto also supports MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5, available on desktop, web, and mobile.

When it comes to fees, Doto keeps things simple with commission-free trading and cost-free deposits and withdrawals. While its spreads vary across instruments and its overnight fees (swaps) can be a bit high, overall, itâs still accessible and transparent.

I also found Dotoâs customer support to be one of the best around â responsive, friendly, and backed by a smart chatbot that actually works.

On the other hand, thereâs no copy trading or Islamic account option, and the education section is somewhat limited and could benefit from more detailed learning resources.

Overall, Doto is a great choice for day traders who rely on real-time signals and technical traders who appreciate advanced charting tools in a user-friendly package.

How Does DuraMarkets Protect You?

I reviewed the brokerâs âTerms of Useâ document and âRisk Noticeâ, which can be accessed from the bottom of the website page. However, I also discovered that there is no dedicated legal docs section on the website.

Here is what I found about DuraMarkets Ltd:

â Segregated Accounts â Client funds are kept separate from the companyâs own capital.

â Negative Balance Protection â Your losses cannot exceed your invested capital.

â Compensation Scheme â In the event of insolvency, you will not be entitled to insurance.

Learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you in our dedicated guide on client protections.

Stability and Transparency

We also assess a brokerâs stability and transparency. This includes how long it has been in business, the company size, and how openly it shares information about its business and services.

The first thing I did was check DuraMarketsâ company background, which is where I hit a roadblock. I discovered that there is almost no information available. The brokerâs âAbout Usâ page is blank and contains no information about when the company was founded or how many people work for it. Another red flag was the lack of social media channels. Typically, I would check a brokerâs LinkedIn page, but DuraMarkets does not have one.

Then, I reviewed DuraMarketsâ client agreement and confirmed that the broker keeps client funds segregated and ensures negative balance protection.

During my review, I noticed that DuraMarkets lacks an account verification process. When I opened my live account with DuraMarkets, I was not asked to upload proof of my ID or address to verify my account, which is a common practice among reliable brokers

Finally, I noticed that DuraMarkets does not display a live spreads feed on the website. Such a feed allows traders to quickly assess a brokerâs fee transparency and competitiveness.

Is DuraMarkets Safe?

Although DuraMarkets does not require account verification and has transparency gaps, I concluded that it has a moderate level of safety due to the following factors:

  • Licensed by an offshore regulator.
  • Keeps client funds in segregated accounts.
  • Guarantees negative balance protection.

Fees

I experienced mostly favorable prices with DuraMarkets. Forex and crypto costs were tight, but index pricing was a bit pricier. I also recorded low gold spreads but high crude oil spreads with the Zero account, and high gold spreads but low crude oil spreads with the Standard account.

I also recorded pretty competitive swaps across most instruments, except for forex, making DuraMarkets an attractive option for swing traders. But I did not find any confirmation of inactivity or maintenance fees.

If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

A classic outlook. MetaTrader should be given credit for popularizing a design that is replicated by many other trading platforms. It features a broad charts area occupying the middle section of the screen, a comprehensive tools panel at the top, and a watchlists + navigator screens on the left-hand side.

Multiple functionalities. My favorite aspect of MetaTrader is its numerous functionalities, accommodating different trading styles. Beyond day and swing trading, the platform also supports automated trading via Expert Advisors (EAs), scalping via the one-click trading and depth-of-market (DoM) tools, copy trading, and more. You can even use the built-in strategy tester to assess the performance of your strategies and tweak their parameters.

Loaded with practical insights. My other favorite thing about MetaTrader is its vast library of supporting content. You can find dozens of practical guides, educational articles, and walkthrough videos integrated directly on the platform and explaining its various functionalities. Few other platforms match MTâs educational database. You can access it from the âHelpâ tab at the top panel and then clicking âVideo Guidesâ or âMQL5 Articlesâ.

Tracking your speed. MetaTrader also allows you to easily track your ping from different servers. You can check a brokerâs available servers by clicking the traffic indicator in the bottom-right corner of the platform.

Using this functionality, I learned that DuraMarkets affords access to three servers: London, Amsterdam, and Frankfurt. As a trader based in Europe, this is quite convenient for me because it allows me to achieve a ping below the industry average of 60 milliseconds. Thus, I consider DuraMarkets an acceptable choice for high-precision trading. However, bear in mind that your execution speed may differ based on your location, server connectivity, internet speed, and other external factors.

Outdated Charting Capabilities. On the downside, MT5âs outdated charting capabilities are outmatched by more modern trading stations, such as cTrader and TradingView. In my opinion, its chart visuals are too rugged.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by DuraMarkets is available for Windows and Mac users and supports 39 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is loaded with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools. You can use these to spot price trends and ranges and to assess their strength. For example, the Ichimoku Cloud indicator applied above shows me that the bullish trend could be flattening out, given that the price action crossed below the two MAs. At the same time, the MACD indicator is showing decreasing momentum. Hence, the two could be signaling a possible bearish correction.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting. I apply tools like the Fibonacci retracement levels to map out major support and resistance levels within a price trend. I then use these as reference points for possible rebounds/reversals or breakouts/breakdowns, depending on the direction of the underlying trend.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry. Typically, I apply higher timeframes (above 4H) to determine the general direction of the market and smaller timeframes (below 1H) to spot viable entries within the broader trend.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format. Personally, I prefer using candlesticks because they provide me with a more comprehensive picture. For example, a bullish Marubozu candlestick may signify strong buying sentiment, whereas the formation of a shooting star candlestick may indicate a possible bearish reversal.

That said, MT5âs charts get cluttered quite easily, especially when applying more than one technical indicator or drawing tool. Price action becomes obscured and difficult to interpret. Overall, MT5âs charts are not ideal for traders accustomed to streamlined and easily scalable setups.

Order Types

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries.
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android devices and offers most of the functionalities of the desktop version. This makes the MT5 app a convenient tool for staying connected to the market and adjusting your positions on the fly.

You can place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as manage position size and risk directly from the app. That said, the charting experience still feels a bit cramped, and price action can be hard to scale and analyze comfortably on a small screen.

DuraMarkets provides Virtual Private Server (VPS) hosting for low-latency trading. DuraMarkets offers a maximum leverage of 1:500, which is considered relatively high. For example, if you deposit $100 into your account and set your leverage at 1:500, you can open a position of $50,000.

DuraMarkets Restricted Countries

DuraMarkets does not accept traders from Afghanistan, Belarus, Burundi, China, Congo, Crimea (Region of Ukraine), Cuba, India, Iran, Iraq, North Korea (Democratic Peopleâs Republic of Korea), Romania, Russia, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Syria, Turkey, the United States of America, Venezuela, Yemen, or any other restricted country or jurisdiction where trading is prohibited by law.

Research

DuraMarkets does not currently offer any research content apart from the economic calendar built into the mobile app version of MetaTrader. There are no market overview articles, webinars, technical/fundamental analyses, or actionable trading signals.

Education

DuraMarkets performed poorly in this category because its educational offering is very limited compared to the industry. The broker has published several educational articles and a few MetaTrader tutorials on its website blog. Currently, no other types of content are available.

DuraMarkets has published about a dozen articles on essential trading concepts and terms, such as using the MACD indicator and handling emotional trading. But the materials are limited in scope and diversity. Hence, you might need to seek additional help outside DuraMarkets.

The Bottom Line

Founded in 2023 and headquartered in the Comoros Union, DuraMarkets is a new forex and CFD broker that offers 95 assets across currency pairs, commodities, indices, and cryptocurrencies.

You can place your orders from the feature-rich MT4 and MT5 platforms, available for desktop, mobile, and web trading. I recorded fast order execution speed, which was lower than the industry benchmark of 60 milliseconds. Another perk is fast, reliable customer support.

While DuraMarketsâ fees vary by account type and traded instrument, I consider the rock-bottom BTCUSD fees to be the brokerâs greatest advantage. I also found that it offers competitive forex prices.

However, the broker offers almost no educational or research content and allows retail traders to use leverage below 1:100 only upon request, limiting its appeal, especially for less experienced traders.

That said, if youâre a cost-conscious swing trader or crypto trader, DuraMarkets could be a good option for you.

Our Take on DuraMarkets

DuraMarkets is an up-and-coming forex and CFD broker founded in 2023 and based in the Comoros Union. It is not licensed or regulated. The broker offers 95 tradable instruments across forex, commodities, indices, and cryptocurrencies. You can trade them on MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 and boost your performance using free VPS hosting.

Fees are low to average on most instruments I tested. Forex costs were very competitive, while commodity conditions depend on the account you use. I would trade gold on the Zero account, while oil is better priced on the Standard account.

I was most surprised by the favorable Bitcoin trading conditions, which were around 5 times cheaper than the industry average. I also found out that overnight fees on metals, energies, indices, and cryptocurrencies were relatively low.

That said, DuraMarkets currently offers almost no educational or research content. On top of that, leverage starts at 1:100, with lower option available only by request, which can significantly increase your trading risk during volatile market conditions.

Overall, DuraMarkets shows promise in pricing and platform support, offering attractive conditions for cost-conscious traders and those seeking fast execution.

Elev8 Regulators

When reviewing a broker, we examine how each of its entities is regulated and assess how effectively they protect clients. We use a three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier-1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about Elev8:

  • Finexis Markets Ltd is registered in the Comoros Union with the Mwali International Services Authority (MISA) under registration number HY00623410. Due to its poor supervision practices, we consider MISA the weakest offshore regulator.
  • Elev8 Markets Limited is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) of Mauritius under license number GB21027161. We rate the FSC as a Tier-3 regulator.

How Does Elev8 Protect You?

I reviewed the brokerâs client agreement and risk disclosure to examine how Elev8 protects its clients. These documents can be accessed from the âLegalâ section of the website.

Here is what I found about Elev8:

â Segregated Accounts â Client funds are kept separate from the companyâs own capital.

â Negative Balance Protection â Your losses cannot exceed your invested capital.

â Compensation Scheme â In the unlikely event of insolvency, you may not be entitled to compensation.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, check our dedicated guide on client protections.

Stability and Transparency

We also assess a brokerâs stability and transparency. This includes how long the company has been in business, its size, and how openly it shares information about its business and services.

I reviewed Elev8âs company background and social media channels, including its LinkedIn profile, and learned that the broker was established four years ago and employs fewer than 20 professionals.

I further checked Elev8âs client agreement and risk notice, both available from the legal docs section of the website. Both documents state that the broker segregates client funds and provides negative balance protection.

I also appreciated Elev8âs high fee transparency. There is a live spreads feed on the website, allowing casual visitors to quickly assess the brokerâs fee transparency and competitiveness.

Is Elev8 Safe?

Elev8 is reasonably safe to trade with due to the following factors:

  • Licensed and regulated by the FSC.
  • Keeps client funds in segregated accounts.
  • Guarantees negative balance protection.
  • Displays live quotes.

Fees

My live testing revealed that Elev8 charges low spreads on currency pairs, stocks, gold, and Bitcoin. On the other hand, costs on indices and oil exceeded the industry average. Swing traders will favor that Elev8 offers swap-free trading across all instruments, unlike most brokers. I also learned that Elev8 does not charge an inactivity fee and that deposits and withdrawals are free.

Elev8 Swaps

A swap fee is the cost of keeping a trade open overnight, and itâs tied to the difference in interest rates between the two currencies in a pair. If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

Unlike most other forex and CFD brokers, Elev8 charges no overnight fees. All available instruments can be traded swap-free. This benefits longer-term and swing traders, as they can keep their positions open for multiple days without worrying about incurring negative interest.

Are Elev8âs Fees Competitive?

ELEV8 Non-Trading Fees

Elev8 does not impose an inactivity fee on dormant accounts. I also learned that the broker does not charge deposit or withdrawal fees, though third-party processing fees may apply.

Platforms and Tools

The broker is breaking ground with its Elev8Trader platform, which features advanced market analytics and high-definition charts. It is available for web and mobile devices. Elev8 also offers MT4 and MT5, whose leg up over the brokerâs own trading platform is higher functionality. You can use MetaTrader for one-click trading, DoM trading, copy trading, and automated trading via Expert Advisors (EAs).

Elev8Trader Web

I tested Elev8Trader and appreciated its clean design and integrated market research, which not every trading platform offers. However, it does not support copy or automated trading, as is available in MetaTrader.

Basic Set of Tools. The Elev8Trader platform can be used to place market, limit, and stop orders. It also supports floating orders (break-even and trailing stop tools). You can place trading alerts and customize your watchlists of selected instruments. I also counted more than 50 analytical tools (technical indicators and drawing tools) and chart configurations.

Intuitive Design. I really appreciated Elev8Trader for its streamlined interface, built for speed and efficiency. You can easily navigate it without feeling overwhelmed. Another highlight of the layout is the clear, fluid charts, which enable deep, penetrating price action analysis.

Integrated Research. The Elev8Trader also features penetrating market research. The integrated trading signals inform you about currently developing trading setups. You can read about price formations and what the underlying technical indicators say about the opportunity. I also really liked that you can copy the setups directly to the chart. You can access those and other research tools from the âSpaceâ section located on the right-hand side.

Educational Content. Another great perk of the Elev8Trader platform is the integrated educational content. You can access over 30 educational articles introducing novice traders to different trading strategies â from day trading to swing trading.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I have also tested MetaTrader 5, which has a rather old-school feel but is packed with more features.

A classic outlook. MetaTrader inspired a classic design that is replicated by many other trading platforms. It features a broad charting area occupying the middle section of the screen, a comprehensive tools panel at the top, and watchlists and navigator screens on the left-hand side.

Multiple functionalities. My favourite thing about MetaTrader is its extensive functionality, which accommodates a range of trading styles. Beyond day and swing trading, the platform also supports automated trading via Expert Advisors (EAs), scalping via the one-click trading and depth-of-market (DoM) tools, copy trading, and more. You can even use the built-in strategy tester to assess your strategiesâ performance and tweak their parameters.

Educational Materials. My other favorite thing about MetaTrader is its extensive library of guides, articles, and tutorials that explain the platformâs various functionalities. Few other platforms match MTâs educational database. You can access it from the âHelpâ tab at the top panel and then clicking âVideo Guidesâ or âMQL5 Articlesâ.

Outdated Look. On the downside, MT5âs outdated charting capabilities are outmatched by more modern trading stations, such as cTrader and TradingView. In my opinion, its chart visuals are too rugged.

Availability & Features

Within the Elev8 ecosystem, the MT5 platform is available for Windows and Mac users and supports 39 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is loaded with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools. You can use these to spot price trends and ranges and to assess their strength.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting. I use tools like the Fibonacci retracement levels to map out major support and resistance levels within a price trend. I then use these as reference points for possible rebounds/reversals or breakouts/breakdowns, depending on the underlying trend.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry. Typically, I use higher timeframes (above 4H) to determine the general direction of the market and smaller timeframes (below 1H) to spot viable entries within the broader trend.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format. Personally, I prefer candlesticks because they provide a more comprehensive picture. For example, a bullish Marubozu candlestick may signify strong buying sentiment, whereas the formation of a shooting star candlestick may indicate a possible bearish reversal.

That said, MT5âs charts get cluttered quite easily, especially when applying more than one technical indicator or drawing tool. Price action becomes obscured and difficult to interpret. Overall, MT5âs charts are not ideal for traders accustomed to streamlined and easily scalable setups.

Order Types

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries.
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android devices and offers most of the desktop versionâs functionality. This makes the MT5 app a convenient tool for staying connected to the market and adjusting your positions on the fly.

You can place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as manage position size and risk directly from the app. That said, the charting experience still feels a bit cramped, and price action can be hard to scale and analyze comfortably on a small screen.

Research

Elev8 delivers a decent selection of research materials, including a basic economic calendar, a news screener, actionable trading signals, and several other tools. The economic calendar is the most basic research tool that informs traders of upcoming market releases and financial decisions. These events are widely anticipated because they can prompt a significant market reaction, creating viable trading opportunities.

Elev8 also publishes market breakdowns on its news screener, helping you stay on top of the latest market-moving headlines. Most articles are focused on the technical aspect of things, tracking price action, the emergence of new levels of support and resistance, and so on.

Education

Elev8 has published several dozen articles and guidebooks for first-time and intermediate traders. The content is primarily focused on the technical side of trading. For example, you can learn how to spot flag patterns and how to use Fibonacci retracement levels. However, no attention is paid to fundamental analysis, risk management, or trading psychology.

I counted about 40 educational articles available on the website and the Elev8Trader platform. They are highly practical and offer valuable trading insights, such as how to spot different trading patterns. On the other hand, the content feels disjointed and lacks an overarching structure. My other gripe is that the materials are only available in written form â there are no videos.

The Bottom Line

Elev8 is a financial derivatives broker offering 260+ tradable instruments to traders globally. The broker has licences from two offshore regulators â MISA and FSC â so keep in mind that the client protection is quite loose.

I found that Elev8 offers very low fees for BTCUSD trading. The costs on forex, gold, and share CFDs were also better than the industry average or aligned with it. Only the prices for WTI Oil and indices exceeded the benchmark.

Elev8 stands out for its swap-free trading across all available assets, making it a great option for swing traders. It also impressed me with its user-friendly Elev8Trader platform, integrated with daily insights from real experts. While the platform doesnât support copy trading or automated trading, you can compensate for this with MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5.

Where Elev8 lags behind other brokers is in its range of tradable instruments and depth of educational content.

All things considered, Elev8 is an OK choice for swing and news traders, largely due to its competitive pricing.

Erranteâs economic calendar is a fundamental research tool that informs traders of upcoming economic releases and financial news that have the potential to move the market and create viable trading opportunities.

The broker also publishes weekly market overviews. These reports help put economic events into context by offering key insights into how the market may react to them.

Errante Research: My Key Takeaways

I appreciated Erranteâs weekly breakdowns for their comprehensiveness. However, I found the overall selection of research content to be slim and lacking in scope.

Education

Errante shines in the education category with its vast and diverse selection of articles, videos, e-books, courses, and webinars. The broker strikes a fine balance between written and video content, catering to the unique preferences of different traders. The educational materials cover topics pertaining to technical analysis, fundamental analysis, and elements of trading psychology.

I counted more than 170 educational videos on Erranteâs website, covering everything from forex basics to MetaTrader tutorials.

Errante has also published five high-quality e-books and four structured courses. The topics of the courses include âIntroduction to Forex Basics,â âForex Trading Essentials,â âFoundations of Technical Analysis,â and âBasics of Fundamental Analysis in Forex Trading.â

On top of that, the broker provides dozens of educational articles and hosts weekly webinars, most of which focus on technical analysis.

All in all, I consider Erranteâs educational offering one of the strongest in the industry. Thereâs something for everyone â from complete beginners to intermediate traders and even experienced market participants.

The Bottom Line

Errante shines when it comes to platforms and education. With MT4, MT5, cTrader, and TradingView all under one roofâand one of the richest learning hubs Iâve seenâitâs a great fit for anyone who wants flexibility and room to grow.

Just be aware that trading costs are mixed on the Standard account. Stocks and major indices are priced well, but forex, commodities, and crypto spreads were on the high side during my tests, and swaps were elevated across the board. Research tools are also fairly minimal compared to competitors.

In short, Errante is an excellent pick for beginners, technical traders, and algo traders who value platform choice and deep educational support. If you rely heavily on low-cost forex or overnight trading, you may want to compare pricing elsewhere.

How eToro Protects You?

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors.
    eToro keeps client funds separately from its own.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. All eToro entities guarantee negative balance protection, except for Etoro USA Securities Inc.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent.
    Clients of eToro (UK) Ltd are protected by up to GBP 85,000 under the Financial Services Compensation Scheme. Clients of eToro (Europe) Ltd are protected by up to EUR 20,000 under the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF). Clients of Etoro USA Securities Inc. are protected by up to USD 500,000 under the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC).
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses.
    The global eToro (Seychelles) Ltd entity provides the highest retail leverage 1:400.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

eToro was founded in 2007 and has established itself as a reputable broker. According to its LinkedIn page, the company employs several thousand people worldwide, which also attests to its longevity and stability.

I pored over eToroâs legal documents, including its Client Agreement and order execution policy documentation, and found that everything was in order. All essential information is readily available and easy to discern.

Is eToro Safe?

I concluded that eToro ranks among the safest forex brokers due to the following factors:

  • Operates on a âbest executionâ basis

The only exception was share CFDs with very low spreads. Social and copy trading are free, and most deposits and withdrawals come at no costâexcept for withdrawals from USD-denominated accounts.   • Stop Orders: Used to limit potential losses if the market moves against a position. A stop-loss is set at a fixed price and, once triggered, becomes a market order executed at the best available price.

eToro US is regulated by top-tier FINRA and is a member of SIPC, which protects clients against the loss of cash and securities. With a lengthy operating history of over 17 years, eToro has a substantial depth of experience as a broker, and my research indicated that the company is highly transparent.

  • eToro USA Securities Inc. (CRD#: 298361/SEC#: 8-70212) is regulated by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) via the Woodbridge district office.

FINRA, a private corporation, establishes and upholds the regulations that all registered brokers in the United States must adhere to. This organization diligently oversees brokers to ensure compliance with its standards, secures restitution for investors who have suffered losses, and actively works to eliminate unethical practitioners from the industry.

Why is it important to know where your broker subsidiary (entity) is regulated?

To serve clients worldwide, brokers must have multiple regional entities. The level of client protection guaranteed by regional regulators varies widely. Here are some of the key features to check on at your broker`s regional entity:

  • Segregation of client funds. Segregating client funds from the operating capital of a broker prevents misuse, ensuring that tradersâ funds can not be used for operational expenses or speculative investments. At eToro USA Securities Inc., all client funds are held in segregated accounts away from the companyâs funds.
  • Negative balance protection. This is a guarantee that clients cannot lose more than their account balance, even if the market unexpectedly makes a massive move or gaps. At eToro USA Securities Inc. accounts are cash only so there is no risk of losing more than your initial deposit.
  • Compensation scheme. A compensation scheme protects client funds in the unlikely event that the broker becomes insolvent. eToro USA Securities Inc. offers SIPC protection of up to $500,000 for securities and cash (up to $500,000 for securities and $250,000 for cash.) This does not cover crypto investments.
  • Maximum leverage. Limiting leverage controls the level of risk traders can take on. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and losses. At eToro USA Securities Inc. the maximum leverage is 1:1.

eToro US distinguishes itself in the American market by not just offering the usual stocks, ETFs, and options trading but also by integrating a diverse range of cryptocurrencies. In my assessment, eToro US is particularly well-suited for beginners, casual investors, and those with a keen interest in the crypto market. How Exness Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. At Exness, all client funds are held in segregated accounts away from the companyâs funds.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. All Exness entities provide negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects retail traders against the brokerâs liabilities in the unlikely event that the company becomes insolvent. As a member of the Financial Commission, Exness ensures clients are protected up to 20,000 EUR per complaint.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The default maximum leverage at the Seychelles entity of Exness is 1:2000.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Exness dates back to 2008, marking it as a highly experienced CFD broker with a lengthy operating history. According to the brokerâs website, the company has over 2,000 employees, reflecting a large brokerage firm.

In my research, Exness showed high transparency in its regulatory status, listing its regulators in the footer of its website pages and on its Regulation page.

The website clearly breaks down trading costs on the Fees page. To get the nitty-gritty details, traders can find the Client Agreement on the Legal Documents page.

Is Exness Safe to Trade With?

Exness operates nine entities, which offer different levels of client protection. The broker is a member of the Financial Commission, an independent self-regulatory organization and external dispute resolution body focused on Forex. This membership provides Exness clients with protection through the Commissionâs Compensation Fund, covering claims up to 20,000 EUR.

To summarize, I rate Exness as trustworthy and stable due to the following:

  • 17-year operating history
  • All entities covered by regulatory bodies
  • All entities segregate funds
  • All entities offer negative balance protection

Exness utilizes a market execution model for most of its account types. This means orders are executed at the best available market price with no requotes, ensuring speed and reliability, even during volatile conditions. The infrastructure behind this model includes a global network of decentralized servers and connections to top-tier liquidity providers, which work together to reduce latency and slippage. For traders using Pro accounts, Exness also offers instant execution, allowing them to target specific prices with the potential for requotes.

Fintana Regulators

When reviewing brokers, we examine the licenses held by each of their entities to determine how effectively they protect clients. We use a simple three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier 1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

How Does Fintana Protect You?

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is how Fintana protects you:

â Segregated accounts â Client funds are kept separate from the companyâs own capital.

â Negative balance protection â Your losses can exceed your invested capital.

To learn more about the most important safety mechanisms and how they apply to you, click here.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

I reviewed the âAbout Usâ section of Fintanaâs website and its LinkedIn page and was surprised to find that both lack some very basic company detailsâsuch as where the broker is headquartered, when it was founded, or how large the company actually is.

Another drawback is that Fintana does not display live spreads on its website. This is usually a key transparency measure, as it allows traders to quickly compare a brokerâs fees with industry standards.

Finally, while the website repeatedly suggests that Fintana offers negative balance protection, I could not find any confirmation of this in the brokerâs legal documents. This inconsistency raises questions about the clarity of the protections actually provided to clients.

Is Fintana Safe?

Fintana is regulated by the Mauritius FSC, a Tier-3 regulator. Client funds are segregated, but I couldnât confirm that the broker provides negative balance protection and a compensation scheme. Their absence leaves traders more exposed to risk.

Transparency is also weak: the website doesnât display live spreads, omits key company details, and its legal documents donât confirm the protections it claims to provide. Overall, Fintana is regulated but less safe than many industry peers.

Fees

Fintanaâs trading fees are on the higher side across all instruments I tested. Spreads came in way above the industry average, and swaps showed the same pattern. While the broker doesnât charge a handling fee on deposits, its inactivity fee is relatively high and applies after a short period of inactivity.

Fintana Swaps

A swap fee is the cost of keeping a trade open overnight, and itâs tied to the difference in interest rates between the two currencies in a pair. If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. I also noticed that Fintanaâs swaps are always credit deductible and never credit receivable, meaning that its clients are always charged overnight costs and never paid overnight interest, regardless of how interest rates on the interbank level change.

All deposits and most withdrawals with Fintana are free of charge, except for wire transfer withdrawals, which incur a $30 handling fee. Third-party processing fees may also apply.

Research Tools

• Daily Analysis Videos: Arguably Fintanaâs best research content, the video breakdowns inform traders of where the market is headed and why. The content is light and easy to assimilate, providing users with a broad overview of changing market dynamics.

Fintanaâs Research: My Key Takeaways

Education

Fintana provides a beginner-friendly education package that includes 8 structured courses with 43 lessons, alongside several ebooks. The materials are clear, accessible, and well-suited for newcomers, though they donât yet cover advanced areas such as in-depth technical and fundamental analysis, trading psychology, or risk management.

Fintana has put together a collection of educational resources, including several video-based courses and guidebooks, giving traders a solid introduction to key trading concepts. The broker currently offers 8 courses with 43 individual lessons that cover a wide variety of topics. Interestingly, some of the lessons even touch on areas like ECN and copy trading, which shows Fintanaâs willingness to broaden tradersâ perspectives.

The guidebooks (presented as âE-Booksâ) also explain different aspects of the trading process in a clear and accessible way. While the materials are more suited to beginners and donât yet dive deeply into advanced areas like technical or fundamental analysis, trading psychology, or risk management, they still provide a useful starting point for those new to trading.

The Bottom Line

Fintana offers a few notable strengths but some big gaps compared to the wider industry. Its proprietary WebTrader, powered by TradingView, is genuinely a highlight â fluid, intuitive, and great for traders who rely heavily on technical analysis.

The broker also deserves credit for offering several account types, practical market research tools, and generally quick customer support.

That said, the downsides are hard to ignore. Trading costs are well above the industry average, swaps are always negative, and a $100 inactivity fee kicks in after only 30 days.

The instrument lineup covers the basics but lacks lower-risk products like ETFs or bonds, making hedging difficult. There are also some transparency concerns, such as unclear account conditions and protections, and Fintana falls behind many of its competitors.

Overall, Fintana may suit experienced traders who prioritize sleek charting and donât mind higher costs. But for beginners or anyone who is cost-conscious, the brokerâs offering feels limited compared to what the broader market provides.

This is what I discovered about the entities operating under the FISG trade name:

  • Interstellar Capital (Pty) Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Conduct Authority (FSCA) of South Africa under license number 52343. We rate the FSCA as a Tier-2 regulator.
  • First Interstellar Global Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Authority (FSA) of Seychelles. We rate the FSA as a Tier-3 regulator.

Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

What Leverage Does FISG Offer?

In the table below, I have listed the maximum retail leverage available with FISG for instruments from different asset classes:

Asset Maximum Leverage
Currency Pairs 1:500
Metals 1:500
Commodities 1:200
Share CFDs Not Specified
Indices 1:200
Cryptocurrencies 1:200

FISG Restricted Countries

FISG does not accept as clients residents of Belarus, Burundi, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, the Republic of Guinea, South Sudan, Ukraine, the United States of America, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, or any other restricted country or jurisdiction where trading is prohibited by law.

Research

FISG provides market news updates and trading signals, all developed in-house. The content is available in both written and video formats, and its quality is solid. That said, the broker could add another perspective to its research by incorporating content from third-party resources.

Research Tools

  • Economic Calendar: The economic calendar informs traders of upcoming market events and economic releases that have the potential to trigger a market reaction, thereby creating viable trading opportunities.

• FISG Notices and Breaking News: The brokerâs proprietary news screener provides brief market breakdowns, informing traders of the latest economic releases and financial news that affect the market.
• FISG Analysis: Market news breakdowns are also available in video format. These materials offer traders a more in-depth overview in an easy-to-understand format.

• Transaction Analysis: FISG also publishes detailed trading signals, informing traders of currently unfolding trading opportunities.
    This type of content comprises several key components: technical breakdowns, comprehensive fundamental analyses, and supporting price charts. Each signal is also supported with a performance tracker.

FISG Research: My Key Takeaways

FISGâs research offering is fairly broad and layered, giving traders a solid overview of ongoing market developments and highlighting potential trading opportunities. The main area for improvement would be the addition of third-party content (such as Autochartist or Trading Central), which could add more nuance and depth to the in-house analysis.

Education

FISG provides several introductory videos and a brief educational course. This content is well-balanced and primarily aimed at beginners and intermediate traders. However, it lacks depth to satisfy the needs of more experienced traders. There are no webinars.

FISGâs educational offering includes a small video library with seven clips covering basic trading concepts like âWhat is Leverage?â and âWhat is Overnight Interest?â The videos are light and easy to follow but fairly limited in scope, offering only a surface-level introduction.

On top of that, the broker has put together a structured educational course consisting of 8 core topicsâranging from technical and fundamental analysis to trading psychology and risk management. The course features 22 individual articles that go into more detail than the videos, making them a better resource overall. Still, the materials remain somewhat basic and may not be sufficient for advanced traders looking for deeper insights.

The Bottom Line

FISG is a mixed bag. On one hand, it delivers solid perks like MetaTrader 4 support, upcoming MT5 integration, copy trading, and impressive crypto conditions with tight BTCUSD spreads and massive 1:200 leverage on crypto. Its in-house market research and structured educational content also make it a decent fit for beginners and intermediate traders.

On the other hand, the broker lags behind industry peers when it comes to fees, with spreads and swaps that are often above the benchmark. A limited selection of trading accounts and unresponsive customer support further hold it back.

All things considered, FISG could be a suitable choice for traders focused on crypto or copy trading, but those seeking tighter fees, stronger transparency, and a wider account range may look for better value elsewhere.

Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Cyprus, FISG is a mid-sized financial derivatives broker offering 111 tradable instruments across forex, commodities, indices, cryptocurrencies, and bonds.

Trading is facilitated through the robust MetaTrader 4, with the broker currently working on integrating the newer MetaTrader 5 platform. FISG also supports copy trading and delivers broad in-house market research.

On the fee side, I found that spreads on oil and share CFDs were roughly in line with the industry average. However, forex and gold spreads â as well as swap fees â were higher than the market benchmark. On the plus side, the broker doesnât charge any fees for deposits or withdrawals.

I was particularly impressed by FISGâs crypto trading conditions, including its tight BTCUSD spread and massive 1:200 leverage â one of the highest in the industry.

On the downside, I found that the brokerâs selection of trading accounts is limited, and its customer support is unresponsive.
