OANDA Trade Web Platform

The OANDA Trade web-based platform is well-designed and easy to navigate. It is also customizable, allowing you to change the layout to suit your preference. Multiple chart layouts are available, and traders can view up to 8 charts simultaneously.

Charts

Charting is provided by TradingView, offering 81 indicators, 50 drawing tools, 10 time frames, and 11 chart types. The platform also allows users to trade directly from the chart, enabling quick and efficient entry and exit from positions.

The range of order types on the OANDA platform is impressive and includes standard order types such as market, limit, and stop-loss. Guaranteed stop-loss orders are also available, protecting clients from slippage and price gaps. It is possible to set time-in-force conditions; you can set your limit of stop-loss orders to expire after a set time, for example, 2 days or 1 week.

There are no alerts and 1-click trading on the OANDA web platform, but they are available on the OANDA mobile app.

The Order Book tool consists of open orders and open position information, showing how OANDA traders are currently positioned within the market. It allows you to see how pending orders and open positions are distributed at different price levels, which has value in determining potential support and resistance levels.
The Heat Map tool highlights instruments with the largest daily percentage price changes, helping traders identify those with the highest volatility.

The Position Ratios tool shows the percentage of OANDA traders who are long or short for each instrument. This data gives you insight into the psychology or sentiment of a market. Traders can interpret the data in a variety of ways. Most commonly, it is understood that when an extreme percentage of traders are either long or short an instrument, a trend reversal may be coming.
Autochartist can be accessed within the OANDA Trade Web platform and provides trade ideas by identifying popular chart patterns like triangle breakouts, channels, and wedges.

OANDA Trade Web Platform: My Key Takeaways

I found the OANDA Trade Web platform to be robust and feature-rich but not entirely beginner-friendly. The look and feel seemed somewhat dated to me. I liked the unique tools like the order book and position ratios, drawing from OANDAâs large client base. The platform also offers first-class charting from TradingView and a robust range of order types that can accommodate experienced traders. However, one major drawback is that 1-click trading is not available.

OANDA Mobile App

OANDAâs mobile app is beautifully designed and has a smooth, user-friendly interface. It features the same range of standard and advanced order types as the web and desktop platforms. The layout is customizable, so you can see your favorite instruments and adjust the size of the charts to suit your preferences.

The charting within the app is solid and has the following features:

  • 16 time frames, ranging from 5 seconds to one month.
  • 9 chart types, including Japanese candlesticks, Heikin Ashi, and OHLC (open-high-low-close).
  • 32 indicators, including MACD (moving average convergence/divergence) and RSI (relative strength index).
  • 11 drawing tools, from pivot points to Fibonacci retracements.

The app also features one-tap trading and alerts. Real-time news from Dow Jones and an economic calendar are also built-in. Two-factor authentication (2FA) is available to add an extra level of security when you sign in to OANDAâs trading platforms from your computer or mobile device. If you need to top up your account on the go, you can add funds via mobile. The app is available in English, German, Japanese, and Chinese.

OANDA Mobile App: My Key Takeaways

This is one of the best-designed and most feature-rich broker apps I have used. It can satisfy the needs of beginners, casual traders, and experienced professionals on the move.

MetaTrader 4 Desktop

OANDA offers the MetaTrader 4 for desktops, which includes advanced functions such as automated trading.

MT4 is available in 39 languages, from Arabic to Vietnamese. The platform provides popular features, including the following:

  • Alerts: This feature updates traders when an instrument reaches a specific price level.
  • Watchlists: Traders can create a list of their favorite instruments and follow live quotes in a market watch panel.
  • One-Click Trading: This feature allows traders to execute orders with a single click and no secondary confirmation. This feature enables traders to operate faster and is especially useful for short-term traders.
  • Trading from the Chart: MT4 also allows users the convenience of trading directly from the chart.

MetaTrader also delivers when it comes to the range of available order types. The platform offers these order types:

  • Market Order: Traders use market orders to buy or sell an instrument at the best current price.
  • Limit Order: Traders use limit orders to buy or sell an instrument at a specified price or better.
  • Stop Loss Order: Traders use stop-loss orders to buy or sell an instrument when its price reaches a specified level.
  • Trailing Stop Order: Traders use trailing stop-loss orders as a stop-loss order at a defined percentage or dollar amount away from an instrumentâs current market price. This order type allows traders to secure profits when they are in a winning trade while not having to exit the position.

MT4 charting features are robust and include:

  • 30 Technical Indicators: These include classic trend indicators, volume indicators, and oscillators.
  • 23 Analytical Objects: These include lines, channels, Gann, and Fibonacci tools.
  • 9 Time Frames: Traders can choose from nine time frames, from one minute to one month.
  • 3 Chart Types: Traders can use Bar Charts, Japanese Candlestick Charts, and Line Charts.

MetaTrader 4 is also popular due to its automated trading features, allowing users to develop, test, and apply Expert Advisors (EAs). EAs are programs that monitor and trade markets using algorithms. While being the most feature-rich and popular trading platform, MetaTrader 4 does not have a slick interface and requires some time and effort to learn.

MetaTrader 4 Trading App

OANDA offers the MetaTrader 4 app for mobile trading, which is available for Android and iOS. The app offers popular features such as alerts, 1-click trading, and trading from the chart.

The MT4 app also provides standard order types, including pending and stop orders. However, trailing stop-loss orders are only available from the desktop.

To change the language of the MT4 app, you must change the language for your entire phone.

As with the desktop and web platforms, the interface is not highly intuitive, but the MT4 app offers an above-average range of features.

MetaTrader 4: My Key Takeaways

As one of the most popular trading platforms in the world and the only one offered by many forex brokers, I have spent a lot of time testing MT4. The platformâs look and feel are a bit dated, and I feel there is room for improvement in design and usability.

Still, MT4 is a highly versatile platform that outperforms many competitors. It offers advanced charting, a comprehensive range of order types, and popular features such as one-click trading, trading directly from charts, and customizable alerts.

Its desktop platform stands out with advanced capabilities, including the ability to run and backtest automated strategies, making it a powerful tool for skilled traders. However, its steep learning curve means it is better suited for experienced traders rather than beginners.

TradingView

OANDA clients can also trade directly from the intuitive and feature-rich TradingView platform (either via the TradingView.com website or its desktop version).

Key features include cutting-edge, highly customizable charts with over 100 popular indicators and 50 drawing tools, as well as a community of millions of like-minded traders and investors.

The platform also features powerful tools like screeners for both shares and forex pairs, heatmaps, cloud-based trading alerts, and news feeds with stories from Reuters and Dow Jones.

OANDA Order Execution Model

OANDA acts as principal, not as agent, and is the sole venue for executing trades. This means that OANDA is the counterparty to all client trades. Clients trade directly with OANDA and not within the underlying market.

Tradable Instruments

OANDA offers a strong range of instruments, including CFDs on forex, index, commodity, and bond. Crypto and shares CFDs are available in some regions. Overall, I rate the selection of tradable instruments at OANDA as better than average

OANDA offers an above-average range of CFDs on currency pairs, commodities, and indices. The offshore entity offers CFDs on shares and cryptocurrencies, but they are not currently available at the UK entity.

What are CFDs?

A Contract for Difference (CFD) is an agreement specifying that the buyer must pay the seller the difference between an assetâs current value and its value at the time the contract was initiated. Like futures and other derivative financial instruments, CFDs allow traders to speculate on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

OANDA offers an attractive variety of tradable instruments. The range of currency pairs, indices, commodities, and bonds is deep. I noted that gold and silver can be traded against various currencies, for example, Gold/CHF and Silver/JPY.

Customer Support

OANDA provides support by phone, WhatsApp, live chat, and email from Sunday at 9 p.m. GMT to Friday at 11 p.m. GMT. During my two-week testing period, I experienced reliable support across all of the available mediums. I rate the support as better than average for the industry.

OANDA Customer Support Test

I tested OANDA customer service with dozens of queries, ranging from platforms to fees and account-related issues.

In the case of live chat and WhatsApp support, I had to navigate a chatbot and verify my email before reaching an agent. Once this was done, I received comprehensive answers to my inquiries. My emails to support (frontdesk@oanda.com) were addressed within one business day.

My experience via phone was also positive. After navigating a series of automated prompts, I was able to reach a helpful, well-informed operator within a couple of minutes.

Deposit and Withdrawal

Deposits and withdrawals at OANDA Global Markets Ltd can be made via bank transfer, credit card, and debit card. In some regions, clients can use alternative methods such as digital wallets. Processing times are average for the industry. While deposits are free, there is a fee for bank transfer withdrawal.

Account Types and Terms

OANDA Europe Ltd. offers two main account types: Standard and Spread Betting. If you meet certain criteria, you can get a Professional Account, which has benefits including increased leverage. Demo accounts are available for all platforms.

OANDA Account Opening Process

To open a CFD account with the UK entity of OANDA, prospective clients must provide the following information:

  • Email address and password set up
  • Personal details (name, date of birth, phone number)
  • Nationality and national insurance number
  • Home address
  • Employment (job title, industry, annual income, savings and investments, source of funds)
  • Trading experience (CFD, forex, or other leveraged derivatives trading)
  • Customer knowledge test (9 questions relating to forex and CFD trading)

Demo Account

OANDA offers demo accounts for the OANDA Trade Web, MT4, and TradingView platforms. Demo accounts are especially important for beginners as they allow them to practice their strategies and get comfortable with the trading platform without risking real money.

The demo account features live quotes and simulates live market conditions in assets like forex and CFDs on commodities, indices, and stocks. Once users are up to speed on a demo, they can easily switch to a live account.

Spread Betting Account

UK residents can open a Spread Betting account free from stamp duty and capital gains tax.

Professional Account

Experienced traders can open a professional account, allowing access to greater leverage and trading in CFDs on cryptocurrencies. To qualify for a professional account, traders must meet at least two of the following criteria:

  • Have placed at least 10 trades per quarter, over the previous four quarters, with a minimum notional value of Â£50,000 per trade, either with OANDA Europe Ltd or other providers.
  • Hold an investment portfolio exceeding â¬500,000.
  • Have at least one year of experience working in the financial sector in a professional position that requires knowledge of FX and CFD trading.

Islamic Account

OANDA does not offer swap-free Islamic accounts.

What is CFD Leverage?

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex and CFD markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is the use of borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

For the OANDA Europe Ltd. entity, the maximum leverage for a Standard Account is 1:30. This means that with an account of $1,000, you can control up to $30,000 worth of positions in the market. This is a relatively moderate level of leverage, but it still entails considerable risk.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders should keep in mind that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

OANDA accepts clients from most countries globally. However, residents of China, India, North Korea, and Iran are not accepted.

Research

OANDA shines in the area of research, offering industry-leading analysis via the MarketPulse website. Launched in 2006 by a team of experienced market analysts, MarketPulse publishes insightful commentary daily with full-time coverage of the worldâs largest financial markets. A strong flow of content is available in written, video, and podcast formats.

OANDA has developed an insightful news and research portal, MarketPulse.com, which covers both fundamental and technical analysis across forex, indices, commodities, and cryptocurrencies.

The Week Ahead articles keep traders abreast of upcoming economic events, providing insights into their potential market impacts. Other articles and videos are more technical, and traders can get ideas from chart patterns and support and resistance levels.

The MarketPulse website has an in-depth global economic calendar detailing event volatility, the actual figure, analyst consensus, and the prior figure. You can customize the calendar to your preference based on countries, indicator categories, and volatility levels.

In the Market Insights podcast, senior market analysts provide in-depth insights into the major economic trends and events that impact the markets.

OANDA Research: My Key Takeaways

OANDA has gone above and beyond in the area of research, with a steady flow of high-quality reports and videos from seasoned analysts. I rate the research materials as among the best in the industry.

Education

OANDA provides clients with educational articles and videos, platform tutorials, and live webinars with industry experts. While the quality of materials is good on the UK website, the content volume is relatively limited and mostly caters to beginners rather than experienced traders. The OANDA Labs section, available on the global entity website, goes into greater depth and can better cater to experienced traders.

The OANDA website education section is divided into sections that provide in-depth guides to the basics of CFD trading and market analysis.

  • The âIntroduction to Leveraged Tradingâ section explains fundamental concepts such as trading with margin, order types, and essential terminology.
  • The âFundamental Analysisâ section highlights the importance and various types of fundamental analysis, provides guidance on trading using this approach, and explains key economic indicators.
  • The âTechnical Analysisâ section walks you through the basics of technical analysis, introduces essential tools, and explains how to identify entry and exit points.

These guides are well-crafted and help new traders build a solid foundation of market-related knowledge.

I liked that the education section introduces actionable ideas and strategies. Guides within the education section cover practical topics like identifying entry and exit points using technical indicators.

The OANDA Trade Web platform offers unique tools and features that may require some explanation. The brokerâs YouTube channel features helpful platform tutorials covering topics like how to use the Order Book tool, and advanced charting options.

Live webinars are a highlight among educational resources. OANDA offers regular webinars hosted by seasoned analysts focused on recent price movements of the major currency pairs. These interactive events explain practical technical themes like how to draw trendlines and uncover areas of support and resistance.

The Bottom Line

OANDA boasts almost 30 years of experience and a strong global presence. Extensively regulated and highly transparent, the CFD industry giant earned a strong trust rating in my review.

OANDA offers a strong range of tradable instruments in major asset classes.

Spreads in CFDs on forex majors and indices are highly competitive, but most other instruments are closer to the industry average.

The brokerâs variety of platforms and tools can cater to a wide range of market approaches, from casual trading to scalping and fully automated trading. The range includes the popular MetaTrader 4 and TradingView, as well as the flagship OANDA platform, available for web and mobile. I especially liked the brokerâs unique tools like sentiment data.

OANDA could improve by offering tighter spreads across all asset classes and cutting account-related fees for its UK-based clients. While there is an abundance of research materials, the written educational resources are currently a bit thin.

Overall, I rate OANDA as a well-rounded broker with a unique offering. It can accommodate different experience levels and trading styles and is particularly algorithmic and short-term trading.

Our Take on OANDA

Founded in 1996, OANDA is a leading multinational broker offering trading in CFDs across a wide range of asset classes. The New York-based broker has multiple global entities overseen by top-tier regional regulators.

OANDA clients can access the markets via OANDA Trade Web, MetaTrader 4, and TradingView platforms. Tradable instruments include an above-average range of CFDs on currency pairs, indices, and commodities. Clients with global and EU entities can also access CFDs on shares and cryptocurrencies.

What is OANDA for?

Casual Trading: Perfect Match

OANDA offers reliable customer support, a range of trading platforms, and demo accounts. Live webinars, third-party tools like Autochartist, and articles outlining actionable strategies provide a valuable framework for casual traders and beginners.

Copy Trading: Acceptable Choice

OANDA does not offer a proprietary copy trading platform. However, if you choose to use MT4, you can automatically copy trades of signal providers.

Swing Trading: Acceptable Choice

OANDA Europe Ltd. offers a relatively limited range of markets for swing trading and does not provide real shares and ETFs. However, the EU entity offers trading in real shares. In my tests, overnight swap fees were average for the industry.

Day Trading: Perfect Match

MetaTrader 4 and TradingView provide one-click trading and trading from the chart, essential features for active traders who are in and out of the market throughout the day. Spreads in major forex pairs are also highly competitive, making it easier for traders to reach profitability. Signals from Autochartist and the Dow Jones newsfeed are valuable resources for day traders.

Scalping: Perfect Match

Scalpers, who are in and out of trading positions within seconds, benefit from OANDAâs reliability and fast order execution, even in volatile market conditions. VPS hosting from Beeks and Liquidity Connect is another advantage for scalpers, offering 24/7 uptime for uninterrupted trading.

News Trading: Perfect Match

Excellent news resources include a steady flow of stories from seasoned in-house analysts via the MarketPulse website and a feed of breaking news from Dow Jones within the OANDA Trade Web platform. Clients can access an in-depth economic calendar to stay on top of the latest economic news.

Automated Trading: Perfect Match

OANDA offers the MetaTrader 4 platform, which features strategy backtesting and automated trading. Clients can also benefit from VPS hosting, maximizing trade execution speed and protecting against power and internet outages. OANDAâs API technology can be used to integrate your strategy with trading applications and build your own custom user interfaces.

Investing: Not Recommended

OANDAâs UK entity lacks popular investing instruments like real shares, ETFs, mutual funds, or managed portfolios. It also has limited tools and research for long-term investors. However, real shares are available at the OANDA TMS Brokers S.A entity, which is available for European clients.

What Sets OANDA Apart?

OANDA has an extensive global presence and is licensed by multiple top-tier regulators, earning it a high trust rating. With decades of operating history, the broker has a wealth of forex industry experience to draw from, which is reflected in the high quality of the research and trading tools available to clients.

In this review of OANDA, we focused on the UK entity (OANDA Europe Ltd.), which is regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). We conducted our tests on the Standard account via the OANDA Trade Web Platform. Some features and services may vary depending on where you reside.

Are Fees at OANDA Competitive?

With a Standard account, I judged the fees at OANDA to be roughly average for the industry. Substantially lower costs are available via the Elite Trader account type, and clients can earn up to $17 in rebates per million units traded when minimum trading volumes are met.

Platforms and Tools

OANDA excels in this category with a broad range of proprietary and third-party platforms. Clients can choose between the OANDA Web platform, MetaTrader 4, TradingView, and the OANDA mobile app. My evaluation indicated that this variety of platforms can cater to beginners and advanced traders.

OANDA Web Platform

The OANDA Web platform is well-designed and easy to navigate. It is also customizable, allowing you to change the layout to suit your preference. Multiple chart layouts are available, and traders can view up to 8 charts at once. This feature lets traders view charts across numerous instruments and timeframes on one screen.
Charts

The platform features TradingView charts, which have over 100 indicators, over 50 drawing tools, 9 time frames, and 11 chart types. Users can also trade directly from the chart.

Orders

chunked.content:
The range of order types on the OANDA Web platform is impressive. Standard order types such as market, limit, and stop-loss are available. It is possible to select âtime in forceâ conditions, meaning that you can set your limit or stop-loss order to expire after a set time. In addition, trailing stop-loss orders are available.

The OANDA Web platform also has built-in Order Book, Heatmap, and Position Ratios tools.

The Order Book tool shows data on the open positions and orders of all the traders and investors using OANDA for a given instrument. This data can give traders a clue about the level of liquidity in the market at different price levels and where there may be strong support and resistance.
The Heatmap tool shows the major market movers, providing traders with ideas for interesting currencies to trade for the day.

The Position Ratios tool shows the percentage of OANDA traders who are long and short in each currency pair. This is called sentiment data and it provides powerful insight into the psychology of a market. Traders can interpret the data in a variety of ways. Most commonly, it is understood that when an extreme percentage of traders are either long or short an instrument, a trend reversal may be imminent.

Alerts and 1-click trading are not available on the OANDA Web platform. These features are available on MT4, the TradingView platform, and the OANDA mobile app.

My Key Takeaways after Testing the OANDA Web Platform

Having spent over two years reviewing the platforms of leading forex brokers, I rate OANDA Web as better than average. I appreciated its flexible order types, robust charting, and real-time news feed from Dow Jones. My experience trading forex showed me that sentiment data is an especially valuable indicator, so I was impressed to see the Position Ratios tool providing insights into the trading activity of OANDAâs large client base. The OANDA Web platform has a user-friendly UX that can accommodate beginners and also advanced proprietary features to satisfy experienced traders.

TradingView

The TradingView platform offers one-click trading, trading from the chart, watchlists, market news, and trading ideas. Traders can easily place trades and manage open positions and pending orders from the platform.

The industry-leading TradingView charts feature 11 time frames, 11 chart types, and over 100 technical indicators. A wide range of drawing tools, from trend lines to Fibonacci retracements, are also available.

The range of available order types is excellent. Market orders, limit orders, stop-loss orders, and trailing stop-loss orders are available. Traders also have the option to apply time-in-force conditions such as Good-Til-Canceled (GTC).

Users can draw inspiration from the massive community active on TradingView with features such as the ideas stream. The TradingView platform has the rare combination of being powerful in its functionality and intuitive with a well-designed interface.

My Key Takeaways after Testing TradingView

My initial impression of the TradingView platform was that its design and usability are second to none. Compared to other brokers, I judged it to be one of the best browser-based platforms on the market. Advanced charting and order types are available, and the platform draws from the wisdom of the crowd with cutting-edge features like its ideas stream. With 1-click trading and trading from the chart, I rate TradingView as a platform that can cater to day traders and scalpers as well as longer-term investors.

MetaTrader 4 Desktop

OANDA offers MetaTrader 4 for desktop, which includes advanced functions such as copy trading and automated trading.

MetaTrader 4 is available in 39 languages, from Arabic to Vietnamese. The platform provides popular features such as:

  • Alerts. This feature allows traders to be updated when an instrument reaches a specific price level. The platform can deliver alerts via audio, email, or push notification to a mobile device.
  • Watchlists. Traders can create a list of their favorite instruments and follow live quotes in a market watch panel.
  • One-Click Trading. This feature allows traders to execute orders with a single click and no secondary confirmation. This feature enables traders to operate faster and is especially useful for short-term traders.
  • Trading from the Chart. MT4 also allows users the convenience of trading directly from the chart.

MetaTrader also delivers when it comes to the range of available order types. The platform offers the following order types:

  • Market Order. Traders use market orders to buy or sell an instrument at the best current price.
  • Limit Order. Traders use limit orders to buy or sell an instrument at a specified price or better.
  • Stop Loss Order. Traders use stop-loss orders to buy or sell an instrument when its price reaches a specified level.
  • Trailing Stop Order. Traders use trailing stop-loss orders as a stop-loss order at a defined percentage or dollar amount away from an instrumentâs current market price. Trailing stop orders allows traders to secure profits when they are in a winning trade while not having to exit the position.

Charting features are robust. MetaTrader 4 offers:

  • 30 Technical Indicators. These include classic trend indicators, volume indicators, and oscillators.
  • 23 Analytical Objects. These include lines, channels, Gann, and Fibonacci tools.
  • 9 Time Frames. Traders can choose from nine time frames, from one minute to one month.
  • 3 Chart Types. Traders can use Bar Charts, Japanese Candlestick Charts, and Line Charts.

MetaTrader is also popular due to its copy trading and automated trading features.

  • Trading Signals. Signals in MetaTrader 4 allow users to copy other tradersâ activity in real time.
  • Automated Trading. MetaTrader 4 allows users to develop, test, and apply Expert Advisors (EAs). EAs are programs that monitor and trade markets using algorithms.

The MetaTrader 4 desktop platform is one of the most feature-rich and popular trading platforms. It does not have the most beautiful interface and requires some time and effort to learn, but that is typical of advanced platforms.

My Key Takeaways after Testing MetaTrader 4

The look and feel of MetaTrader 4 are a bit dated â I felt there is room for improvement in design and usability. But as one of the most popular trading platforms in the world and the only one offered by many forex brokers, I have spent a lot of time testing it.

MT4 is actually very well-rounded and can do more than most competitors â with advanced charting, a complete range of order types, and popular features like 1-click trading, trading from the chart, and alerts. The advanced features of the desktop platform set it apart in that it enables traders to run and backtest automated strategies.

Although it presents a steep learning curve, MT4 can cater to beginners. Meanwhile, its algorithmic trading capability and MAM/PAMM solutions can also accommodate professional traders and money managers.

OANDA Mobile App

OANDAâs mobile app has an intuitive and user-friendly interface. The same range of standard and advanced order types on the OANDA Web platform is available on the app. The layout is customizable, so you can see your favorite instruments and adjust the size of the charts to suit your preferences.

The charting within the app is solid and has the following features:

  • 16 time frames, ranging from 5 seconds to one month.
  • 9 chart types, including Japanese candlesticks, Heikin Ashi, and OHLC (open-high-low-close).
  • 15 overlays, from Bollinger Bands to exponential moving averages.
  • 17 indicators, including MACD (moving average convergence/divergence) and RSI (relative strength index).
  • 11 drawing tools, from pivot points to Fibonacci retracements.

Unlike the web interface, one-click trading and alerts are available via the app. Real-time news from Dow Jones and an economic calendar is also built-in. Two-factor authentication (2FA) is available to add an extra level of security when you sign in to OANDAâs trading platforms from your computer or mobile device. If you need to top-up your account on the go, it is possible to add funds via mobile. The app is available in English, German, Japanese and Chinese.

My Key Takeaways after Testing OANDA US Mobile App

After two weeks of testing the OANDA Mobile app, I rate it as easy to use and feature-rich. Attention to detail is reflected in advanced settings, such as the ability to configure the daily candle start and end times. Compared with dozens of trading apps I have reviewed, I judged the design and usability of OANDAâs app as above average. With advanced order types, robust charting, real-time news, and alerts, this app is suitable for both beginners and advanced traders.

Order Execution

The US division of OANDA (OANDA Corporation) is a market maker broker. Market makers typically generate revenue through the bid/offer spread. Market makers attempt to match client orders to avoid trading directly in the market and increase their spread capture.

Tradable Instruments

OANDA Corporation (the US entity of OANDA) offers clients a range of forex pairs and spot cryptocurrencies through Paxos*. Traders can access major, minor, and exotic currency pairs as well as popular cryptocurrencies via a separate account.

*Cryptocurrencies are offered through Paxos which is a separate legal entity from OANDA.

CFD trading is not allowed in the United States due to restrictions by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on over-the-counter (OTC) instruments. OTC trading is done directly between two parties without going through a financial exchange.

OANDA Corporation offers trading in forex and a range of popular cryptocurrencies. At the time of this writing, clients can access the following tradable instruments:

  • 8 Cryptocurrencies with Paxos*. Major and minor coins, such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Uniswap.

OANDA is one of a handful of brokers offering spot forex trading in the United States. After testing the available instruments at OANDA US for two weeks, I judged that it provides a good range of pairs to work with.

United States traders can experience trading popular pairs like EUR/USD, more volatile minor pairs like GBP/JPY, and even exotic pairs like TRY/JPY. The option of trading popular spot cryptocurrencies in addition to forex is rare in the US and enhances the overall offering.

Overall, the range of instruments can cater to beginners, and there is also enough variety to satisfy advanced traders.

Customer Support

OANDA offers customer support 24/5 via live chat and phone (212 858 7690). Support via email (frontdesk@oanda.com) is 24/7. I tested and rated support at OANDA as better than average for the industry in light of its fast and helpful responses in dozens of tests.

I tested customer support with various queries, ranging from platforms to tradable instruments. Chat support responded within seconds, and emails were typically responded to the same day or within one business day.

Via phone, navigating a series of automated questions designed to segment callers was necessary, but ultimately I received good support from industry-savvy agents.

OANDA offers free demo accounts via the OANDA Trade web platform, the OANDA mobile app, and MetaTrader 4. Demo accounts are a boon for beginners, allowing them to practice their strategies and get comfortable with the trading platform without risking any real money.

The demo account features live quotes and simulates live market conditions in multiple forex pairs. Once users have gotten up to speed on a demo account, they can easily switch over to a live version.

Leverage

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is using borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

For US clients, OANDA offers a maximum of 1:50 in leverage. 1:50 leverage means that with $1,000 of funds in an account, a trader can take on up to $50,000 worth of market positions.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders must remember that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

Research

OANDA hits the mark in the area of research, with industry-leading analysis available from the MarketPulse website and news from Dow Jones. A strong flow of frequently updated content is provided in written, video, and podcast formats.

OANDAâs news and research portal, MarketPulse.com, offers insightful analysis covering both fundamental and technical analysis across forex, indices, commodities, and cryptocurrencies. The Week Ahead articles keep traders abreast of upcoming economic events and what to expect. Other articles and videos are more technical, and traders can get ideas from chart patterns and support and resistance levels.

News from Dow Jones is available from OANDAâs web, desktop, and mobile platforms. The global team of Dow Jones business news reporters and editors provides:

  • Real-time breaking news
  • Expert trend analysis
  • In-depth policy commentary

OANDA US clients also have access to powerful third-party tools: AutoChartist, MotiveWave, and MultiCharts.

  • Autochartist automatically identifies chart patterns and key price levels and uses this information to predict the most likely direction of the trend.
  • MotiveWave provides advanced charting capabilities for strategy backtesting, strategy optimization, and replay mode.
  • MultiCharts is available via the OANDA Application Programming Interface (API) and offers high-definition charting, dynamic strategy backtesting, and EasyLanguage support.

My Key Takeaways after Examining OANDA US Research Section

I came away feeling like OANDA US checks all the boxes regarding research. Its decades of experience in the forex market are reflected in the high-quality analysis of MarketPulse writers. Traders can rely on fast updates on major news events and economic releases from the Dow Jones news feed.

I was most impressed by the powerful proprietary research tools, including sentiment analysis, within the OANDA Web platform. The third-party research tools from MultiCharts and MotiveWave enable strategy backtesting and optimization and cater primarily to advanced traders. Meanwhile, trading ideas from Autochartist are easy for beginners to grasp.

Education

OANDA has an impressive range of educational offerings, from platform tutorials to live webinars with industry experts. The volume and quality of the materials are better than average for the industry.

OANDAâs educational resources include a wide variety of educational articles, videos, and live webinars.

The trading resources section on Oanda.com covers basics like leveraged trading to more advanced themes, including technical analysis, indicators, and trading strategies. I liked that OANDA goes beyond theory and delves into practical topics like finding good entry and exit points for a trade.

Learning from industry experts in a live setting is one of the best ways of building a foundation of market knowledge. OANDA delivers in this area with live and recorded webinars spanning topics like risk management, Fibonacci, and platform tutorials.

The Trade Tap blog is another great resource, providing clients with further market insights. Long-form articles tackle themes like Crypto Technical Analysis and How to use Divergence Analysis in Your Trading.

The Bottom Line

OANDA is a forex industry pioneer with over 25 years of experience. The companyâs US entity is one of a small number of brokers providing US residents access to the spot forex market. With a $0 minimum deposit, the barrier to entry is low, and the range of available platforms and tools is excellent.

While spreads for the Standard Account are about average for the industry, competitive trading costs are available with the Elite Trader account type. OANDA really shines in its offering of research and educational materials, which can cater to various experience levels. Reliable customer support rounds out a robust overall offering from this broker.

OCTA Regulations

When we review brokers, we look at the licenses held by each of their entities to understand how well they protect clients. We use a simple three-tier system to rank regulatory bodies, with Tier 1 being the most trusted and offering the highest level of protection.

This is what I discovered about the four entities operating under the OCTA trade name:

  • OCTA Markets Cyprus Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) under license number 372/18. We rate CySEC as a Tier-1 regulator.

OCTA Swaps

A swap fee is a traderâs cost for holding an open position overnight because of changing interest rates. Swap long refers to the charge deductible or credit receivable for holding a buy position open overnight. In turn, swap short relates to the charges/credits deductible or receivable for holding a selling position open overnight.

OCTAâs unique approach to swaps sets it apart from other brokers. All available assets are swap-free, with no hidden costs or extra commissions. This makes OCTA an attractive option for traders who hold positions overnight.

Orders

OctaTrader features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which supports immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the OctaTrader platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries, but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and trigger the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you loseâwithout ever buying real gold.

The biggest perk? You can jump in or out of the market quickly to take advantage of even the smallest price changes.

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

The brokerâs YouTube channel hosts over 400 educational videos and past webinars, tackling topics as simple as the ABCs of trading and as complex as Elliott Wave strategies. Fresh webinars are published regularly in English, Malay, Thai, Spanish, and Portuguese, catering to all experience levelsâfrom first-time traders to market veterans. OCTA has also created a detailed 11-lesson video course that dives deeper into core areas like chart analysis, market fundamentals, and building the right trading mindset.

The Bottom Line

OCTA, founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Comoros, sets itself apart with a trader-focused, innovative approach. The standout features include its AI-powered market research, extensive educational resources, and the sleek OctaTrader platform, which provides a refreshing alternative to MetaTrader 4 and 5. The brokerâs policy of offering swap-free trading on all instruments, at no extra cost, is a rare advantage in the industry.

When stacked against competitors, OCTA lands in the mid-range for fees. While spreads on EURUSD and share CFDs are impressively tight, costs on commodities and indicesâespecially crude oilâare noticeably higher than average. Still, the lack of non-trading fees and its universal swap-free structure give it a significant edge for traders who hold positions overnight.

Overall, OCTAâs offering is well-suited for long-term traders, investors, day traders, and copy traders alike. Although its lineup of instruments could be expanded to include more low-risk securities like ETFs or bonds, it delivers strong value through its platform innovation, accessible account structure, and a combination of features that blend usability with robust market insights.

chunked.content:
Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All Plus500 entities ensure this.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. All Plus500 entities provide negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects retail traders against the brokerâs liabilities in the unlikely event that the company becomes insolvent. Clients of Plus500CY Ltd are insured by the Investor Compensation Scheme (ICF) for up to â¬20,000.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. Plus500CY Ltd offers leverage of up to 1:30, while Plus500SEY Ltd provides the highest leverage, offering up to 1:300.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall transparency.

Plus500 was founded in 2008, marking it as an experienced CFD broker with a substantial track record. According to its LinkedIn page, the company is headquartered in London and has 201-500 employees.

My research showed that Plus500 is highly transparent about its regulatory status, listing its regulators in the footer of each page of its website. The website breaks down fees clearly on the Fees and Charges page. Further details can be found in the User Agreement on the Terms and Agreements page.

Is Plus500 Safe to Trade With?

To sum it up, Plus500 stands out as a highly trusted and stable broker thanks to these key qualities:

Plus500 WebTrader Platform

Plus500`s flagship trading platform, WebTrader, is accessible via a web browser and a Microsoft Windows app. It is available in 31 languages and features two-factor authentication for additional security when you log in.

WebTrader allows users to easily create watchlists, analyze charts, enter trades, and monitor market positions. The platform makes it easy to switch between demo and live trading with a single click. A dark mode option helps make the screen easier on the eyes at night.

Traders often need to pull up an instrument at short notice, so a good search is an essential feature of a trading platform. Plus500 WebTrader has an excellent search tool at the top of the screen, making it easy to find whatever asset you want to access.

Charts

The WebTrader platform offers robust charting capabilities. The range includes 20 chart types, such as Candles, Renko, and Range Bars.

Traders can apply over 100 technical indicators to their charts along with classic drawing tools like Fibonacci retracement levels. There are eleven available time frames for charts, ranging from one minute to one week.

The platform is customizable, and a helpful feature called Multiple Charts View allows you to view numerous charts laid out to your preference on the same screen.

Orders

WebTrader provides all standard order types, such as market, limit, and stop loss. More advanced trailing stop orders are also available.

  • Market Order: Traders use market orders to buy or sell an instrument at the best current price.
  • Limit Order: Traders use limit orders to buy or sell an instrument at a specified price or better.
  • Stop-Loss Order: Traders use stop-loss orders to buy or sell an instrument when its price reaches a specified level.
  • Trailing Stop Order: Traders use trailing stop-loss orders as a stop-loss order at a defined percentage or number of pips away from an instrumentâs current market price.

Plus500 Alerts

Alerts from the WebTrader platform can update you when the price of an asset reaches a certain level or changes by a set percentage. Clients can also receive notifications when tradersâ sentiment hits a specified level.

Alerts can be sent by email, SMS, or push notifications. The minimalist layout of the platform makes these functions effortless to use.

Plus500 WebTrader: My Key Takeaways

WebTrader is an exceptional platform for casual traders and swing traders thanks to its first-class design and usability.

Beyond design, it offers powerful charting and flexible order types. Better-than-average trading tools, research, and customer support are all available without leaving the platformâa major bonus, in my view.

It is not for every trader, though. The lack of 1-click trading and trading from the chart makes WebTrader unsuitable for day traders and scalpers. The platform also does not offer automated trading or copy trading features.

Plus500 Mobile App

The Plus500 mobile app, available for iOS and Android, offers nearly the same set of tools as the WebTrader platform.

The app has an intuitive interface and offers a range of great features, including:

  • Two-Factor Authentication: Users can improve their account security by requiring a verification code sent via SMS for every new device login.
  • Demo Mode: Users can easily switch between a demo account and live trading within the app.
  • Diverse Order Types: The app offers market, limit, stop-loss, and trailing stop orders.
  • Alerts: Users can set alerts to be sent via email, SMS, or push notification when an asset reaches a set level.
  • Economic Calendar: The Plus500 economic calendar shows all the key information about upcoming releases, such as the expected market impact, analyst expectations, and figures from previous releases.

Charting on the mobile app is robust and provides:

  • 13 Chart Types: A broader than average range, from Bar charts to Point & Figure charts.
  • 11 Time Frames: These range from 1 Minute to 1 Week.
  • 100+ Indicators: An extensive range of indicators (more than MetaTrader) â from Accumulation/Distribution to ZigZag.
  • 22 Drawing Tools: These include classics such as Fibonacci, Gartley, and Pitchfork.

Plus500 Mobile App: My Key Takeaways

Overall, I concluded that this is an excellent app with a superb design and robust built-in tools. With features like +Insights research, market news, and an economic calendar, the Plus500 app goes above and beyond the average broker app. However, like WebTrader, it lacks 1-click trading for speedy order entry.

Plus500 Order Execution Model

Plus500 is the counterparty to clientsâ trades. In other words, Plus500 transacts with clients as a principal on the basis of a quote. The broker acts as the sole execution venue and as the principal in all client trades. All trades are executed by Plus500 using the Plus500 Ltd trading platform, and for each trade, an identical hedge trade takes place between Plus500 and Plus500 Ltd.

A Contract for Difference (CFD) is an agreement specifying that the buyer must pay the seller the difference between an assetâs current value and its value at the time the contract was initiated. Like futures and other derivative financial instruments, CFDs allow traders to speculate on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex and CFD markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is the use of borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

For the Plus500CY Ltd entity, the maximum leverage for a retail account is 1:30. This means that with an account of $1,000, you can control up to $30,000 worth of positions in the market. This level of leverage carries substantial risk.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders should keep in mind that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

The Bottom Line

Plus500 takes a different approach from other leading CFD brokers in that it does not try to appeal to every kind of trader. Rather, it has focused on technology and innovation to create what I rate as the most user-friendly and smooth CFD trading experience available.

Everything about this broker â from the website to its platform and ever-present customer support â removes the usual friction of getting started and becoming active in financial markets.

Plus500 excelled in our Trust category, with its large global presence as a multi-regulated and publicly traded broker. Its range of instruments is also remarkable, beating the industry average in every asset class and featuring unusual assets like options and extended-hours stocks.

The Plus500 WebTrader platform and mobile app are outstanding in their design and usability for casual and position traders. Unique research tools like +Insights underscore the brokerâs commitment to innovation. However, the WebTrader platform lacks features suitable for short-term traders like day traders and scalpers.

Trading costs reflected in the spreads are not highly competitive overall. However, I would point out that these initial costs of entering a trade are much less important when you are placing fewer trades and holding positions for longer periods, as the platform is geared towards.

Educational and research materials are solid, but in line with the theme of the broker, are more suitable for new/casual traders rather than professionals.

If you are looking to dip your toes into the financial markets for the first time or have a full-time occupation and would like an easy solution for getting involved with trading and investing, I rate Plus500 as a strong choice.

How PrimeXBT Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

  • Segregation of Client Fund: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts, separate from those used for the brokerâs corporate capital, mitigates the risk of accounting errors. All of PrimeXBTâs entities ensure this.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. All PrimeXBT entities provide negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects clients if a broker becomes insolvent. PrimeXBT does not offer a government-backed compensation scheme, but all clients have access to The Financial Commission, an independent dispute resolution body that can award compensation in eligible cases.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Founded in 2018, PrimeXBT has a moderate operating history in the industry. According to its LinkedIn profile, the company employs between 201 and 500 staff, indicating a mid-sized operation.

PrimeXBT provides standard corporate and regulatory information transparently, with its entities listed in both the website footer and on a dedicated Regulation page. Trading costs are clearly outlined in the Fees and Conditions section, and more detailed terms can be found in the Legal Documents area, including the full Terms and Conditions.

I rate PrimeXBT as having an average level of transparency, although it could be made clearer where the broker is based.

Is PrimeXBT Safe to Trade With?

To conclude, my findings indicate that PrimeXBT can be regarded as having a mixed level of trust and stability due to the following factors:

  • All entities segregate funds
  • All entities offer negative balance protection
  • Adequate level of transparency

The broker does not charge fees for deposits or withdrawals, and there are no inactivity fees.

There are also educational explainers covering trading concepts and crypto market dynamics, which can support beginners as they build their knowledge. The Bottom Line

Founded in 2018, PrimeXBT is a modern, crypto-focused multi-asset broker offering over 190 CFDs, plus access to real crypto and futures trading. Education is above average thanks to videos, articles, webinars, and Trading Central insights for funded clients. On the downside, the range of stock CFDs is limited, thereâs no phone support, and VPS hosting isnât offered.

I consider PrimeXBT a flexible, modern platform that gives access to trade CFDs and futures from a single login. Thanks to its intuitive PXTrader 2.0 platform, low spreads on EUR/USD and gold, and a decent selection of educational materials, I rate RpimeXBT a strong choice for both beginners and casual traders.

Intuitive design with clean charts. The greatest advantage of the PU Web Trader over MetaTrader is its superior charting capabilities. Universal and highly customizable. PU Web Trader is compatible with all major browsers and available in 21 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and more.

PU Web Trader also lets you set your preferred leverage rate from 1:100 to 1:1000. This feature allows you to configure your exposure as per the current market sentiment. Accordingly, you can use higher leverage in less volatile markets or lower your leverage when the market seems more erratic.

Extra details on instruments. Before placing an order, I recommend checking exactly what you plan to trade â how much it will cost you, how much you plan to trade, and when you can place the order.   • 60+ drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting. I use tools like Fibonacci retracement levels to identify major support and resistance levels within a price trend. I then use these as reference points for possible rebounds/reversals or breakouts/breakdowns, depending on the underlying trend.
  • 9 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry. Typically, I use higher timeframes (above 4H) to determine the marketâs general direction and smaller timeframes (below 1H) to spot viable entries within the broader trend.
  • 10 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format. Personally, I prefer candlesticks because they provide a more comprehensive picture. For example, a bullish Marubozu candlestick may signify strong buying sentiment, whereas the formation of a shooting star candlestick may indicate a possible bearish reversal.

I really enjoyed tinkering with the PU Web Trader. The platformâs high-definition charts are not cluttered, even if you apply multiple drawing tools and technical indicators, and price action always remains clearly visible.

MetaTrader 5 is a solid platform for fast and straightforward trading, particularly if youâre into algorithmic strategies or use EAs. Itâs reliable, packed with tools, and supports detailed trade execution.

However, its interface feels dated compared to more modern alternatives like TradingView or cTrader. If youâre a trader who values sleek design and customizable charting, MT5 might feel a bit too rigid and visually overwhelming.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Research

PU Prime delivers strong market research, combining its own in-house content with the Autochartist package. Traders get access to a news screener, market analyses, sentiment gauges, webinars, and actionable trading signalsâall designed to help them stay on top of market developments and spot new opportunities.

Research Tools

  • Economic Calendar: The economic calendar informs traders of upcoming market events and economic releases that have the potential to stir a market reaction and therefore create viable trading opportunities.
• Market Insights: PU Primeâs news screener provides a steady flow of market analyses, breaking down key economic events and decisions and their impact on the market.

• Currency Heatmap: This sentiment gauge helps traders track the changing strengths of instruments across various asset classes compared to other instruments from the same market. Traders are thus presented with a quick overview of changing buying and selling pressures.

• Autochartist Content: Autochartist is a well-known tool for market reviews and technical breakdowns. What makes it especially useful is that it highlights trading setups as theyâre developing. Each idea comes with entry and exit points, stop-loss levels, and key support and resistance zones, giving traders a clear roadmap for potential trades.

PU Prime Research: My Key Takeaways

PU Prime really stands out with its well-rounded market research, catering to both day traders and swing traders. The steady stream of market news, easy-to-use sentiment gauges, and actionable trading signals create a layered and sophisticated package. What I liked most is the balance between PU Primeâs own in-house insights and third-party tools like Autochartist, which makes the research both practical and versatile.

Education

PU Prime goes the extra mile with its rich educational resources. The broker offers a mix of videos, articles, regular webinars, and a full trading academy. The content is well-structured, easy to follow, and packed with useful insightsâmaking it a solid fit for both beginners and more experienced traders.

I counted 48 educational videos on PU Primeâs YouTube channel. Theyâre light, easy to follow, and give beginners a hands-off way to start learning. The broker also runs regular webinars, which provide live coverage of major market events and economic releases.

I especially liked PU Primeâs trading academy, which features around 150 articles on key topics like technical and fundamental analysis, trading psychology, and risk management. The content is well-structured and layered, making it useful for everyoneâfrom complete beginners to more advanced traders.

The cherry on top is PU Primeâs Trading Quizzes section, which allows traders to test their knowledge at their own pace.

The Bottom Line

PU Prime has grown into a solid all-round broker since its launch in 2015, offering 960+ instruments and a well-balanced mix of forex, stocks, cryptos, ETFs, and bonds. Its research and education stand out, with in-house insights, Autochartist integration, and a structured trading academy thatâs more advanced than most competitors.

On the safety side, PU Prime covers its bases with four regulated entities, segregated accounts, negative balance protection, and even private indemnity insuranceâsomething few brokers provide. The only drawback is that one entity remains unregulated, though overall protections are stronger than the industry norm.

I enjoyed using PU Web Trade for its intuitive design and high-definition charts. While the proprietary platform doesnât natively support one-click trading or automated strategies via Expert Advisors (EAs), you can easily bridge this gap by using MT4 or MT5. Additionally, the PU Prime app performed reliably during my testing, making it a great tool for trading on the go.

In terms of costs, spreads are generally mid-range, but I found them impressively tight on share CFDs and BTCUSD, which makes PU Prime competitive where it counts. Add in the fact that there are no non-trading fees (like deposit, withdrawal, or inactivity charges), and itâs cost-friendly compared to many rivals.

Customer support was quick and is available in several languages, though itâs not flawlessâI noticed a small gap in accuracy during testing.

Thanks to its $50 entry-level account, copy trading, and strong education, PU Prime is a great fit for new traders. While raw spread accounts, VPS reimbursement, and robust algo support benefit and advanced traders and professionals.

Our Take on PU Prime

PU Prime is a well-rounded financial derivatives broker that has built a solid reputation since its launch in 2015. Headquartered in Mauritius and backed by multiple licenses, the broker gives traders access to more than 960 instruments across forex, commodities, indices, shares, cryptocurrencies, bonds, and ETFs.

In my testing, I found PU Primeâs fees favorable. Spreads are generally in line with the industry average, but particularly tight on share CFDs and BTCUSD. I also liked that the broker doesnât charge non-trading fees, making it more cost-effective than many competitors.

What really sets PU Prime apart is its strong research and education. Traders get access to in-house market insights alongside the Autochartist package, plus regular webinars and a rich library of articles and videos.

On the platform side, PU Prime has developed its own PU Web Trader with superior charting capabilities and an all-in-one PU Prime App. It also offers MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 and supports copy and automated trading.

My only small gripe was with customer support, which wasnât always as sharp as the brokerâs performance in other areas.

Overall, Iâd say PU Prime is a great choice for a wide range of tradersâfrom complete beginners just starting out to advanced algo traders looking for low spreads and strong tools.

According to its LinkedIn page, RoboForex has been around since 2009 and employs nearly 200 professionals worldwide. I reviewed the brokerâs website and legal documents, and everything checked out. MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I tested the MetaTrader 5 (MT5) desktop platform and found it relatively easy to navigate. The main dashboard is intuitive, with charts, order types, and trading instruments located in familiar places. Even first-time users can pick up the basics without much effort.

However, the platform design feels a bit outdated. Compared to more modern trading platforms, MT5âs chart visuals are rugged and lack the sleek, polished look that many traders today prefer.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by RoboForex is available for Windows and Mac users and supports 52 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese â making it accessible to traders around the globe.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

In my view, MT5 really shines when it comes to automated trading. It supports Expert Advisors (EAs) and comes with an easy-to-use strategy tester, allowing algo traders to fine-tune their systems for different market conditions.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is loaded with analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format.

That said, the charts can get visually cluttered quite fast â even when only two indicators are active. This can make it harder to interpret price action clearly and may not be ideal for traders who rely heavily on clean, minimalistic chart setups.

Order Types

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a reliable platform for fast and straightforward trading, especially if you use algorithmic strategies or Expert Advisors (EAs). Itâs packed with tools, supports detailed trade execution, and has long been a favorite among forex traders.

That said, the interface feels a bit dated compared to more modern platforms like TradingView or cTrader. Another limitation at RoboForex is that MT5 only provides access to around 200 CFD instruments. To tap into the brokerâs full product offering, including thousands of stocks and ETFs, youâll need to use the R StocksTrader platform.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

MT5 App: My Key Takeaways

The MetaTrader app stands out for its convenience, making it an essential tool for adjusting trades, especially during periods of heightened volatility. However, it is cumbersome and not the best choice for analyzing price action.

R StocksTrader

The R StocksTrader web platform feels lighter and more modern than MetaTrader. Itâs intuitive to use, easy to navigate, and supports key order types like market, limit, and stop orders. This makes it a solid choice for traders who want a clean interface without sacrificing functionality.

Traders can customize their favorite watchlists, place trading alerts, and use the one-click trading functionality. The platform also features 38 technical indicators, 31 drawing tools, 10 timeframes, and 5 chart types.

VPS Hosting

RoboForex also offers Virtual Private Server (VPS) hosting for traders who need low-latency execution, which is especially useful for running automated strategies. The service is free if you trade at least three lots per month; otherwise, it comes with a modest $5 monthly fee.

RoboForex Execution Model

RoboForex operates on a hybrid STP/ECN model without a dealing desk. Client orders are either routed to the brokerâs pool of liquidity providers, where they are filled at the best available price, or they are matched electronically (buying orders to selling orders and vice versa) using communication networks.

MetaTrader 5 is a solid platform for fast and straightforward trading, particularly if youâre into algorithmic strategies or use EAs. Itâs reliable, packed with tools, and supports detailed trade execution.

However, its interface feels dated compared to more modern alternatives like TradingView or cTrader. If youâre a trader who values sleek design and customizable charting, MT5 might feel a bit too rigid and visually overwhelming.

• News Screener: This tool allows traders to stay on top of the latest market developments. It tracks economic releases and financial updates and breaks down their immediate impact on the market.

Rock-West Research: My Key Takeaways

In my view, Rock-Westâs research is useful but pretty basic. The technical analysis feels a bit rough and only gives a surface-level look at trading opportunities. Whatâs missing are price chart breakdowns, which are crucial for this kind of content. I also think the broker could really benefit from adding third-party research tools like Trading Central and Autochartist to bring in more depth and perspective.

Education

Rock-West offers several dozen articles and videos covering the basics of crude oil and crypto trading. The content is easy to grasp, but generally lacking depth. Not enough attention is paid to the intricacies of technical analysis, fundamental analysis, or trading psychology.

Rock-West has published over 50 educational articles on its website, available from the Info Centre section. These are mostly opinion pieces that touch on general trading topics like the habits of successful traders. While easy to read, I found the content too broad and lacking depthâthereâs little on practical skills such as reading price action or applying proper risk management.

The brokerâs YouTube channel adds a few dozen how-to videos, but these too are basic and unsophisticated, offering limited value for traders who want detailed, actionable guidance.

The Bottom Line

After testing Rock-West, Iâd say itâs a broker that leans heavily toward crypto traders. With 168+ digital assets and some of the tightest BTC/USD spreads Iâve seen (sometimes under $1), itâs one of the better options in the industry if your focus is on cryptocurrencies.

That said, once you step outside of crypto, the picture changes. Forex, indices, and commodities spreads were average to high in my tests, and the complete lack of share CFDs or ETFs makes the overall product range feel limited compared to most brokers. The educational content is also quite basic, which makes Rock-West less appealing for beginners.

On the safety side, Rock-West is licensed by the FSA Seychelles, an offshore regulator. It does segregate client funds, but the absence of negative balance protection and a compensation scheme puts it behind brokers regulated in stricter jurisdictions.

Overall, I see Rock-West as a solid choice for traders who prioritize crypto variety and copy trading tools. But if youâre looking for a wider range of assets, consistently lower costs, or tighter regulatory safeguards, Rock-West may not fully meet those expectations.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of client funds. Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Client funds are kept in segregated accounts with Shares.com.
  • Negative balance protection. This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance for retail clients. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. The broker guarantees negative balance protection.
  • Compensation scheme. A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Clients of Shares.com are not protected under a compensation scheme.
  • Maximum leverage. Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with Shares.com is 1:200.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

I reviewed Shares.comâs legal documents and assessed that everything was in order. Client protections are clearly outlined in the client agreement, which is easily accessible and written in an easy-to-understand way. Moreover, the broker displays live spread data on the website.

I also discovered that Shares.com has issued a âbest execution policy,â which is a legal mandate to provide traders with optimal price quotes under the prevailing market conditions. Additionally, the broker has a robust client categorization policy and complaints handling policy.

Is Shares.com Safe to Trade With?

I determined that Shares.com can be considered safe to trade with due to the following factors:

  • Licensed and regulated
  • Keeps client funds in segregated accounts
  • Ensures negative balance protection
  • Provides transparent legal documents

I have broken down the three primary order types on the Shares.com web trader below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

Shares.com Platform: My Key Takeaways
