SimpleFX Regulations

In our reviews, we examine the licenses and regulations of each entity operated by a broker, allowing us to compare their different levels of protection. We rank licenses by various regulatory bodies on a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing indicates the highest level of regulation.

This is what I discovered about the two entities operating under the SimpleFX trade name:

  • 8TECH ZA (Pty) Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) of South Africa under license number 53073. We rate the FSCA as a Tier-2 regulator.
  • 8Tech SVG (formerly SimpleFX Ltd) is registered in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines under register number 22361 BC 2014. The entity is not regulated.
  • 8tech Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) of Mauritius under license number GB23201604. We rate the FSC as a Tier-3 regulator.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity they choose to open an account with.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of client funds. Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Client funds are kept in segregated accounts with both SimpleFX entities.
  • Negative balance protection. This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. Both SimpleFX entities claim to provide negative balance protection.
  • Compensation scheme. A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. SimpleFX clients are not protected by a compensation scheme.
  • Maximum leverage. Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with SimpleFX is 1:1000.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

SimpleFX has been operational for over a decade, which attests to its well-functioning business model. I went over the brokerâs legal documents, including its Client Agreement, and assessed that everything was in order. All important information is readily available and easy to discern.

Additionally, I discovered that the Mauritius-based entity operates on a âbest executionâ basis, whereby itâs required to provide its clients with the most optimal price quotes under the prevailing market conditions.

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

SimpleFXâs market research is comprised exclusively of content developed in-house, including a variety of market breakdowns, insights, and featured trading ideas. The content is updated frequently, though some of the materials lack depth.

  • Trading News: The brokerâs platform also has a built-in news screener so that traders can stay informed about recent news and market developments.
  • Featured Trading Ideas: SimpleFX platform users have access to actionable trading ideas that heavily emphasize technical analysis. While the charts are well-structured, this type of content lacks proper explanations.

SimpleFX Research: My Key Takeaways

As a whole, SimpleFXâs research content is sufficiently diverse, though it lacks depth in some aspects. While its market insights are very informative, its trading ideas often lack context. In my view, SimpleFX could improve its market research by incorporating content from third-party providers, such as Trading Central or Autochartist. This would make the brokerâs offering a lot more nuanced.

Education
SimpleFX has a detailed glossary, a blog with several dozen articles, and several educational videos on its YouTube channel. However, the brokerâs educational content lacks structure and depth.

SimpleFX has published 27 platform and app tutorials on its YouTube channel. It also has more than 100 written articles in its blog, though not all of these are purely educational. Finally, the broker has a pretty detailed glossary.

The Bottom Line

SimpleFX is a multi-asset derivatives broker offering over 1000 CFDs across forex, commodities, shares, indices, cryptocurrencies, and bonds.

The broker has developed its own versatile, feature-rich trading platform, which is seamlessly integrated with TradingView. It also provides trading APIs and a solid selection of market research content, making it a suitable choice for day traders and algorithmic traders. Additionally, it offers unique features like the âStake&Tradeâ service.

However, SimpleFXâs trading fees are higher than the industry average, and it lacks copy trading and Islamic (swap-free) accounts. Overall, I consider SimpleFX a decent financial derivatives broker, though there is room for improvement.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

On top of that, Spreadex has a best execution policy, meaning itâs legally bound to give clients the best possible price quotes under current market conditions.

That said, my only real gripe is that the broker doesnât publish daily swaps or rollover data. The platform points you back to the website for funding numbers, but I couldnât actually find them listed anywhere.

  • Protects client money from the brokerâs credit risk.

The Bottom Line

Spreadex is a long-standing, FCA-regulated broker that has carved out a niche with its excellent web platform, TradingView integration, and a product lineup that few competitors can match.

Beyond the usual forex, commodities, and indices, it offers hundreds of ETFs, bonds, options, and even periodic IPOsâmaking it a unique pick for traders who want access to instruments that arenât widely available elsewhere. Its platform is also a standout, packed with advanced charting tools, technical overlays, and risk management features that make it a dream for day traders, scalpers, and news traders.

On the flip side, Spreadexâs fees are a mixed bag. Add in the lack of demo accounts, automated trading, and copy trading, and it may feel limiting compared to more versatile brokers.

Still, if you value cutting-edge platforms, comprehensive research, and access to a truly unique range of instruments, Spreadex remains one of the stronger choices on the UK marketâespecially for technically driven traders who donât mind navigating slightly higher costs on certain assets.

What Are CFDs?

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you loseâwithout ever buying real gold.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money, allowing them to open larger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

STARTRADER offers penetrating and well-balanced market research. There are an economic calendar, technical and fundamental analyses, and the Trading Central package. As it stands, STARTRADERâs market research is geared mainly towards day traders.

• Market Insights: Clients of STARTRADER can stay in sync with the latest market developments thanks to the brokerâs frequent market updates. The articles are broadly separated into two categories: technical and fundamental. • Technical Breakdowns: What I found of great value with STARTRADER is its technical analyses of prominent assets, such as EURUSD, XAUUSD, BTCUSD, and more. From each article, traders can learn about currently unfolding trading setups, key resistance and support levels to watch out for, the underlying buying and selling pressures, and more. Most articles feature a supporting chart.

• Trading Central: In addition to its proprietary content, STARTRADER incorporates the Trading Central package, which features the Market Buzz feature (a market sentiment gauge), featured trading ideas, and technical breakdowns. The service is among the best and most widely used in the industry. It is available to STARTRADER clients with funded accounts with at least $200.

STARTRADER Research: My Key Takeaways

STARTRADER combines its own market research with the Trading Central content, providing its clients with a 360-degree market overview. The materials are both illuminating and written in an easy-to-understand manner. I also found that the broker used to publish video breakdowns on its YouTube channel, but no longer does.

Education

STARTRADER offers informative educational content primarily geared towards the needs of beginner and intermediate traders. The collection includes educational videos, articles, and webinars in multiple languages. My only gripe is that the educational section lacks a bit of structure.

I counted over 120 educational videos and more than 80 articles on STARTRADERâs website and YouTube channel. I was pleasantly surprised to find topics that most brokers rarely touch on â like âThe Difference Between Active and Passive Income.â However, the content lacks a clear learning path, making it less ideal for those seeking a structured educational experience.

I also appreciated that STARTRADER hosts regular webinars in English, Chinese, and Arabic, with over 40 recorded sessions available on its YouTube channel. The brokerâs experts do a great job covering essential aspects of technical and fundamental analysis, offering practical insights for traders at different skill levels.

The Bottom Line

STARTRADER strikes an impressive balance between affordability, research depth, and innovation. Its tight spreads on major assets, zero non-trading fees, and robust crypto offering â including 80 digital assets and BTC/ETH base currencies â make it stand out in a crowded market.

The broker incorporates the standard suites of MT4 and MT5, and has also developed a sophisticated mobile app offering STARTRADER clients everything they may need at their fingertips.

STARTRADER also delivers top-notch market research and illuminating educational content. The broker is tightly regulated and has taken extra precautions to protect its clients against its credit liabilities.

That said, the lack of a proprietary web platform and unclear ECN commission rates slightly dull the shine.

Compared to many brokers, STARTRADER delivers more value to active traders, particularly day traders, copy traders, and crypto CFDs enthusiasts, who seek competitive pricing and robust analytical tools.

  • Swissquote Bank Europe Ltd holds a banking license and is regulated by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) in Luxembourg, under the supervision of the European Central Bank (ECB). We rate the CSSF as a Tier-1 regulator.

The charts are wide and fluid, offering a penetrating look into price action. Searching for a particular instrument is fast and easy, and I particularly enjoyed the ease of watchlist customization. The CFXD platform lets you configure your workstation and reorganize the different panels, unlike more rugged trading platforms like MetaTrader.

Availability & Features

The CFXD platform by Swissquote is compatible with all major search browsers and supports multiple languages, including English, French, Russian, Italian, Polish, Spanish, German, and Arabic.

CFXD features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Monitor your favorite trading instruments from your custom watchlists.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.
  • FIX API Compatibility: Allows you to tap into the interbank level and obtain raw spreads directly from an exchangeâs order books. The service is primarily used for Direct Market Access (DMA), resulting in even faster execution.
  • Autochartist Research: Access actionable trading signals from Autochartist and replicate them with just a few clicks. For my review, I checked one such signal on the GBPJPY pair â an emerging ABCD pattern. It signaled the development of the final CD impulse, which was underscored by the RSI indicator and Fibonacci retracement levels. I also received the most important trade levels, including an entry price, a take profit, and a stop loss.

Charting & Analysis Tools

I learned that CFXDâs high-definition charts are powered by TradingView, which is arguably the best software for illustrating price action in high definition. I found price action fluid and easily scalable, enabling me to spot currently developing trading setups within broader, well-established trends.

CFXD is packed with analytical tools and chart configurations, including:

  • 86 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools. You can use these to spot price trends and ranges and to assess their strength.
  • 70+ drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting. I use tools like Fibonacci retracement levels to identify major support and resistance levels within a price trend. I then use these as reference points for possible rebounds/reversals or breakouts/breakdowns, depending on the underlying trend.
  • 15 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis. Notably, CFXD is one of the few platforms that features timeframes lower than 1 minute, catering to the needs of scalpers and high-frequency traders. Typically, I use higher timeframes (above 4H) to determine the marketâs general direction and smaller timeframes (below 1H) to spot viable entries within the broader trend.
  • 15 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format. I prefer using candlesticks because they provide a more comprehensive picture. For example, you can look for bearish or bullish Doji, Hammer, or Shooting Star candles at the top/bottom of price trends, as possible indications of upcoming reversals.

I enjoyed the level of customization the CFXD offers: you can apply several charts to monitor multiple markets at once, or focus on a single chart on a beautiful, wide-screen display. With just a single look, I was able to gather so much about the growing bearish momentum on the EURUSD above, thanks to CFXDâs flexibility.

I used the Ichimoku Cloud indicator, and the price action was not obscured by its multiple lines. Not only that, I was able to indicate mounting bearish sentiment, which was also reflected in the MACD stochastic indicator.

Another perk of the CFXD platform is that it lets you overlay the prices of multiple instruments on the same chart. You can use the âCompareâ tool to spot cross-market correlations.

Order Types

CFXD has a major leg up over other platforms because it supports both basic and complex order types, giving the user greater flexibility:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries.
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.
  • OCO Orders: A combination of a limit and a stop order. The instruction is to execute one when its underlying parameters are met and to terminate the other.
  • IF-Done: A two-step order whereby the execution of the primary (entry) order triggers the execution of the secondary order (e.g., for a stop-loss, take-profit, etc).
  • IF-OCO: A variation of the IF-Done order where the execution of the primary order triggers a second OCO order.

Swissquote App

I tested the Swissquote app on my personal Google Pixel phone running Android and was impressed by the mix of a light, user-friendly design and high functionality.

The app lets you trade on the go, monitor your open trades, place orders, and stay up to date with the latest market news. You can also access actionable trading signals from Autochartist from the âInspirationâ tab.

I used the app to place several market orders on the EURUSD via my demo account. Finding the instrument in the search bar, powering up the chart, and configuring the parameters for my trades was fast and easy. I did not observe any slippage.

These protocols are used to achieve fast execution speeds and obtain raw spreads directly from an exchangeâs order books. You can use FIX APIs on Swissquoteâs CFXD platform. Swissquote Execution Model

Swissquote operates on a hybrid principal/ECN model without a dealing desk. Client orders are either filled internally by the bank or matched on the interbank level using Electronic Communication Networks (ECNs). This hybrid model enables rapid order execution speeds, averaging 9 milliseconds.

Research

Swissquote provides news briefs and video breakdowns, which monitor and explain the latest market-moving headlines in great detail. They are enhanced with actionable trading signals from Autochartist, integrated directly into the CFXD platform. I tracked a GBPJPY signal by Autochartist for the formation of an ABCD pattern, and found it great for day and news traders. I also used the âInspireâ section of the website as a gateway to the brokerâs newsletter, blog, and detailed expert insights. I consider Swissquoteâs research offering to be better and broader than many other brokers.

In the Spotlight

I accessed a variety of news breakdowns and market review articles from the âIn the spotlightâ section of the Swissquote blog. These articles use fundamental and economic analysis and break down key market developments.

I read the latest article on the ramifications of Middle East tensions for energy prices and what they mean for investors. The text was very insightful and well-structured.

YouTube Content

Swissquote stays active on YouTube, publishing several videos a day. Some zoom in on basic market developments, such as XRPâs recent price gains, while others cover broader, more complex topics, such as the challenges facing Central Banks amid the energy market crisis sparked by the U.S./Iran war in the Gulf.

I watched Swissquoteâs recent video on central banksâ reaction to the Middle East tensions and was impressed by the attention to detail in Swissquoteâs hot take. The essentials behind complex geopolitical developments were captured and presented in an easy-to-understand way, even for first-time traders.

You will also find four podcast series on the Swissquote YouTube channel: âMarket Talkâ and âCrypto Talkâ that cover general market trends, as well as âUnlocked: Beyond the Headlinesâ, for those wanting to get to the nitty-gritty aspects of major market trends, and âAnnual Reportsâ covering the bankâs activity over the year.

Autochartist Content

One of the highlights of the CFXD platform is its integration with Autochartist content. You can use the various filters to find trading opportunities for a specific instrument, by a specific price pattern, or by probability.

I checked the GBPUSD pair and read about the key price levels to watch out for following the recent bearish correction. I also found the volatility forecasts quite useful for planning your trading week ahead.

Other Research Tools

Swissquote delivers a steady stream of additional research tools and services, including the Swissquote magazine and newsletter, its morning news screener, a proprietary podcast, and various sentiment gauges from the âinspirationâ section of the website.

Education

Swissquote offers an extensive collection of educational materials, including articles, videos, regular webinars, and podcasts. You can learn about technical analysis, fundamental analysis, risk management, and trading psychology. There are also 9 eBooks dedicated to dividend generation and risk diversification. The range and quality of Swissquoteâs educational content far surpass those of most other brokers.

I read several of Swissquoteâs articles, including the âMastering risk management in Forexâ article by Stefano Gianti, Education Manager at Swissquote. It begins with a definition of risk management and its importance in trading, then delves into risk diversification, proper risk-and-reward assessment, and more. I found this and other articles by Swissquote valuable for beginners interested in becoming consistent traders.

There are also plenty of materials dedicated to technical analysis, fundamental analysis, and trading psychology. These are available in written and video format from the brokerâs website and YouTube channel. There are also hundreds of platform tutorials, webinars, and key expert insights available in English and Chinese.

Swissquote also provides plenty of materials dedicated to investing. You can learn about the ABCs of stock investing, portfolio building for dividend generation, and more, from Swissquoteâs 9 eBooks.

The Bottom Line

Swissquote is a major investment bank based in Switzerland and founded in 1996. My analysis confirms it holds seven licenses from top-tier regulators and is publicly traded on the Swiss SIX exchange, a strong testament to its safety and financial stability.

The broker offers a massive catalog of over 4 million trading and investing products, including roughly 450 Forex and CFD assets. These are available on the proprietary CFXD platform, which boasts complex order types (e.g., OCO and IF-Done), high-definition charts, and integrated market research by Autochartist. While the CFXD platform lacks features like Expert Advisors or Depth of Market trading, Swissquote compensates for this by fully supporting MT4 and MT5.

Swissquote excels in superior execution quality: it reports average speeds of 9 ms and a 98% fill rate, which is why I consider the broker an excellent option for day and high-frequency traders.

Where Swissquote lags is in the pricing structure. During live testing, I recorded spreads that exceeded the industry benchmark across almost every instrument, except for share CFDs. For example, the spread on EURUSD was 1.8 pips, which is much higher than the 1.15-pip industry average. On top of that, the $1,000 minimum deposit creates a steep entry barrier for more casual traders.

Overall, I find Swissquote to be a strong choice for serious traders and funded professionals who prioritize regulatory safety and an institutional-grade platform over low trading costs.

What I Did Not Test

Please note that for this Swissquote review, I did not:

  1. open and test the trading conditions of Swissquoteâs Islamic account;
  2. upload proof of ID and proof of address to fully verify my Swissquote live account;
  3. deposit or withdraw real capital into or from Swissquote.

How Taurex Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is how Taurex protects you:

  • Keeps client funds segregated.
  • Operates on a best execution basis.
  • Guarantees negative balance protection on the UK entity.
  • Has issued a private indemnity insurance.

However, the negative balance protection is not available for global clients who open accounts with the FSA-regulated entity.

Discover more about the key safety mechanisms and their application in our comprehensive guide on client protections.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

Taurex has been operational for 8 years and employs around 200 professionals globally, according to the broker. This attests to its longevity and corporate stability.

I also learned that Taurex operates on a âbest executionâ basis, meaning it is required to deliver optimal price quotes under the prevailing market conditions. I also appreciated that live spread data is displayed on the website so that casual visitors can quickly assess the brokerâs fee transparency and competitiveness.

I also checked Taurexâs legal documents and client agreement and assessed that everything was in order. Essential data is easily accessible and pretty self-explanatory, and there are no major omissions.

Is Taurex Safe?

I concluded that Taurex can be considered safe due to the following factors:

  • Licensed and regulated in multiple jurisdictions.
  • Client money is protected from the brokerâs credit risk.
  • The broker is required to deliver optimal pricing.

Fees

Taurex offers some of the industryâs highest forex spreads, all the while providing some of the lowest crypto and indices spreads. I also concluded that the brokerâs swaps were elevated above the benchmark. Deposits are cost-free, but withdrawals are liable for a handling fee.

Are Taurexâs Fees Competitive?

Taurexâs costs can really vary depending on what youâre trading. The broker offers some of the lowest spreads on Bitcoin and indices across the industry. But its spreads on forex pairs and crude oil, as well as swap fees tend to be higher than average.

The same mixed picture applies to non-trading fees. While deposits are free, thereâs a fairly hefty inactivity fee and a handling charge on withdrawals.

Taurex also provides FIX APIs for low-latency trading and direct market access, as well as Pelican and Brokeree for copy trading.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I tested the desktop version of MetaTrader 5. The charts, orders, and various instruments are located in easy-to-find places, and even first-time traders can quickly learn their way around. My only gripe with the platform is that its charts feel rugged and outdated compared to newer and sleeker trading stations.

Taurexâs MT5 platform is available on Windows and Mac and supports 52 languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Arabic, Chinese, and more.

MT5 features include:

  • Alerts-Setting Option: Traders can set alerts for when the price of a given instrument falls/rises to a predetermined level, which could potentially signal a viable entry opportunity.
  • Watchlist Customization: Traders can populate watchlists with their favorite instruments and track market changes more easily.
  • One-click Trading: This feature enables instant market entries at the spot price and is invaluable for high-precision traders, such as scalpers.
  • Trading from the Chart: Traders can place conventional trading orders directly from the chart, specifying the entry price, volume level, stop and take-profit levels, and more.

In my opinion, MT5 is best suited for automated trading via Expert Advisors (EAs). The platform also has an intuitive strategy tester, allowing experienced algo traders to tweak the parameters of their strategies so that they can be used under different market conditions.

Charts

I have broken down the available analytical tools and chart configurations below:

  • 38 technical indicators: Including trend-based and volume-based indicators, and oscillators to analyze price action and assess market sentiment, helping predict market movements.
  • 24 drawing tools: Tools like Fibonacci retracement levels and Elliott waves help identify price patterns, support/resistance levels, and breakout points. However, MT5âs design can make price action harder to interpret.
  • 21 timeframes: For multi-timeframe analysis, enabling detailed price action analysis. MetaTrader 5 has one of the largest such offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Price action can be displayed as line, bars, or candlesticks, offering diverse perspectives on trading opportunities.

As shown above, MetaTraderâs charts can quickly become cluttered, even with just two indicators. This can obscure price action examination and make it harder to perform detailed technical analysis.

Orders

MetaTrader 5 features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading for immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the MetaTrader 5 platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries, but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a decent option for fast and simple order execution. However, its dated and rugged design is inferior to newer and sleeker platforms. While I appreciate MT5âs impressive selection of 21 timeframes, I find MT5âs charting capabilities too rigid and less effective.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

The protocol connects traders to the industryâs biggest liquidity providers and helps them obtain raw spreads directly from an exchangeâs order books. FIX APIs are the go-to option for traders interested in Direct Market Access (DMA) trading.

Taurex Execution Model

Taurex utilizes Electronic-Communication-Networks (ECN) technology as its principal execution model. Client orders are matched electronically (buying orders to selling orders and vice versa) at the interbank level. This helps Taurex achieve fast execution speeds and obtain competitive price quotes for its clients.

What Are CFDs?

CFDs (Contracts for Difference) let you trade on the price movements of assets, like gold, without actually owning them.

For example, if you go long on gold and the price rises, you profit; if it falls, you loseâwithout ever buying real gold.

The biggest perk? You can jump in or out of the market quickly to take advantage of even the smallest price changes.

Taurex offers three retail account types: Standard Zero, Pro Zero, and Raw. The broker also provides PAMM accounts for managed trading and Cent accounts for algo testing. Swap-free trading via Islamic accounts is also available.

To set up an account with Taurex, follow these simple steps:

  1. Click âOpen Accountâ at the top-right corner of the main page.

What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Research

Taurex shines in the research category with its comprehensive offering. The broker provides top-of-the-line market breakdowns developed in-house, along with content by Acuity and Trading Central. The variety of market news, breakdowns, and featured trading ideas is a great fit for day traders and swing traders.

Research Tools

I have broken down the most important types of market research provided by Taurex below:

  • Economic Calendar: The economic calendar tracks key economic events, such as financial releases and speeches, that have the power to stir the market and result in viable trading opportunities.
  • Market Insights: Taurex develops its own broad and penetrating market insights. They dive deep into recent market developments and present the reader with a comprehensive picture of market behavior. I appreciated that articles in this category are supported by price charts.
  • Trading Central: The Trading Central package contains a market sentiment gauge, a powerful economic calendar, and featured trading ideas. These inform readers of how and when to exploit viable trading opportunities.
  • Acuity: Taurex also incorporates the Acuity trading package, offering AI-powered technical analyses.

Taurex Research: My Key Takeaways

Taurexâs market research is broad and diverse. It utilizes elements of technical, fundamental, and economic analysis to present the user with a 360-degree coverage of recent market developments and emerging trading opportunities.

Education

Taurex delivers a steady stream of educational videos, guides, live streams, and one-on-one sessions with market experts. The offering is mostly geared towards the ABCs of trading, with less attention paid to more complex topics. As a whole, I rate Taurexâs educational offering as very high quality but with a limited scope.

I counted 28 introductory guides and 67 educational videos available in English and Arabic on the brokerâs YouTube channel. These cover a broad range of topics, such as âTrading Share CFDs: Best Practicesâ and âCrypto CFDs Demystifiedâ.

I also noticed that Taurex used to upload educational webinars, but it does not anymore. However, it publishes live streams about identifying viable trading opportunities and breaking down complex market data so that first-time traders can understand it.

The Bottom Line

Taurex comes across as a well-rounded and forward-thinking broker that has clearly put effort into building a robust offering for active traders. What stood out to me the most was its incredibly tight spreads on crypto and indicesâamong the best Iâve seen in the industry.

The broker also nails it with its research tools, FIX API solutions, and social/copy trading integrations through Pelican and Brokeree. If youâre a day trader, algo trader, or someone who thrives on timely market insights, Taurex delivers a highly attractive package.

That said, the picture isnât entirely perfect. Forex spreads and swap fees were noticeably high in my tests, and the educational content, while high-quality, is not quite comprehensive enough for beginners just starting out.

Still, Taurex shows it understands what performance-driven traders want: fast execution, a wide instrument selection (including 142 ETFs), and a choice of reliable platforms like MT4, MT5, and a well-designed proprietary app. For serious traders who can look past a few downsides, Taurex is definitely worth a closer look.

How TenTrade Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

â Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. TenTrade segregates all client funds.

â Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. TenTrade provides negative balance protection.

â Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects retail traders against the brokerâs liabilities in the unlikely event that the company becomes insolvent. TenTrade clients are not protected by a compensation scheme.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Founded in 2019, TenTrade has a relatively short but established presence in the industry. Its LinkedIn profile lists between 51 and 200 employees, placing it in the small to mid-sized broker category.

TenTrade provides clear corporate and regulatory information, with its operating entities disclosed in the website footer and trading costs detailed in the Client Agreement in the Legal Documents section. Overall, the essential details are accessible without excessive digging. I rate TenTrade as having an average level of transparency.

Is TenTrade Safe to Trade With?

In summary, my findings indicate that TenTrade can be regarded as having a moderate level of trust and stability due to the following factors:

  • Operates under a single offshore entity regulated by the Seychelles FSA, which offers lighter oversight than top-tier regulators.
  • Provides key safeguards, including segregated client funds and negative balance protection.
  • Clearly discloses its corporate structure and trading conditions on its website.
  • Has a relatively short operating history, having been founded in 2019.

TenTrade charges no fees for deposits or withdrawals, but an inactivity fee applies to dormant accounts.

Are TenTrade Fees Competitive?

The ECN account offers tighter raw spreads plus commissions, providing better value for active traders and scalpers. TenTrade also does not charge for deposits or withdrawals; however, an inactivity fee applies after three months of dormancy.

Platforms and Tools

TenTrade offers MetaTrader 5 (MT5) across desktop, web, and mobile. The intuitive MT5 web platform is suitable for beginners, while the more robust desktop platform offers advanced features like automated trading that appeal to experienced traders. Unlike many of its competitors, TenTrade does not offer any proprietary platform or alternatives to MetaTrader.

General Ease of Use

The MT5 platform provides a robust trading experience, featuring a clear and intuitive interface. While it is feature-rich and better suited to experienced traders, beginners can get up to speed with practice via the demo account. TenTrade provides access to MT5 via desktop, web, and mobile.

Charts

MetaTrader 5 offers flexible charting with candlestick, bar, and line types, over 80 technical indicators, and more than 40 drawing tools. Timeframes range from 1 minute to 1 month, making it suitable for both scalpers and long-term traders. Charts can be customized, detached, and used for one-click trading.

Orders

MT5 supports market, limit, stop, trailing stop, and pending orders, giving traders flexible execution options suitable for scalping, swing trading, and automated strategies. For greater precision, orders can be placed directly from the chart or the Depth of Market (DOM) tool.

General Ease of Use

The MT5 web platform delivers a clean, desktop-like trading experience directly in your browser with no installation required. My first impression was that it feels very similar to the TradingView platform. Navigation is smooth and intuitive, making it easy to manage watchlists, browse markets, and place trades from any device. Real-time quotes and quick access to contract specifications keep key information at your fingertips, while the platformâs overall layout is polished and beginner-friendly.

Charts

Charting on MT5 Web is robust, offering 30 built-in indicators, 24 drawing tools, and nine timeframes ranging from one minute to one month. Traders can switch between candlestick, line, and bar charts, and place trades directly from the chart with one click. I especially like the ability to overlay upcoming economic events onto the chart, which helps traders stay aware of market-moving releases without leaving the platform.

Orders

MetaTrader Web supports all major order types, including market, limit, and stop orders, as well as stop-loss and take-profit levels, for effective risk management. Execution is fast, and the interface makes it easy to place, modify, or close positions in seconds. With its full order functionality and advanced tools, MT5 Web provides a powerful and convenient trading experience entirely within the browser.

MT5 Mobile App

General Ease of Use

The MT5 mobile app has a clean, intuitive design thatâs easy to navigate on small screens. Traders can create watchlists, view interactive charts, and place or adjust orders in just a few taps. With real-time quotes, news, and an economic calendar, it delivers fast execution and convenient access to detailed market information on the go.

Charts

The MT5 app offers versatile charting tools with multiple types, including candlestick, line, and bar charts. Traders can apply over 30 built-in indicators such as Moving Averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and RSI, plus 20+ drawing tools like trend lines and Fibonacci retracements. Timeframes span from one minute to one month, supporting both short-term and long-term analysis, with one-touch trading directly from charts.

Orders

The MT5 app offers a full range of order types to suit different trading styles. Market orders allow instant execution, while limit and stop orders help traders enter at predefined levels. Stop-loss and take-profit orders manage risk and secure gains, giving traders precise control over execution and risk management.

MetaTrader 5: My Key Takeaways

MT5 delivers a strong, all-round trading experience across desktop, mobile, and web. The desktop platform offers fast execution, deep customisation, advanced charting, and reliable algorithmic trading through Expert Advisors (EAs), making it ideal for serious traders.

The mobile app combines simplicity with powerful features, providing solid charting tools, fast execution, integrated news, and effective risk management for trading on the go. The web platform adds a clean, intuitive interface that feels similar to TradingView, with smooth navigation, real-time quotes, robust charting tools, full order functionality, and convenient browser-based access.

Copy Trading

TenTradeâs copy trading platform offers a straightforward way for users to mirror the strategies of experienced traders. It integrates seamlessly with MT5 and is available for all account types, making it easy for both beginners and time-pressed traders to gain market exposure without having to manage every trade manually. Joining as a follower is free, and trades are copied automatically in real time, with adjustable risk settings and no limitations on withdrawing profits.

For skilled traders, TenTrade provides the opportunity to become copy providers and earn passive income based on their performance. Providers can build a following, manage multiple accounts, and withdraw their earnings freely. The platform also fosters a community-driven environment where strategies and insights can be shared. However, I noted that there were relatively few attractive strategies on the platform when I performed my tests.

TenTrade Order Execution Model

TenTrade is the contractual counterparty to clients. In this sense, it is a market maker. When executing orders, TenTrade obtains the best possible result for clients, taking into account factors like price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size, and market impact.

Tradable Instruments

TenTrade offers a selection of 175 CFD instruments across forex, commodities, indices, cryptocurrencies, and stocks. The range is above average in some categories (indices, crypto) but smaller in others (stocks) compared to top multi-asset brokers.

What are CFDs?

A Contract for Difference (CFD) is an agreement specifying that the buyer must pay the seller the difference between an assetâs current value and its value at the time the contract was initiated. Like futures and other derivative financial instruments, CFDs allow traders to speculate on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

I tested TenTradeâs customer support for more than a week and received helpful answers via live chat, although there was a short wait for a response. The ticketing system within the client portal performed well, and I consistently received same-day responses to all inquiries.

Once the profile is set up, the broker prompts you to verify your identity by uploading standard documents such as proof of identity and proof of address. Overall, the experience feels streamlined and simple.

What is CFD Leverage?

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex and CFD markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is the use of borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

TentTrade offers the maximum leverage of 1:500 on the Pro Account. This means that with an account of $1,000, you can control up to $500,000 worth of positions in the market. This is a high level of leverage and risky to use.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders should keep in mind that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

Research

TenTrade delivers a regular stream of market commentary through its News Room section, offering technical insights, market updates, and an integrated economic calendar. The content is timely and easy to navigate, though the depth is moderate. The platform does not include third-party tools like Trading Central and lacks a real-time news feed, such as Reuters, so traders may need to rely on external sources for deeper analysis. Overall, I rate TenTradeâs research offering as average for the industry.

TenTradeâs News Room provides a clean and well-organized hub for ongoing market coverage, featuring technical analysis, market news, and broader educational commentary. The content is neatly categorised and easy to navigate, helping traders quickly find updates that suit their style.

Posts cover major currency pairs, important economic releases, and developments in equity markets. The frequency of updates is relatively light, with new articles added only every three days. The platform includes an economic calendar, which adds helpful context by highlighting key data points and events that may influence upcoming price action.

The analysis provided is generally concise and actionable, focusing on chart patterns, important levels, and short-term market drivers. This makes it useful for everyday trade planning, though some articles remain high-level rather than deeply analytical.

Author details are limited, which makes it harder to evaluate the depth of expertise behind the commentary. Itâs also important to note that TenTrade lacks a real-time professional news feed, like Reuters or Bloomberg, so traders who rely on instant headline updates will need to use external sources.

TenTrade Research: My Key Takeaways

Overall, TenTradeâs News Room is a solid supplementary resource for traders seeking regular, digestible insights across popular markets. It works best as a quick commentary tool rather than a full research terminal. For those who appreciate straightforward analysis and a built-in economic calendar, it complements the broader educational materials offered through the TenTrade Academy.

Education

TenTrade provides a well-rounded educational offering through its TenTrade Academy, which includes written guides, video tutorials, e-books, and live webinars. The material is well structured and suitable for both beginners and intermediate traders, covering everything from trading fundamentals to psychology and prop trading. The interactive webinars add extra value for those who prefer live instruction. Overall, I rate TenTradeâs educational resources as better than average for the industry.

TenTradeâs educational hub, the TenTrade Academy, offers a broad and well-organised selection of learning materials suitable for beginners through to more experienced traders. The academy offers live webinars, downloadable e-books, video tutorials, and written guides, providing users with multiple ways to learn at their own pace.

The range is impressively wide, covering introductory topics such as how forex trading works as well as more advanced areas like prop trading, trading psychology, and copy trading. Overall, the content feels structured, accessible, and designed to help traders build both foundational knowledge and practical skills.

The interactive components add meaningful value. Live webinars create opportunities to hear from market professionals and revisit recorded sessions later, while the e-books stand out for being concise and actionable. Titles like âThe A to Z of Tradingâ and âScalping Method: How to Trade Within a Dayâ provide clear explanations that can help traders apply theory into practice. As a whole, TenTrade Academy offers a solid mix of formats and topics, making it a valuable resource for anyone seeking to deepen their understanding of trading.

The Bottom Line

TenTrade delivers an accessible trading environment with flexible account options and a built-in funded-trader program that helps it stand out. Founded in 2019 and regulated in Seychelles, it provides key safeguards like segregated funds and negative balance protection, though its offshore oversight is lighter than that of top-tier regulators. Transparency is solid, with clear documentation and straightforward account terms.

Fees vary by account type. The ECN and Pro Plus accounts are competitive, while the Pro account is closer to industry averages. Some instruments, including GBP/JPY and the DAX 40, show wider spreads. On the other hand, TenTrade charges no deposit or withdrawal fees, which adds convenience for active users.

MT5 is the brokerâs only platform, but it offers strong charting, fast execution, algorithmic trading support, and smooth performance across desktop, web, and mobile. Additional features like copy trading, PAMM accounts, and high-leverage options broaden the brokerâs appeal. However, the absence of a real-time institutional newsfeed, VPS hosting, and alternative platforms may limit more advanced traders.

Overall, TenTrade works best for casual traders, day traders, and those interested in copy trading or funded-account growth. Swing traders and scalpers can use it effectively with some caveats, while long-term investors may find the platformâs CFD-only structure too limited for their needs.

Stability and Transparency

I also reviewed Tickmillâs legal documentation and found everything to be well-organized and transparent. My only minor concern is that the website lists average spreads instead of live data, which makes it harder for traders to assess real-time pricing conditions.

What I appreciate most about MT5 is that it caters to the unique needs of traders from different backgrounds. Traders can use it to perform basic technical analysis, place trading orders with ease, and engage in copy trading. MT5 appeals to more experienced traders with its Depth of Market (DOM) tool and Expert Advisors (EAs) for algorithmic trading. The platform also features a strategy tester tool, helping algo traders perfect their systems.

On the downside, MT5âs charting capabilities are outmatched by more modern trading stations, such as cTrader and TradingView. Its chart visuals are rugged and lack the sleek, polished look that many traders today prefer.

That said, MT5âs charts get cluttered quite easily, especially when applying more than one technical indicator or drawing tool. Price action becomes obscured and difficult to interpret. Overall, MT5âs charts are not ideal for traders accustomed to streamlined and easily scalable setups.

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android. It retains the high functionality of its desktop counterpart, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Tickmill Research: My Key Takeaways

Tickmill combines sophisticated in-house research content with third-party tools. It publishes high-end fundamental analyses, technical analyses, and market breakdowns, and also incorporates actionable trading signals by Acuity.

I appreciated the depth and diversity of the materials, which complement each other seamlessly. Traders have a 360-degree overview of key market developments and trading setups. In my opinion, Tickmill offers one of the best research services in the industry.

Education

Tickmill provides outstanding educational content, including a wide variety of educational videos, webinars, articles, and ebooks. The broker even has its own podcast called Bright Minds. Overall, I appreciated the scope and practicality of Tickmillâs educational materials, which cover trading essentials and cater to traders at all experience levels.

• Webinars and Seminars: Tickmill also impresses with the scope of its webinars and seminars that are available from both the brokerâs website and YouTube channel.

• Video Content: Tickmill also provides a rich collection of introductory videos informing the trader of essential trading concepts and know-how.

The Bottom Line

Tickmill is a well-rounded, feature-packed multi-asset broker established in 2014. It offers over 630 tradable CFD instruments and has earned a strong reputation for its fast execution speeds, competitive fees, and powerful trading platforms.

Tickmill delivers on the technology front, supporting MT4, MT5, TradingView, and its sleek Tickmill Trader platform. It enhances these with MetaTrader add-ons, copy trading, and VPS hosting for low-latency performance. Execution speed is another strong point, averaging around 15 milliseconds, which gives scalpers and high-frequency traders a real edge.

The brokerâs standout strengths lie in its top-tier research and education, which go far beyond what most competitors offer. Traders get access to detailed market analyses, AI-powered trading signals from Acuity, and an impressive lineup of learning resources, from ebooks and webinars to the Bright Minds podcast.

Of course, Tickmill isnât perfect. Its Classic account isnât available on Tickmill Trader or TradingView, and forex spreads came in wider than the benchmark during my live test. Still, these are relatively small downsides in the grand scheme.

All things considered, Tickmill is one of the most balanced brokers out there, equally suited for beginners, active traders, and experienced professionals. Whether youâre focused on education, research, or execution quality, Tickmill checks nearly every box.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

A classic outlook. MetaTrader should be given credit for popularizing a design that is replicated by many other trading platforms. Its charting area is broad and occupies the middle section of the screen. There is also a top panel with multiple tools and functions, and a watchlist of selected instruments on the left.

Multiple functionalities. You can use MetaTrader for a range of styles, from day trading to swing trading. Algorithmic trading via EAs is also possible. The platform features a built-in strategy tester so you can tweak your strategy parameters, and a trading journal to track your execution speed.

Practical insights. MetaTrader is loaded with educational articles and videos to help you make the most out of it, and also to learn how to use different technical indicators and drawing tools. You can access the educational content from the âHelpâ tab at the top panel and then by clicking âVideo Guidesâ or âMQL5 Articlesâ.

Speed tracking. I learned that TMGM offers access to 7 global servers, affording its clients greater flexibility. The one drawback is that TMGM does not have an EU-based server, which disadvantages local traders. On the plus side, the broker provides Virtual Private Server (VPS) hosting. You can subscribe to it and achieve much faster execution speeds.

Outdated charting capabilities. The biggest drawback of MetaTrader is its charts. Scaling price action up or down is not easy, and it is hard for users to get a sense of where the market is headed next.

  • 21 timeframes: From 1 minute to 1 month. The different timeframes allow you to zoom in and out on price action and assess how the market behaves in the short- and long-term.
  • 3 chart types: Including line, bars, and candlesticks.

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entries at the best available price.
  • Limit Orders: Used for precise entries at an exact price.
  • Stop Orders: Typically used to protect the primary position.

You can open a demo account before or alongside your live CFD account.

Try the âCFD Trading Essentialsâ if you want to understand how to read price action behavior and how to apply basic risk management, or jump to the âAdvanced Strategiesâ if you wish to learn useful techniques of day and swing trading.

The Bottom Line

TMGM is a well-regulated financial derivatives broker, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Australia. It offers more than 240 tradable instruments at competitive prices. The highlight for me was the $15 BTCUSD spread, making the broker an excellent choice for crypto traders.

You can choose between the MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 platforms, as well as the all-in-one TMGM app. Another perk of the broker is its free VPS offer. You can use it to achieve fast execution speeds below 5ms.

The other strong points of TMGM include its wide-spanning educational content and robust market research. On the other hand, the brokerâs high swaps on certain instruments exceeded the industry average.

I concluded that TMGM is a great fit for day and news traders. Beginners and crypto enthusiasts would also benefit from it. However, the generally higher swaps make TMGM less suitable for swing traders.

How Trading 212 Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category, we assess how stable and transparent a broker is. This includes how long theyâve been in business, the size of the company, and how openly they share important information.

In my research, I found that Trading 212 has been around for over 20 years. According to its LinkedIn page, the broker employs more than 1,200 professionals worldwide, which speaks to the strength of its business model.

I also reviewed the brokerâs legal documents and found them clear and well-organized, with essential information easy to access. Another positive is that Trading 212 operates on a âbest executionâ basis, meaning it is legally required to offer clients the best available spreads under current market conditions.

That said, I did notice a minor transparency gap regarding fees. The average spreads published on the websiteâfor example, a 0.0002-pip EUR/USD spreadâwere far from what I observed in testing of the CFD account, where the average EUR/USD spread was closer to 1.5 pips. I also noted that current swap rates arenât published on the site, which could be improved.

Is Trading 212 Safe?

Orders

Trading 212 Web Trader features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which support immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries, but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and trigger the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

CFDs (Contracts for Difference) let you trade on the price movements of assetsâlike goldâwithout actually owning them.

On the downside, the broker does not integrate third-party research tools like Autochartist or Trading Central, which could have added extra perspective and depth.

Education

Trading 212 provides a comprehensive educational package, featuring over 400 videos and webinars on its YouTube channel, as well as more than 120 written articles on its website. Most of the content focuses on core investing topics, but thereâs also solid coverage of technical and fundamental analysis as well as trading psychology.

Trading 212 delivers a solid range of educational resources. Its YouTube channel hosts 350+ videos covering everything from technical analysis (like how to read price charts) to fundamental analysis (understanding market drivers) and trading psychology (developing the right mindset). On top of that, another 60 videos are available directly through the platform.

Most of the brokerâs written content focuses on investing, with beginner-friendly guides on topics like dividends and portfolio building. Overall, I found the education library practical and approachable, making it a strong starting point for newcomers while still offering useful material for more experienced traders.

The Bottom Line

After thoroughly testing Trading 212, I see it as a broker that excels in safety, accessibility, and product range, but comes with some trade-offs in pricing and functionality.

Being regulated only by Tier-1 authorities makes it one of the safest options in the industry, which gave me confidence during my review. I was especially impressed by its 10,000+ real stocks and ETFs, fractional shares, and PIEs portfolios, which go far beyond what most brokers offer.

On the flip side, my live testing revealed that spreads on forex, indices, and crypto are higher than the industry average, which limits its appeal for cost-sensitive day traders and scalpers. The lack of automated trading tools is another drawback for advanced users.

Overall, I consider Trading 212 an excellent choice for long-term investors and casual traders seeking a secure, beginner-friendly platform with a vast selection of assets. However, if your top priority is ultra-tight spreads or automated strategies, Trading 212 may not be the ideal fit compared to more specialized competitors.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All Trading.com entities guarantee the segregation of client funds from the companyâs corporate capital.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. All Trading.com entities ensure negative balance protection, except for Trading.com Markets Inc.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Clients of Trading.com Markets EU Limited are protected by up to EUR 20,000 under the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF). Clients of Trading Point of Financial Instruments UK Limited are protected by up to GBP 85,000 under the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS).
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. Clients from Europe, the UK, and Australia have access to up to 1:30 leverage, while US clients can trade with leverage of up to 1:50.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

Despite Trading.com launched only recently in 2019, in just six years it has built a reputation as a reliable and rapidly growing broker. According to its LinkedIn page, the company now employs over 70 people, reflecting its steady expansion and industry presence.

I reviewed Trading.comâs legal documents, including the client agreement, execution policy, and risk disclosure, and found them to be clear, transparent, and easy to understand. All key information regarding the brokerâs services and client protections is well-documented and presented without bias, making it accessible even to less experienced traders.

Is Trading.com Safe to Trade With?

I determined that Trading.com has a high level of safety due to the following factors:

  • Tightly regulated by four top-tier institutions
  • Keeps client funds segregated
  • Guarantees negative balance protection (except for US entity)
  • Operates on a best execution basis

The broker doesnât charge handling fees for deposits or withdrawals, but inactive accounts are subject to an inactivity fee.

The platform is available on all major browsers and in six languages: English, French, German, Italian, Polish, and Spanish.

The features include:

  • Market Research: The platform is also integrated with a news screener powered by Trading.com. It helps traders stay on top of the latest market developments and take advantage of currently evolving trading opportunities.

Charts

The charts are undoubtedly the best feature of Trading.comâs platform. They are fluid and easily scalable, with price action represented clearly and in great detail. This allows technical traders to spot emerging trading setups quickly and easily. Moreover, unlike older platforms like MetaTrader, these wide charts are not cluttered when adding more than one indicator or drawing tool.

I have broken down the available analytical tools and chart configurations below:

  • 75 drawing tools: Tools like Fibonacci retracement levels and Elliott waves help identify price patterns, support/resistance levels, and breakout points.
  • 9 timeframes: For multi-timeframe analysis, enabling detailed price action analysis.
  • 16 chart types: Price action can be displayed as line, bars, or candlesticks, offering diverse perspectives on trading opportunities.

In my opinion, the chart screen is one of the most crucial features of a trading platform. It equips traders with essential tools and configurations to analyze price action and spot trading opportunities. Just as important is the ability to easily scale price action, allowing for a clearer and more detailed view of market movements.

Orders

Trading.comâs web trader supports one- and two-click trading, spot trading, and pending orders. I have broken down the available order types on the platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

Trading.com WebTrader: My Key Takeaways

Trading.comâs platform is a great fit for day traders, scalpers, and experienced chart artists. Its user-friendly interface makes it extremely easy to navigate, while its high-definition charts accommodate probing technical analyses. The platform is also integrated with regularly updated market research so that users can stay on top of the latest market trends.

Trading.comâs mobile app retains the practicality of its web counterpart. It is available on iOS and Android, and enables quick and easy access to the market on the go. The app is handy for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

There is an integrated market research, which includes an economic calendar, news screener, and economic sentiment. The app also features biometric login and direct customer support. You can use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, and to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives that speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical ownership.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Trading.com offers 52 written articles and 13 educational videos, which are available for free on the website. These materials are easy to grasp even by inexperienced traders and cover topics related to technical analysis, fundamental analysis, trading psychology, and risk management.

The Bottom Line

Established in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Trading.com is a financial derivatives broker regulated by CySEC, ASIC, FCA, and the NFA, adhering to some of the strictest safety standards in the industry.

Clients can access over 1,400 tradable instruments across various markets. The broker stands out with its versatile trading platform and mobile app, offering advanced charting tools and built-in market research, along with support for MetaTrader 5.

Fees are fair and competitive, and the brokerâs educational and research content is clear and informative. However, it does lack a raw spread account and doesnât currently offer third-party research tools.

I consider Trading.com a strong option for day traders, swing traders, and anyone looking for a secure and well-regulated broker, backed by user-friendly tools and a broad range of markets.

Trading.com is regulated by five top-tier financial authorities: CFTC, NFA, FCA, CySEC, and ASIC. This strong regulatory oversight contributes to its high trust rating in our review. All client funds are kept separate from company funds, ensuring an added layer of security. Although Trading.com was launched in 2019 and is a relatively new brand, it is owned by Trading Point Group, a well-established financial services provider founded in 2009.

Trading.com Regulators

In our reviews, we examine the regulatory status of each entity operated by a broker. This allows us to compare the different levels of client protection. We rank regulators using a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing reflects the highest level of regulation.

Here are my findings on the various entities of Trading.com:

  • Trading.com Markets Inc. is a registered Retail Foreign Exchange Dealer with the Commodities Futures Trading Commission and a member of the National Futures Association (NFA) #0516820. We rate CFTC and NFA as Tier-1 regulators.
  • Trading.com Markets EU Limited is authorised and regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) 256/14. We rate CySEC as a Tier-1 regulator.
  • Trading Point of Financial Instruments UK Limited, trading as Trading.com, is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) FRN 705428. We rate FCA as a Tier-1 regulator.
  • Trading.com Markets PTY Ltd. is authorised and regulated by the Australian Securities and Investment Commission (ASIC), AFSL 443670. We rate ASIC as a Tier-1 regulator.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections Associated with Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All of Trading.com entities ensure this.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. Trading.com US does not provide negative balance protection. All other entities guarantee negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects retail traders against the brokerâs liabilities in the unlikely event that the company becomes insolvent. Accounts with Trading.com Markets Inc.(US) are not insured.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The Trading.com Markets Inc. (US) entity offers maximum leverage of 1:50. All other entities offer a maximum leverage of 1:30.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Trading.com launched in 2019, reflecting a moderate level of industry experience. However, the parent company, Trading Point Group, has a more extensive operating history of 16 years. According to the brokerâs LinkedIn page, the company has 51â200 employees, indicating it is a small to mid-size brokerage firm.

In my research, I found Trading.com US to be highly transparent about its regulatory status, with its regulators clearly listed in the website footer. Trading costs are outlined in a straightforward manner on the Forex Pricing page, while more detailed information is available in the Customer Agreement found under the Legal Documents section.

Is Trading.com Safe to Trade With?

To summarize, I rate Trading.com as trustworthy and stable due to the following:

  • Licensed by multiple top-tier regulators
  • All entities segregate funds
  • Part of Trading Point Group â a larger and more experienced company
  • Has a high level of transparency

Fees

My hands-on tests showed that Trading.com US offers average trading fees overall. Spreads in major and minor pairs are in line with industry norms. Swap fees were also average during my test. Trading.com US charges an inactivity fee of $10 for dormant accounts for over 1 year. A fee of $13 is charged for bank wire deposits and withdrawals under $250.

Trading.com US Trading Fees

Trading.com US Spreads

To evaluate Trading.com US spreads, I ran live tests on 15 May 2025 during two of the most active market sessions: the London open and shortly after the New York openâperiods known for high liquidity and typically tighter spreads.

Here are the results:

The EUR/USD spreads at Trading.com US were slightly wider than the industry average, suggesting room for improvement on this popular pair. GBP/JPY spreads were notably wider than average in both sessions, which could impact cost efficiency for traders focused on this volatile cross.

While execution remains fast, the current spread levels make Trading.com US a less competitive choice in terms of pricing, especially for scalpers and high-frequency traders who depend on razor-thin margins.

Trading.com US Swap Fees

The table below shows the overnight financing costsâswap feesâfor holding one full-sized forex contract (100,000 units of the base currency) at Trading.com US. The data was recorded on May 19, 2025, and includes both Swap Long (buy positions) and Swap Short (sell positions):
