Swap rates at Trading.com US fall in line with industry averages. EUR/USD shows a typical charge for long positions and a moderate credit for shorts. GBP/JPY, a more volatile pair, shows a relatively high swap credit for longs but also a steep charge on shorts.

Overall, traders should factor in these overnight costs when managing longer-term positions, but the fees are broadly comparable to what youâd find with most major brokers.

Trading.com US Non-Trading Fees

A funded real account with no open positions or trading activity for 12 consecutive months is considered dormant and is charged an inactivity fee of $10 per month. Also, a $13 fee is charged for both bank wire deposits and withdrawals when the amount is below $250.

Are Trading.com US Fees Competitive?

I rate the fees at Trading.com US as average for the following reasons:

  • Standard spreads in major and minor pairs
  • Low inactivity fee after 1 year
  • Average swap fees
  • Small fee for bank wire deposits and withdrawals under $250

Platform and Tools

Trading.com US provides clients with its proprietary WebTrader platform and mobile app. Clients can also access MetaTrader 5, which features advanced charts and order types, and enables automated trading. I rate the platform offering as better than average for the industry.

Platform/Tool Suitable For
Trading.com WebTrader Beginners, casual traders, experienced traders, social trading, news trading
MetaTrader 5 Experienced traders, day trading, scalping, algo trading, backtesting, trading signals, copy trading
Trading.com Mobile App Beginners

Trading.com WebTrader Platform

The flagship Trading.com WebTrader platform is built with the user in mind. The interface is uncluttered and customizable, while providing key features like watchlists, a news feed, price alerts, one-click trading, trading from the chart, trading signals, investor sentiment data, and live chat support.

Charting within the WebTrader platform offers a solid range of indicators, drawing tools, time frames, and chart types. Traders can make use of the following range of charting features:

  • 29 technical indicators, including trend indicators, oscillators, and volatility indicators.
  • 9 timeframes, from 1 minute to 1 month.
  • 5 chart types, including Candlestick, Bar, Line, Mountain, and Heikin Ashi.
  • 17 drawing tools, including channel, pitchfork, and Fibonacci retracement.
  • 3 layout options, including single chart, grid of 4, and grid of 6.

The platform features standard order types, including market orders, limit orders, and stop loss orders. If you want to cancel your order after a specified date and time, time-in-force conditions can be applied. Trailing stop loss orders are not currently available.

WebTraderâs investor sentiment data displays the proportion of Trading Point Group clients holding buy or sell positions, providing real-time insight into the prevailing mood among these traders. This sentiment snapshot reflects whether the majority of clients are optimistic (bullish) or pessimistic (bearish) about a particular asset, helping users gauge market psychology.

Traders can stay on top of the latest news headlines via a Reuters news feed, ensuring they have immediate access to real-time, market-moving information. The integrated Reuters feed delivers up-to-the-minute coverage on global financial markets, including breaking news, economic updates, and market analysis.

The Technical Summary tool shows the strength and direction of a currency pairâs underlying trend across multiple timeframes. This is useful for identifying potential entry and exit points, confirming trade setups, and aligning short-term trades with longer-term market momentum.

Trade signals from Analyzzer and Trading Central provide actionable insights based on technical analysis. These signals highlight potential buy or sell opportunities by identifying key chart patterns, support and resistance levels, and momentum shifts. Integrated directly into the platform, they help traders make quicker, data-driven decisions.

WebTrader Platform: My Key Takeaways

During my testing, I appreciated the clean and simple design of Trading.comâs WebTrader, which makes it easy to navigate even for those new to trading. The uncluttered layout allows users to focus on the markets without distractions, while the customizable interface adds flexibility for more experienced traders.

I was also impressed by the variety of tools available, which support efficient trade execution and informed decision-making. The platformâs charting capabilities are solid for a browser-based platform and offer enough flexibility for most users. Overall, I rate this platform a great fit for beginners, casual traders, and day traders.

Trading.com US Mobile App

The Trading.com US mobile app, available for both iOS and Android, delivers a seamless and intuitive trading experience designed for traders on the move. Its interface allows you to monitor markets, execute trades, and manage your account with just a tap. The app features advanced charting tools, price alerts, an economic calendar, and integrated expert analysis, making it suitable for both beginners and seasoned traders alike.

Trading.com US Mobile App: My Key Takeaways

Like the Trading.com WebTrader platform, the mobile app is designed for simplicity and provides a smooth experience while also packing powerful features. I especially liked the sleek design and availability of 1-tap trading and full-screen charting in landscape mode.

MetaTrader 5

Alongside the WebTrader platform, Trading.com US clients can also access MetaTrader 5 (MT5), which is available in 52 languagesâfrom Arabic to Vietnamese. MT5 offers a suite of powerful features, including:

  • Alerts, which notify traders when a selected instrument hits a specified price level.
  • Watchlists, allowing users to monitor their preferred instruments and view real-time quotes in a customizable market watch panel.
  • One-Click Trading, enabling fast order execution without secondary confirmationâideal for scalpers and other short-term traders.
  • Trading from the Chart lets traders place and manage orders directly within the price chart for greater efficiency.

MetaTraderâs popularity is driven by its integrated copy trading and automated trading capabilities.

  • Trading Signals: The MetaTrader 5 platform features a Trading Signals service, allowing users to automatically replicate the trades of experienced traders in real time. By subscribing to a signal provider, users can mirror professional strategies and diversify their portfolios without manual intervention.
  • Automated Trading: MetaTrader 5 also supports the development, testing, and deployment of Expert Advisors (EAs)âautomated trading programs that use algorithms to monitor markets and execute trades on behalf of the user. These tools enable traders to automate their strategies and benefit from algorithmic trading without the need for constant oversight.

MetaTrader 5 provides powerful charting capabilities, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators, covering trend analysis, volume, and oscillators.
  • 44 analytical tools, such as lines, channels, and both Gann and Fibonacci instruments.
  • 21 selectable time frames, ranging from one minute up to one month.
  • 3 chart formats: bar charts, Japanese candlesticks, and line charts.

MetaTrader 5 offers a comprehensive selection of order types to suit various trading strategies:

  • Market Order: Executes a buy or sell at the best available current price.
  • Limit Order: Executes a trade at a specified price or better, allowing for greater price control.
  • Stop-Loss Order: Triggers a buy or sell when the instrument reaches a predetermined price, helping to limit potential losses.
  • Stop Limit Order: Combines a stop-loss and a limit order, enabling more precise risk management by specifying both a trigger price and a limit price.
  • Trailing Stop Order: Sets a stop-loss that automatically adjusts as the market price moves in your favor, helping to lock in profits without requiring you to manually exit the position.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 (MT5) is a highly regarded and widely used desktop platform among retail traders. While it delivers an impressive array of features, its advanced capabilities may be daunting for beginners. Compared to the Trading.com WebTrader platform, MT5 offers a more comprehensive suite of technical indicators, advanced charting tools, and support for automated trading strategies.

MetaTrader 5 Mobile App

Trading.com US clients can access the MetaTrader 5 (MT5) mobile app, available for both Android and iOS devices. The app supports essential trading features such as one-click execution, customizable alerts, and trading directly from charts. It offers a variety of order types, including market, pending, and stop ordersâthough trailing stop-loss orders are only available on the desktop version.

While the appâs interface is intuitive and packed with functionality, changing its language requires adjusting the language settings on your entire device. Overall, the MT5 mobile app delivers a robust trading experience with an impressive range of technical indicators and charting capabilities, making it one of the strongest mobile platforms on the market.

Trading.com Order Execution Model

Trading.com US operates as a market maker, acting as the counterparty to all client trades. This means clients trade directly with Trading.com US rather than through the underlying market. All transactions are executed through an execution-only dealing desk, allowing the broker to offer competitive pricing on trades.

Tradable Instruments

Trading.com US offers a solid lineup of 69 forex pairs, spanning major, minor, and exotic currencies. While the broker doesnât support other asset classes like stocks and commodities, its forex offering is broader than the industry average.

I found the range of currency pairs to be better than average, with access to popular staples like EUR/USD, dynamic minors like GBP/JPY, and less common exotic pairs such as USD/TRY.

Although Trading.com US is limited to forex, it offers a robust and varied selection of currency pairs, appealing to both beginners and experienced traders seeking exposure to a wide range of market conditions.

Customer Support

Trading.com US provides 24/5 customer support through live chat, phone, and email. In my experience, their support stands out as above average via live chat and email, thanks to consistently fast and helpful responses across dozens of test interactions. However, I was not able to reach an operator by phone.

Trading.com Customer Support Test

I tested customer support with a range of queries, covering topics from trading platforms to available instruments. Live chat responses came within seconds, while email replies typically arrived the same day or by the next business day. I tried calling support several times, but was not able to reach an agent.

Currently, support is limited to the English language only.

Deposit and Withdrawal

At Trading.com US, deposit and withdrawal options are limited to bank wire transfers and ACH payments. Due to local regulatory guidelines, the platform does not accept credit cards, PayPal, or Western Union for funding accounts. Processing times are typical for the industry. A $13 fee applies to both deposits and withdrawals via bank wire if the amount is under $250.

Again, processing times are average, and the same fee applies to bank wire withdrawals under $250.

While the processing times align with industry standards, the deposit fee for small bank wire transfers is notable, as most brokers do not charge fees for deposits. Withdrawal fees for bank wires, however, are more common among brokers.

Account Types and Terms

Trading.com US simplifies forex trading by offering a single, comprehensive account type: the T1 Account. This account is commission-free, all costs are reflected in the spread. All accounts are denominated in U.S. dollars, and there is a low minimum deposit of $50.

Trading.com US Account Opening Process

To open an account at Trading.com US, prospective clients must answer the following questions:

  • Personal Details: Name, email, mobile number, address, citizenship, date of birth, Social Security number or Tax ID.
  • Financial Profile: Planned investment amount, trading purpose, source of funds, employment status, annual income, and net worth.
  • Trading Background: Experience level with trading stocks, options, futures, forex, and cryptocurrencies. Are you a forex counterparty or a related person of one?

Additionally, the following documents are necessary for verification of identity and residence:

  • A valid government-issued photo ID such as a driverâs license, state ID, or passport.
  • A recent document showing your current address, such as a utility bill, bank statement, or credit card statement issued within the last 6 months. If your government-issued ID includes your address, it can be used for both proof of identity and proof of residence.

Demo Account

Trading.com US provides free demo accounts through its WebTrader platform, mobile app, and MetaTrader 5. These accounts are ideal for beginners, offering a risk-free way to practice trading strategies and explore the platformâs features.

The demo environment mirrors real market conditions with live quotes across all 69 forex pairs. When users feel ready, transitioning to a live account is a simple and seamless process.

Islamic Account

Trading.com US does not offer swap-free Islamic accounts.

What is Leverage in Forex Trading?

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is using borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

For US clients, Trading.com offers a maximum of 1:50 in leverage. It means that with $1,000 of funds in an account, a trader can take on up to $50,000 worth of market positions.

Leverage varies greatly by currency pair. For example, 1:50 leverage is available for EUR/USD, while the available leverage for USD/TRY is only 1:4.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders should keep in mind that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

Trading.com US Supported Countries

The Trading.com US entity only provides services to residents of the United States. However, other entities cater to global clients.

Research

Trading.com US excels in the research category, offering a wide array of resources. The broker consistently delivers insightful technical and fundamental analysis, available in both written and video formats.
Additionally, Trading.com integrates research from Trading Central and a Reuters news feed directly into its WebTrader platform. Overall, I consider Trading.comâs research offering to be a cut above average.

Trading.comâs Daily Update offers traders a concise overview of recent financial news and upcoming events that could impact the markets. This daily synopsis is designed to keep traders informed about overnight developments and provide insights into factors that could move the forex market throughout the day.

Trading.com offers a Reuters news feed that gives traders real-time financial news and market analysis via the website and WebTrader platform. This helps users stay updated on key global events, market movements, and political developments as they happen. The feed covers everything from currency changes and commodity prices to stock market trendsâgiving traders the insights they need to make smarter decisions.

The economic calendar on Trading.com is a simple, powerful tool that helps traders stay ahead of key financial events. It delivers real-time updates on major economic indicators, central bank decisions, and other market-moving news. Users can filter events by country, category, and impact level to get the most relevant information. With this calendar, traders can better anticipate market volatility and make smarter, more informed decisions.

Trading.com Research: My Key Takeaways

Trading.com provides a solid mix of research resources to support traders of all experience levels. Users can access a continuous stream of high-quality news and analysis from both the in-house team and trusted third-party sources like Reuters, Analyzzer, and Trading Central. A major plus is that this content is easily accessible on both the website and the WebTrader platform. Trading.com also sets itself apart with unique tools like investor sentiment, adding extra insight for decision-making.

Education

Trading.com provides a well-structured suite of educational materials, most useful for beginner and intermediate traders. The content includes step-by-step tutorials in both text and video formats, as well as platform walkthroughs, making it accessible and practical for those new to trading or seeking to solidify foundational knowledge. I rate the education offering as better than average for the industry.

Trading.com offers a comprehensive library of written tutorials to aid trader development. The Beginner section explains basic terms like pips, spreads, and long/short trading.

As traders move on to the intermediate section, they are introduced to the concepts of leverage, risk management, and trading psychology.

Finally, the advanced section explains technical and fundamental analysis, including how to read chart patterns and interpret economic indicators. The bite-sized lessons are easy to consume, and I liked the recap at the end to help reinforce key concepts.

For those who prefer visual learning, Trading.com also provides concise 2-3 minute video tutorials that cover the same essential trading concepts as the written guides.

Platform Walkthroughs

Brief video walkthroughs guide users through the WebTrader platform and mobile app, demonstrating how to place trades, use charting tools, and set up indicators. This is particularly helpful for new users getting acquainted with the interface.

Glossary and Tools

A comprehensive glossary defines over 600 trading terms, and a forex calculator assists users in practical aspects of trading, such as calculating margin, swap fees, and pip value quickly and easily.

While Trading.comâs educational resources are strong for beginners and intermediate traders, advanced materials are somewhat limited. For example, it would be great to see the inclusion of more sophisticated trading strategies and coverage of automated trading. The education offering could also be further enhanced by introducing live webinars and interactive Q&A sessions for real-time engagement.

The Bottom Line

Trading.com earned a high trust rating in my review, despite being a relatively new broker in the industry. It holds licenses from top-tier regulators in the US, UK, EU, and Australia. Unlike many global forex brokers, Trading.com does not operate any offshore entities. Its website reflects a strong commitment to transparency, with a clean layout and clear information on account features, fees, and regulatory oversight.

In the US, Trading.com focuses solely on forex trading, offering a solid lineup of 69 currency pairs. This selection is competitive and suitable for both beginners and seasoned traders. However, the range of instruments could be improved by adding another asset class, like cryptocurrencies. During my tests, spreads were average, leaving room to do better in this area.

A standout feature is Trading.comâs proprietary WebTrader platform. It features a sleek, minimalist design and an intuitive interface. Tools like Trading Central signals, investor sentiment data, and Reuters news feed enhance the experience and support informed decision-making. For experienced clients, MetaTrader 5 is also available, offering powerful charting capabilities, algorithmic trading, and extensive technical analysis tools.

Trading.com US maintains its commitment to simplicity with a single account type and a low minimum deposit, making it easy for new users to get started. Backed by strong regulation, transparent practices, and powerful platforms, Trading.com is a compelling option for American forex traders seeking an innovative, well-rounded broker.

Trading.com was established in 2019 and expanded into the US retail forex market in 2022. The New York-based broker has a strong global presence with entities licensed by multiple regulators, including top-tier NFA and CFTC. Trading.com is a part of the Trading Point Group, the same parent company behind the well-known brand XM.

US clients can trade 69 forex pairs using Trading.comâs WebTrader platform, mobile app, or MetaTrader 5. While forex spreads are generally in line with industry norms, the platform stands out with a better-than-average suite of trading tools, including trading signals from Trading Central, sentiment data, and a Reuters news feed.

With a focus on simplicity and fast, transparent access to the forex market, Trading.com US is a good fit for beginners and casual traders. My tests showed that the broker can also accommodate more experienced day traders and algo traders, thanks to its advanced platforms.

TSG Brokers Regulators

In our reviews, we examine the regulatory status of each entity operated by a broker. This allows us to compare the different levels of client protection. We rank regulators using a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing reflects the highest level of regulation.

Here are my findings on TSG Brokers:

  • TSG Brokers Ltd is licensed and regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) under license number 291/16. We rate CySEC as a Tier-1 regulator.

How TSG Brokers Protects You

Brokers often operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

â Segregation of client funds. TSG Brokers Ltd keeps client funds in fully segregated bank accounts, separate from the brokerâs own operating capital. This structure helps reduce the risk of accounting errors and ensures that client money remains protected.

â Negative balance protection. TSG Brokers Ltd provides negative balance protection, ensuring that traders cannot lose more than the funds deposited in their accounts. This safeguard is particularly important during periods of high market volatility, as it prevents losses from exceeding your account balance.

â Compensation scheme. Clients of TSG Brokers Ltd are protected by the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF) up to â¬20,000, providing an additional layer of protection in the event the firm is unable to meet its financial obligations.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors related to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

TSG Brokers is a new broker, but its foundations are solid. Launched in 2025 and headquartered in Nicosia, Cyprus, it operates within a clear European regulatory framework and is structured to meet modern compliance and client-protection standards.

Transparency is one of TSGâs stronger points. During my review, I found clear and accessible disclosures covering the companyâs regulatory status, legal entity, trading conditions, and client protections. While its operating history is still short, TSG Brokers offers a well-regulated, well-documented setup that inspires confidence.

Is TSG Brokers Safe to Trade With?

To summarize, my findings indicate that TSG Brokers can be regarded as having a relatively high level of trust and stability due to the following factors:

  • Founded in 2025, reflecting a limited operating history
  • Regulated by a Tier-1 authority (CySEC) under the EU regulatory framework
  • Segregated client funds, negative balance protection, and investor compensation coverage up to â¬20,000
  • Clear disclosure of legal, regulatory, and trading information

Fees

My test showed that TSG Brokers has transparent and competitive pricing. I recorded tight spreads across almost all instruments I tested, while some costs were industry-average. However, overnight fees exceeded the benchmark during my test. I concluded that TSGâs fee structure was geared toward active trading rather than long-term holding. The broker charges an account maintenance and dormancy fee after 12 months of inactivity.

TSG Brokers charges a one-off administration fee of â¬25 when a customerâs trading account remains inactive for 12 months. An inactivity fee of â¬10 will also be deducted from the client account on the last day of the 12 months of inactivity.

Are TSG Brokersâ Fees Competitive?

I rate TSG Brokers as highly competitive if you trade actively and donât hold positions for long. TSG Brokersâ ultra-tight spreads across forex, indices, and crypto are consistently better than industry averages, making it a strong pick for day traders, scalpers, and systematic strategies.

A trade-off comes with overnight holding: swap rates are on the high side, and positive carry isnât passed on, which makes the platform less appealing for long-term or carry-focused traders.

Platforms and Tools

TSG Brokers offers a streamlined platform lineup that covers the needs of most retail traders without unnecessary complexity. You can trade through the browser-based TSG Trade Web platform, a full-featured mobile app, or MetaTrader 5 for more advanced and automated strategies.

TSG Trade Web Platform

The TSG Trade Web platform is a clean, browser-based interface designed for traders who want fast access to markets without installing software. Navigation is intuitive, with clearly separated sections for charts, order entry, portfolio tracking, and performance analytics.

During my testing, the platform loaded quickly, charts were responsive, and basic workflows like placing trades, modifying orders, and monitoring positions were easy to execute.

General Ease of Use

The interface of the TSG platform is uncluttered and beginner-friendly. Core tools are accessible within one or two clicks, and the learning curve is noticeably lower than on more complex professional platforms.

Key Features

The standout features of the TSG Trade Web platform include:

  • Intuitive Charts: Integrated charting with decent technical depth for a web-based platform.
  • Alerts: Traders can set alerts for trade execution events and receive reminders for EU, US, and Asian market opens and closes. Notifications are delivered via email, SMS, and push notifications.
  • Watchlists: Custom watchlists allow you to track favorite instruments across forex, indices, commodities, stocks, and crypto in one place.
  • Direct Hedging: Traders can open opposing positions on the same instrument to manage short-term risk or implement strategy-based hedging.
  • Language Support: Available in 8 languages: Arabic, English, French, German, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, and Spanish.
  • Trading Journal: Built-in performance analytics help traders review and refine their strategies.
  • Portfolio Tracking: Clear visualization of exposure and profit and loss across different markets.

Charts

The TSG Trade Web platform offers solid charting tools suitable for technical analysis:

  • 24 technical indicators covering trend, momentum, oscillators, and volatility
  • 4 chart types: candlestick, mountain, line, and bar
  • 9 timeframes ranging from 1 minute to 1 month
  • 14 drawing tools, including Fibonacci retracements, trendlines, and pitchforks

Charts are responsive and easy to customize, though power users may still prefer MT5 for deeper indicator libraries and automation.

Orders

TSG Trade supports all essential order types, including market, limit, and stop-loss orders. Order tickets are straightforward and clearly laid out, making trade execution fluid.

Portfolio

The portfolio section illustrates your open positions by market and displays real-time profit and loss. This makes it easy to assess exposure at a glance and adjust risk as market conditions change.

Trading Journal

The integrated trading journal provides detailed performance insights, including drawdown, profit factor, win rate, total P&L, number of trades, trade allocation, and profit by market. Itâs a useful built-in tool for traders who want to review results without exporting data to third-party software.

TSG Trade Web Platform: My Key Takeaways

After using the TSG Trade Web platform daily for over a week, it stood out as a well-balanced, execution-focused trading environment. Compared with other broker web platforms Iâve tested, TSGâs offering is a no-frills entry-level solution.

It is less customizable than professional terminals like MT5 and lacks popular features such as 1-click trading, trading from the chart, and advanced order types. Still, I rate TSG Trade as a reliable, intuitive platform best suited for beginners and casual traders.

TSG Trade Mobile App

The TSG Trade Mobile App closely mirrors the web platform, featuring a modern design and smooth navigation optimized for smaller screens. The charting interface is easy to use, and core functions like placing trades, managing positions, and checking account details are well organized.

General Ease of Use

The app is intuitive and beginner-friendly, with logical menus and fast access to key trading functions.

Charts

The TSG app includes dependable charting for on-the-go trading:

  • 26 indicators covering directional movement, momentum, oscillators, volatility, and volume
  • 4 chart types: candlestick, mountain, line, and bar

TSG Trade Mobile App: My Key Takeaways

The mobile app feels polished and reliable, with biometric login adding a layer of convenience and security. You can deposit and withdraw funds directly in the app, making it practical for traders who prefer to handle everything on mobile. While advanced traders will still gravitate toward MT5, the app is suitable for active monitoring, discretionary trading, and risk management on the go.

Execution Speed

My tests in MetaTrader 5 showed relatively fast execution speeds of 55 milliseconds.

TSG Brokers Order Execution Model

TSG Brokers uses an STP execution model, routing trades to third-party venues rather than internalizing orders, with price, total cost, and execution speed prioritized under MiFID II rules.

Tradable Instruments

TSG Brokers provides over 300 CFDs covering forex, indices, commodities, shares, and crypto. The range of assets allows traders to execute popular strategies, including trend, breakout, and event-driven trading within a flexible risk-on/risk-off framework. What are CFDs?

A Contract for Difference (CFD) is an agreement specifying that the buyer must pay the seller the difference between an assetâs current value and its value at the time the contract was initiated. Like futures and other derivative financial instruments, CFDs allow traders to speculate on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

TSG Brokers offers customer support Monday to Friday, 9:00â18:00, via email and phone. During my test, live chat wasnât available, but email responses were prompt, and phone support was easy to reach. I received helpful answers, and the agents were knowledgeable and direct.

TSG Brokers Customer Support Test

Support is a key component of a brokerâs offering, whether you are a new trader looking for guidance on how to use the platform or an experienced trader who needs help fast to exit their positions in the event of a technical glitch.

Over a two-week test period, TSGâs support proved reliable and consistent. I asked a mix of basic questions about fees and more detailed ones about platforms, tools, and regulation, and each was handled clearly and efficiently. Overall, I had a positive impression of the quality of TSG support.

However, its working hours are limited when compared to many brokers that offer 24/7 help. Plus, adding live chat would be a great advantage for faster resolution of basic inquiries.

The structure is clear: lower-tier accounts prioritize accessibility, while higher tiers unlock tighter pricing, raw spreads, and higher leverage for qualifying traders. What is CFD Leverage?

Leverage allows traders to control larger positions with less capital. For retail clients, TSG Brokers caps leverage at 1:30, meaning a â¬1,000 balance can control up to â¬30,000 in market exposure. Leverage varies by asset class, reflecting their differing risk profiles. It can magnify gains, but it also increases losses, so risk management is essential.

Research

In the research section, TSG Brokers offers an in-depth 2026 forex market report, an economic calendar, and a listing of top stories from TradingView on the website homepage. The broker lacks regular in-house market analysis and third-party analytical tools.

TSG Brokers offers an in-depth report titled âForex Market Overview 2026: Statistics and Realistic Profit Expectations.â The research helps everyday traders understand loss rates, the realities of small accounts, and why discipline and structure matter.

You can also access an economic calendar on the TSGâs website. It surfaces the weekâs real risk drivers, from global events like Davos to high-impact CPI, labor, and central-bank releases.

The broker has also published an economic calendar tutorial, which explains how to use macro data, correlations, and event timing to manage hidden risk and plan trades around high-impact news.

On the homepage of the website, you can find a listing of the top news stories from TradingView, covering forex, indices, crypto, commodities, and equity markets.

TSG Brokers Research: My Key Takeaways

While TSG Brokers offers fast STP execution and competitive spreads in normal conditions, its research content is limited to a market news widget powered by TradingView. TSG does not publish any other research content like regular market analysis, which is important for timing and contextualizing high-impact releases.

Education

TSGâs educational materials are basic but well-structured. There are two introductory courses that cover forex fundamentals, platform use, and risk awareness. The broker could do better by adding more written and video content, as well as live learning events such as webinars.

TSGâs educational materials are built around two introductory modules that emphasize core forex concepts, risk awareness, and practical platform use. The first module explains how the forex market works, covering currency pairs, pips, leverage, and volatility in clear, accessible terms.

The second module shifts to execution, offering step-by-step guidance on MT5 across desktop and web, account setup, charting, indicators, and order management, with a strong focus on workflow and discipline. Each module ends with a short quiz to reinforce key points. While the content is intentionally basic, it provides a well-structured foundation for traders who want to understand the market and tools before trading live.

The blog section of the TSG Brokers website contains a selection of interesting guides. For example, the report on the âBenefits of Trading with an STP Brokerâ highlights faster, automated order routing, market-driven pricing, and fewer conflicts of interest, helping traders understand why execution quality and liquidity matter.

The TSG Brokers YouTube channel offers a small selection of short videos on using the TSG trading platform. Theyâre quick, straightforward, and best suited for new users who want a basic walkthrough.

The Bottom Line

TSG Brokers is an execution focused CFD broker built for active traders rather than investors. Regulated by CySEC, it offers strong client protections, a transparent website and legal documents, and a clean regulatory setup despite its relatively short operating history.

Fees are competitive where it matters most for short-term trading, with ultra-low spreads and fast STP execution, though higher swap costs make it less appealing for long-term positions. Platform options are well-balanced, combining the user-friendly TSG Trade platform with MetaTrader 5 for advanced and automated strategies.

While the low trading costs impressed me, I noted that the broker could do better in several key areas. At the top of my wish list would be expanding customer support to include live chat and broadening the analysis materials.

Overall, TSG Brokers is best suited for day traders, scalpers, and algorithmic traders who value execution quality, essential tools, and a professional trading environment over extensive research libraries or long-term investing features.

Our Take on TSG Brokers

TSG Brokers is a multi-asset CFD broker launched in 2025 and headquartered in Nicosia, Cyprus. Clients can access over 300 CFD instruments across forex, equities, indices, commodities, and cryptocurrencies.

The broker offers the TSG Trade Web platform, with an intuitive layout and innovative features like a built-in Trading Journal. You can also use the TSG Trade mobile app while on the go and MetaTrader 5 if you prefer a more advanced setup.

Fees are a notable advantage of TSG. The broker keeps the spreads low across all popular assets Iâve tested. I was especially impressed by the rock-bottom pricing on EUR/USD, Germany 40, and Bitcoin.

TSG Brokers is regulated by the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC), providing EU-level client protections, including segregated funds and negative balance protection for retail clients. It operates independently but is backed by the same ownership group as the prop trading firm The5ers.

There is room for improvement in some areas. The broker lacks live chat support, and research and educational materials are still relatively narrow.

Overall, I rate TSG Brokers as a strong option for traders seeking access to popular CFD markets with low trading costs and reliable execution.

Vantage Swaps

A swap fee is the cost of keeping a trade open overnight, and itâs tied to the difference in interest rates between the two currencies in a pair. If youâre holding a buy (long) position, you may either pay or earn interest depending on the ratesâthis is called a swap long. The same applies to a sell (short) position, where the overnight charge or credit is called a swap short.

The values listed below are for one full base currency contract (100,000 units).

EURUSD Charge of $8.07 Credit of $3.94
GBPJPY Credit of $6.62 Charge of $24.96

I concluded that the brokerâs swap fees sit in the middle ground across all instruments I tested. So you can consider Vantage for overnight trading, but remember that swap rates always change.

Vantage Non-Trading Fees

Vantage does not charge any non-trading fees, including an inactivity fee. Deposits and withdrawals are also cost-free*.

Are Vantageâs Fees Competitive?

I found Vantageâs fees to be highly competitive. In my tests, spreads on most instruments came in below the industry benchmark, while swap rates were closer to the market average. On top of that, Vantage doesnât charge non-trading fees*, which adds to its appeal as a low-cost broker overall.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

For this review, I tested MetaTrader 5 (MT5), the popular platform among retail traders seeking more traditional setups and high functionality. It supports basic technical analysis, easy order execution, and automated trading. MT5 also boasts a simplified interface, making it easy to navigate.

What I like most about MT5 is how well it adapts to different trading styles and experience levels. Itâs suitable for basic technical analysis, placing trading orders, and copy trading. MT5 is also loaded with multiple integrated how-to articles and videos, helping users learn how to use the software.

For more experienced traders, MT5 offers a Depth of Market (DOM) tool and Expert Advisors (EAs) for algorithmic trading. The platform also features a strategy tester tool, helping algo traders perfect their systems.

On the downside, MT5âs charting capabilities are outmatched by more modern trading stations, such as cTrader and TradingView. In my opinion, its chart visuals are outdated and appear somewhat rugged.

Availability & Features

The MT5 platform by Vantage is available for Linux, Windows, and macOS users and supports 39 languages, including English, Spanish, German, Arabic, and Chinese.

MT5 features include:

  • Price Alerts: Set alerts when an instrument hits a specific price â ideal for spotting trade entry opportunities.
  • Customizable Watchlists: Keep tabs on your favorite instruments with ease.
  • One-Click Trading: Enter trades instantly at market price â perfect for scalpers or fast-paced traders.
  • Chart Trading: Place and manage orders directly from the chart, including entry points, volume, stop-loss, and take-profit levels.

Charting & Analysis Tools

MT5 is packed with many analytical tools, including:

  • 38 built-in technical indicators: From trend-following to oscillators and volume-based tools.
  • 24 drawing tools: Including Fibonacci retracements, Elliott Waves, and more for technical pattern spotting.
  • 21 timeframes: Great for multi-timeframe analysis â one of the largest offerings in the industry.
  • 3 chart types: Line, bar, and candlestick options let traders view price action in their preferred format.

That said, MT5âs charts can get cluttered quite easily, especially when applying more than one technical indicator or drawing tool. Price action becomes obscured and difficult to interpret. Overall, MT5âs charts are not ideal for traders accustomed to streamlined and easily scalable setups.

Order Types

MT5 offers three execution modes and covers all the core order types needed by most traders:

  • Market Orders: Instant execution at the best available price â ideal for quick entries.
  • Limit Orders: Target a specific price level for entry, though execution isnât guaranteed.
  • Stop Orders: Protect open positions with predefined risk levels. Stop-loss orders automatically convert into market orders once triggered.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

I consider MetaTrader 5 (MT5) a solid choice for traders from all backgrounds â from first-time traders to seasoned professionals. The platform is packed with multiple valuable tools and can be used for conducting basic technical analysis, copy trading, one-click trading, and automated trading.

My main gripe with MT5 is its rugged, somewhat inflexible look. Charts can feel a bit clunky, and zooming in or out isnât always smooth, which can make it harder for technical traders to spot clean entry points.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android and keeps most of the functionality of the desktop version, making it easy to stay connected to the markets on the go. Itâs especially useful for opening, closing, and adjusting trades quickly.

You can place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as manage position size and risk levels directly from the app. That said, the charting experience still feels a bit cramped, and price action can be hard to scale and analyze comfortably on a small screen.

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money, allowing them to open larger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Research

There is plenty to like about Vantageâs research offering: from its frequent news updates to its in-depth market analyses. You can use the content to learn about the latest financial news, such as the FOMCâs policy decisions, and identify new trading opportunities. Vantage also publishes insightful podcast episodes. All materials are presented in a clear and easy-to-understand format.

Economic Calendar

The economic calendar is a fundamental research tool that informs traders of upcoming economic releases and financial news that could move the market and create viable trading opportunities.

Market News and Analysis

This section serves as a practical resource for daily monitoring. It features a live news screener that tracks global economic shifts, providing a steady stream of data that can help identify the catalysts behind specific price movements.

From a traderâs perspective, the value lies in the depth of the content. Rather than just skimming the surface of major headlines, Vantage offers technical breakdowns and fundamental commentary that explore the mechanics of high-impact economic releases.

Market Sentiment

Vantageâs client sentiment tool offers a direct window into the positioning of other traders within the platformâs ecosystem. By aggregating real-time data on the ratio of long versus short positions across major currency pairs, indices, and commodities, it provides a âcrowd-sourcedâ perspective on market direction.

For a strategic trader, this data is most valuable when used as a contrarian indicator or a confirmation tool. Seeing that 80% of retail clients are net-long on a pair thatâs hitting a major resistance level can be a powerful signal of a potential reversal or an âovercrowdedâ trade. While no single metric should dictate a position, having access to this internal sentiment helps bridge the gap between abstract price action and the actual human psychology driving the current trend.

Technical Analysis

Powered by TradingView, Vantageâs Technical Analysis gauge shows how traders are leaning across key markets like forex, indices, commodities, share CFDs, and crypto. Itâs a quick snapshot of the current market mood and helps highlight the prevailing sentiment.

The Vantage View

In collaboration with Bloomberg Media Studios, Vantage has also launched its own video series on YouTube and Spotify, where it breaks down major macro shifts and growing themes like Space Economy, AI, and ESG.

What I like about it is the âbig pictureâ angle. With Bloomberg-level production and expert commentary, it feels less like daily market noise and more like a longer-term roadmap, helping you connect macro megatrends to the assets that eventually start moving on your charts.

Trump Tariffs

The âTrump Tariffsâ segment is quite innovative and very helpful for navigating the unpredictability of global geopolitics. This is a place where you can stay up-to-date on the latest news related to the trade war between the US and China, as well as President Trumpâs foreign tariff policy, and their broader impact on global markets.

Daily Financial News

Vantage also publishes video breakdowns of current news on its YouTube channel. The content provides a hands-off approach to staying informed.

Vantage Research: My Key Takeaways

It sets the standard. In my opinion, Vantage offers one of the most complete research packages in the industry. It covers the market from every angle, delivering top-notch news, deep analysis, and actionable trading signals. I found the variety impressive, ranging from standard sentiment gauges to more unconventional materials like the Vantage podcast seriesâa feature few competitors offer.

It works for every level. Despite its depth, the content never feels overwhelming. It is presented in a clear, easy-to-understand format that works just as well for a total beginner as it does for a seasoned veteran.

Education

Vantage provides a rich and diverse collection of educational materials, including articles, videos, regular webinars, platform tutorials, courses, and e-books. Traders have a comprehensive 360-degree coverage of essential trading terms and concepts â from technical and fundamental analysis to the psychology of trading.

Articles

Traders have access to over 350 educational articles on Vantage Academy. They cover a wide range of topics, including technical analysis, forex trading, commodity trading, and more.

Vantageâs educational articles

Courses

If youâre just getting into trading, Vantageâs beginner courses are a solid place to start. There are four dedicated tracks (Forex, Stocks, Indices, and Gold), and together they offer a structured, step-by-step learning path with over 600 minutes of content, all geared specifically toward new traders.

Vantageâs educational courses

Webinars

Vantage runs weekly webinars and uploads the recordings to its YouTube channel, where there are over 200 videos available right now. Itâs a great way to pick up new skills and stay engaged with different aspects of trading without having to learn everything on your own.

One thing I genuinely liked is that Vantage highlights the speakers upfront. Their profiles are shown on the webinar sign-up page, and most of them are experienced market professionals, which adds a nice layer of credibility to the whole series.

e-Books

Vantage has published a variety of eBooks that delve even deeper into the subject matter. The eBooks are geared towards trading enthusiasts who want to absorb every minor detail.

Terminology

The Terminology section of Vantageâs Academy provides an encyclopedic breakdown of key trading terms and concepts, including their definitions and functions.

Platform Tutorials

If you want to learn more about MetaTrader 5, you can watch video lessons that explain how to use the platform and maximize its benefits. There are also tutorials dedicated to the copy trading service.

The Bottom Line

After testing Vantage, Iâd rate it as one of the most well-rounded brokers in the industry, especially for active traders who care about tight pricing, powerful platforms, and strong market intel. A lot of brokers do one or two things really well, but Vantage covers more boxes than most. The lineup of platforms includes MT4/MT5, TradingView, its own Web Trading, and the Vantage App. Plus, it gives access to a free VPS and a copy trading service.

What really impressed me is how much Vantage puts into research and education. The broker doesnât just throw a basic news feed at you. It delivers frequent market updates, technical and fundamental analysis, sentiment tools, and actionable signals. On the educational front, thereâs a lot of depth too: hundreds of articles, structured beginner courses, e-books, and weekly webinars. Itâs the kind of setup that works whether youâre learning the ropes or sharpening your edge.

Pricing was also a big win in my testing. Spreads were competitive across most markets, and on BTCUSD, crude oil, gold, and major indices, Vantage came in better than the industry average. Swaps were mostly in the middle range, so holding overnight trades is still realistic, and the lack of inactivity fees or internal deposit/withdrawal charges* makes it even more cost-friendly.

That said, itâs not flawless. Iâd love to see faster customer support during peak hours, and the forex spreads could be more competitive considering how strong pricing is elsewhere.

Final verdict: Vantage is a top-tier choice for traders who want an âeverything in one placeâ broker with great costs and tools. If youâre into day trading, scalping, news trading, crypto, or automation, itâs easily one of the better options on the market.

Risk Warning: Trading derivatives carries high risks. General advice only. Please refer to Vantageâs risk disclosure statement before trading.

Our Take on Vantage

Vantage is one of the most well-rounded brokers Iâve tested, combining competitive fees, strong client protection, a broad range of products, and an excellent overall trading environment. Founded in 2009, the broker has built a solid reputation over time, and my live tests confirmed that its pricing is especially sharp in areas like crypto, commodities, and major indices.

Platform-wise, Vantage delivers one of the strongest lineups in the market. It offers its own Web Trading platform and Vantage App, alongside TradingView and the full MetaTrader suite. The main downside I found was customer support, which can be sluggish during peak hours. Still, compared to the broader market, Vantage stands out as a premium all-in-one broker that checks almost every box for serious retail traders.

Versus Trade Regulations

In our reviews, we examine the licenses and regulations of each entity operated by a broker, allowing us to compare their different levels of protection. We rank licenses by various regulatory bodies on a three-tier system, where Tier-1 licensing indicates the highest level of regulation.

This is what I discovered about the single entity operating under the Versus Trade trade name:

  • Versus Trade Ltd is a registered company in Saint Lucia with reference number 2024-00586. The entity is also licensed and regulated in Mauritius by the Financial Services Commission (FSC). We rate the FSC as a Tier-3 regulator.

Understanding the Regulatory Protections of Your Account

Brokers operate multiple entities globally, but regulatory protections vary. Some regulators enforce stricter financial standards than others, so traders should understand the safety measures of the entity with which they choose to open an account.

Here is what you need to be looking for in a broker in terms of safety mechanisms:

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. Versus Trade keeps client funds in segregated accounts.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. Versus Trade guarantees negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects traders against the brokerâs liabilities if the company becomes insolvent. Versus Trade does not participate in a compensation scheme.
  • Maximum Leverage: Capping the maximum leverage restricts the extent of market exposure to retail traders. The higher the leverage, the higher the potential profits and potential losses. The maximum retail leverage with Versus Trade is 1:2000.

Stability and Transparency

In our Trust category assessments, we evaluate factors tied to stability and transparency, including the brokerâs longevity, company size, and information transparency.

Founded in 2024, Versus Trade is a newcomer to the trading industry. According to its LinkedIn page, the company employs up to 50 people.

I reviewed Versus Tradeâs Client Agreement and found that everything was in order. My only gripe is that no live spread data is displayed on the brokerâs website. Overall, I assess the brokerâs transparency level as pretty decent.

Is Versus Trade Safe to Trade With?

I concluded that Versus Trade is sufficiently safe to trade with because:

  • Keeps client funds in segregated accounts
  • Ensures negative balance protection
  • Has transparent legal documents

Fees

Versus Trade offers commission-based trading, with spreads that are generally on the lower end, often beating the industry average. Unlike many competitors, Versus Trade does not charge swap fees on popular instruments, making its pricing even more competitive. To top it off, the broker imposes no handling fees on deposits or withdrawals, and no inactivity fees on dormant accounts.

I assessed that Versus Tradeâs fees are highly competitive. Its spreads outperform the industry average, and most instruments are available for swap-free trading. Additionally, the broker supports commission-free trading on its Standard account.

Traders also benefit from the absence of non-trading charges. Deposits and withdrawals incur no handling fees, and dormant accounts are not subject to inactivity fees.

Platforms and Tools

Versus Trade offers the renowned MetaTrader 5 platform, available for desktop, web, and mobile trading. MT5 is a fitting choice for traders with different backgrounds and experience levels. However, its layout may seem outdated compared to newer trading platforms.

MetaTrader 5 Desktop

I tested the desktop version of MetaTrader 5, one of the most popular platforms among retail traders. The charts, orders, and various instruments are located in easy-to-find places, and even first-time traders can quickly learn their way around. My only gripe with the platform is that its charts feel rugged and outdated compared to newer and sleeker trading software.

Versus Tradeâs MT5 platform is available on Windows and Mac and supports 39 languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Arabic, Chinese, and more.

MT5 features include:

  • Alerts-Setting Option: Traders can set alerts for when the price of a given instrument falls/rises to a predetermined level, which could potentially signal a viable entry opportunity.
  • Watchlist Customization: Traders can populate watchlists with their favorite instruments and track market changes more easily.
  • One-click Trading: This feature enables instant market entries at the spot price and is invaluable for high-precision traders, such as scalpers.
  • Trading from the Chart: Traders can place conventional trading orders directly from the chart, specifying the entry price, volume level, stop and take-profit levels, and more.

In my opinion, MT5 is best suited for automated trading, which is available via Expert Advisors (EAs). The platform also has an intuitive strategy tester, allowing experienced algo traders to tweak the parameters of their strategies so that they can be used under different market conditions.

Charts

As shown above, MetaTraderâs charts can quickly become cluttered, even with just two indicators. This can obscure price action examination and make it harder to perform detailed technical analysis.

I have broken down the available analytical tools and chart configurations below:

  • 38 technical indicators: Including trend-based and volume-based indicators, and oscillators to analyze price action and assess market sentiment, helping predict market movements.
  • 24 drawing tools: Tools like Fibonacci retracement levels and Elliott waves help identify price patterns, support/resistance levels, and breakout points. However, MT5âs design can make price action harder to interpret.
  • 21 timeframes: For multi-timeframe analysis, enabling detailed price action analysis.
  • 3 chart types: Price action can be displayed as line, bars, or candlesticks, offering diverse perspectives on trading opportunities.

The chart screen is undeniably one of the most crucial features of a trading platform. It equips traders with essential tools and configurations to analyze price action and spot trading opportunities. Just as important is the ability to easily scale price action, allowing for a clearer and more detailed view of market movements.

Orders

MetaTrader 5 features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which supports immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the MetaTrader 5 platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries, but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and triggers the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

MT5 Desktop: My Key Takeaways

MetaTrader 5 is a good option for fast and simple order execution. However, its dated and rugged design is inferior to newer and sleeker platforms. As a trader who prioritizes flexible charts that are easily scalable, I find MT5âs charting capabilities too rigid and less effective.

MT5 App

The MT5 mobile app is available on iOS and Android, enabling quick and easy access to the market on the go. It is very useful for opening, terminating, and adjusting open positions.

You can also use the app to place market, limit, and stop orders, as well as to adjust the exposure of your open trades.

What Are CFDs?

Contracts for difference (CFDs) are derivatives that speculate on the underlying assetâs price without physical ownership.

For example, a long position on gold would generate profit as the price rises or incur a loss as it falls, all without the need to purchase actual gold bars.

One of the biggest advantages of trading CFDs is that traders can get in and out of the market almost instantaneously, thereby catching even minute changes in the price of the derivative.

Orders

MetaTrader 5 features three types of order execution: market, pending, and one-click trading, which supports immediate entries at the spot price.

I have broken down the available order types on the MetaTrader 5 platform below:

  • Market Orders: Used for immediate entry at the best available price. They guarantee volume filling, though the entry price may differ from the requested price.
  • Limit Orders: Guarantee exact price entries, but wonât be filled if the price doesnât reach the trigger level.
  • Stop Orders: They are used to support open positions by limiting the maximum loss that can be incurred if the market turns in the opposite direction. A stop-loss order is placed at a fixed price below or above the spot price. If the market does indeed turn and trigger the stop-loss, it will transform into a market order and get filled at the best possible price.

Leverage determines a traderâs overall market exposure. When trading Contracts for Difference (CFDs), positions can be opened for a fraction of their value because of leverage. Essentially, the broker lends the trader money so that they can open bigger positions. Leverage multiplies the profits a trader generates from winning positions, but also the losses incurred from failed trades.

Education
VT Markets provides a decent flow of webinars and educational videos, covering a wide variety of trading topics. However, the broker lacks written content like articles, guides, and e-books.

I found over 20 educational videos and past webinars on the brokerâs YouTube channel. VT Markets tends to focus on broader topics, such as Why Traders Should Embrace Market Swings, but also dives into more advanced areas like building a trading plan and understanding the role of trading psychology. However, it falls short on beginner-friendly basicsâthereâs little content on essentials like reading price action or using stop-loss orders.

The Bottom Line

VT Markets comes across as a well-rounded and highly competitive broker that can hold its own against the best in the industry. It delivers an impressive package, with a wider range of instruments than most competitors, especially in forex, indices, and cryptocurrencies.

The razor-sharp spreads on indices, stock CFDs, and Bitcoin are a highlight. The platform lineup â MT4, MT5, TradingView, and proprietary apps â covers the needs of casual traders, strategy-driven swing traders, and even algorithmic and copy traders. Combined with in-depth research from Trading Central and the brokerâs own market insights, the offering feels robust and well thought out.

That said, there are areas where VT Markets could improve. Its educational resources lack the depth and variety needed for complete beginner support, and certain withdrawal methods come with extra fees. While the broker is not regulated by a top-tier authority, it still maintains strong client protection measures.

In the end, VT Markets is a great fit for active traders looking for low spreads on select markets, a deep instrument pool, and a choice of advanced platforms. It may not be the first pick for someone seeking a full beginner-friendly learning hub, but for traders who already have some experience and want a broker that can support a wide range of strategies, itâs an excellent option.

How XM Protects You

Brokers operate multiple entities to serve clients globally, yet regulatory protections vary by jurisdiction. Some regulators enforce strict financial standards, while others are more lenient. Traders should understand the protection offered by the entity where they intend to open an account.

  • Segregation of Client Funds: Keeping client funds in segregated bank accounts from the ones used for the brokerâs corporate capital negates the risk of accounting errors. All of XMâs entities ensure this.
  • Negative Balance Protection: This safety mechanism removes the risk of trading losses exceeding the account balance. In other words, the losses you incur from trading are capped at the amount you have put in your trading account. This is especially important in volatile markets. All XM entities provide negative balance protection.
  • Compensation Scheme: A compensation scheme protects retail traders against the brokerâs liabilities in the unlikely event that the company becomes insolvent. Only clients of Trading Point of Financial Instruments Ltd (EU-based entity) are insured up to 20,000 EUR by the Investor Compensation Fund (ICF).
  • Secure Socket Layer (SSL): XM uses advanced SSL encryption to safeguard clientsâ personal and financial information. This technology ensures that all data transmitted between the client and the platform remains protected, private, and inaccessible to unauthorized parties.
  • Secure Payment Methods: XM offers a wide range of trusted, security-focused payment options, each thoroughly vetted to meet strict protection standards and ensure safe, reliable transactions for clients.

Stability and Transparency

In our tests for the Trust category, we also cover factors relating to stability and transparency. Here, we focus on the brokerâs operating history, size, and overall credibility.

Founded in 2009, XM has established itself as a highly experienced CFD broker with a long-standing track record in the industry. According to the broker, it has over 1,000 employees worldwide, underscoring its status as a large and well-resourced brokerage. XM is a part of Trading Point Group, which also owns Trading.com.

With over 15 million clients across more than 190 countries, XM is one of the worldâs largest brokers, processing nearly 14 million trades daily.

XM also demonstrates transparency in its regulatory profile, prominently listing its licenses in the website footer and on a dedicated Regulation page. The brokerâs Help Center addresses questions on fees, while more detailed terms are available in the Client Agreement, found under the Legal Documents section.

Is XM Safe to Trade With?

In summary, my findings indicate that XM can be regarded as having a moderate to high level of trust and stability due to the following factors:

  • 15-year operating history
  • All entities are regulated
  • All entities segregate funds
  • All entities offer negative balance protection

The only drawback of XM is that all entities (except the EU-based Trading Point of Financial Instruments Ltd) lack a compensation scheme in the event of broker insolvency.

XM Order Execution Model

XM uses the B-Book, or âMarket Maker,â model, in which the broker takes the opposite side of your trades. In this setup, your orders are filled directly by XM, with the broker buying when you sell and selling when you buy. XM takes all reasonable steps to deal on the terms that are the best available (best execution).

Like futures and other derivative financial instruments, CFDs allow traders to speculate on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

I was impressed by the breadth of XMâs tradable instruments. Thematic indices such as LATAM Giants and Trump Winners add unique depth, while turbo stocks provide traders with enhanced leverage on shares. Crypto traders, in particular, benefit from a remarkably wide selection of 60 pairs.

Customer Support

XM offers round-the-clock customer support through live chat, phone, and email. After testing the service with dozens of inquiries, I came away with a very positive impression. The live chat in particular stood out as fast, reliable, and highly convenient.

When you open an account with XM, you are assigned a dedicated Client Relations Manager who provides personalised support from the start. This representative becomes your main point of contact for key account matters, helping ensure a smooth trading experience.

XMâs customer support also stands out for its broad multilingual coverage, offering assistance in more than 30 languages. Support is available in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Thai, Malay, Hindi, Vietnamese, Russian, Chinese, and many other languages.

XM Customer Support Test

Support is a key component of a brokerâs offering â whether you are a new trader looking for guidance on how to use the platform or an experienced trader who needs help fast to exit their positions in the event of a technical glitch.

Over a two-week test period, XMâs 24/7 customer support consistently impressed me. Live chat agents replied in under a minute every time, while email responses were also prompt. My questions ranged from simple fee inquiries to more complex issues regarding platforms, tools, and regulations. In every case, the support team provided clear, helpful answers, making the overall experience smooth.
Deposit and Withdrawal

XM makes funding and withdrawals straightforward with multiple options, including bank transfers, credit/debit cards, digital wallets, and crypto. Processing times are faster than the industry average, with withdrawals instantly handled through XMâs AI-powered system. Both deposits and withdrawals are largely free of charge*. Overall, XM excels in this area, delivering an above-average service.

What is CFD Leverage?

One of the reasons that traders are attracted to the forex and CFD markets is the high degree of available leverage. Leverage is the use of borrowed funds to increase the size of your trading positions beyond what would be possible using only the cash in your account.

For the XM Global Limited entity, the maximum leverage is 1:1000. This means that with an account of $1,000, you can control up to $1,000,000 worth of positions in the market. This is an unusually high level of leverage and very risky to use.

Leverage is often described as a âdouble-edged swordâ as it can hurt you as much as it helps you. Traders should keep in mind that it can amplify both their profits and their losses.

Research

XM offers an excellent selection of research resources, including daily market analysis from its experienced in-house team, third-party insights from Trading Central, and a Reuters news feed directly integrated into the web platform. XM delivers a consistent flow of research through its web platform, which is available in both text and video formats. The commentary spans a wide range of assets, with an emphasis on forex and commodities. Covering both technical and fundamental themes in detail, it offers valuable insights for traders of all experience levels.

Trading Central is available through the web platform and provides actionable insights and trade ideas. The third-party research tool enhances decision-making with technical analysis, forecasts, and strategy suggestions for forex, commodities, indices, and stocks.

The XM web platform also integrates a Reuters news feed, giving traders direct access to trusted, real-time financial news. Covering global markets, economics, and key events, the feed helps users stay informed and react quickly to market-moving developments.

XM supports fundamental analysts with an interactive economic calendar that displays upcoming news events by region, expected impact, and release time. The calendar includes consensus forecasts, actual results, and links to charts of affected instruments.

Traders can also use the platformâs market sentiment tools to gauge how positioning is distributed across the market, which can support both contrarian and confirmation-based strategies.

XM Research: My Key Takeaways

I was impressed by XMâs well-rounded suite of research tools, combining in-house market analysis, third-party insights from Trading Central, and real-time financial updates from Reuters. Together, these resources provide traders with a powerful range of technical and fundamental insights without leaving the platform.

Education

XM offers a robust educational suite featuring daily multilingual webinars, structured video lessons led by Avramis Despotis, and interactive Live Education rooms. Covering fundamentals, strategies, psychology, and real-time market analysis, these resources provide accessible, professional-level training that equips traders with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.

XM offers an extensive webinar program that runs seven days a week, led by a team of 77 expert instructors. The free, interactive sessions bring professional-level knowledge directly to traders in an accessible format. Available in 23 languages, the webinars cover a broad range of themes, including actionable trading strategies and live trading sessions. All materials are conveniently available on the XM web platform and mobile app.

Traders can access a comprehensive educational course powered by Tradepedia. Led by founder Avramis Despotis, the program spans eight modules that progress from trading fundamentals to advanced topics such as trading psychology and strategies.

Within each module, lessons are delivered in concise video format, typically under 10 minutes, covering focused themes like news trading and Elliott Wave theory. The course is rich in valuable content and provides new traders with a solid foundation for taking on the markets.

XMâs Live Education is an interactive way for traders to sharpen their skills, with daily sessions covering technical, fundamental, and market-specific themes. Highlights include the Forex Power Hour, where experts provide real-time analysis on currency pairs. The US Market Open Hour is focused on stock and index opportunities as news breaks. Traders can also deepen their technical edge in the Indicators Masterclass or gain context on macroeconomic events in Letâs Talk Fundamentals. Together, these live rooms offer practical, hands-on learning.

XM also offers a podcast series for traders who prefer learning on the go, with episodes covering market recaps, weekly trading themes, macroeconomic developments, and central bank updates, as well as trading psychology. The podcast is available both through the client area and on major podcast platforms, making it easy to stay informed during a commute, workout, or any moment away from the screen.

The Bottom Line

XM Group is a long-established company with over 15 years of experience and multiple entities regulated worldwide. Client funds are segregated, and negative balance protection is standard, but compensation coverage is limited outside the EU.

The broker offers more than 1,400 instruments across forex, commodities, indices, shares, and crypto. Unique products like thematic indices and turbo stocks add depth. Traders can choose between XMâs proprietary web platform and mobile app or the popular MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5. The extensive built-in features of the XM web platform and mobile app really make it stand out from the crowd.

Fees are mixed. Standard Account spreads are relatively high, while the Ultra Low account provides tighter spreads and swap-free options on selected instruments. Non-trading fees are minimal, with only a $10 inactivity charge. Deposits and withdrawals are free and fast, although crypto funding is not yet available. Free VPS hosting is offered to clients who meet balance and trading volume requirements.

I rate XM as a strong choice for beginners, casual traders, swing traders, and day traders. Scalpers and long-term investors may find some limitations, such as the absence of raw-spread accounts or investment products like exchange-traded ETFs and bonds. Overall, with its excellent education, research, and customer support, XM delivers a well-rounded and robust trading experience.

The company is also publicly traded on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, reflecting its transparency and financial stability. As of April 2025, its market capitalization has grown to 8.8 billion PLN (approximately 2.3 billion USD), further solidifying its position as one of the most stable and trustworthy forex and CFD brokers.
